Sports.title: Desire Doue forced off with gruesome tooth injury
Sports.content:
Desire Doue's tooth got dislodged after a nasty tangle during France's Nations League defeat against Italy.

The French international received an elbow in the face by Davide Frattesi that dislodged his tooth.

2 It was a very unfortunate incident, but it left Doue in a world of pain Credit: Getty

It was a total accident, but the blow did serious damage to his teeth, and the forward was immediately taken off.

It happened towards the end of the game, with Senny Maylu of Paris Saint-Germain replaced him.

The PSG star indicated that he required medical attention that he received on the field before Zinedine Zidane took him off.

Story of the game

Italy dealt out a first defeat to Zidane as France manager as the Azzurri moved top of their Nations League.

It takes who wins the group to the final game with just a point separating Belgium, France and Italy.

Things started very well for Les Bleus as well as Michael Olise opened the scoring on ten minutes after a costly error by Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the scores were levelled 16 minutes later as Francesco Pio Esposito continued his great form for Inter Milan with the equaliser.

And in the second half, the 2006 world champions ran away with the match.

Esposito scored from the penalty spot before Frattesi bagged three minutes later to put the game beyond France.

And after the game, Zidane said: "When we were struggling, we didn’t manage to react within the framework of the game plan that we put in place.

2 It's another painful night for Zidane against Italy Credit: AFP

"We did it at 0-0 or at 1-0, but as soon as they took the lead, we were in disarray, notably defensively. We won’t be worried. It is a part of football.

"It is better that these kinds of moments come now. It wasn’t a ‘non-match’ tonight, but there is something to improve upon.”

There was no Kylian Mbappe for Les Bleus, but he could be back to face Turkey on Sunday.

They have been the whipping boys of the group losing every match so far.

France know if they win that, they stand a very good chance of topping the group.

On Mbappe's fitness, Zidane said: "Yes, yes, I hope so! [he will be available to face Turkey].

"That's why he stayed with us in the camp... I don't think it's anything serious.

"The idea is to get him back on the pitch.”

Sports.title: Championship striker working as financial adviser alongside £12.5k-a-week football career
Sports.content:
Charlton striker Matty Godden is ready for life after football.

The Addicks ace confirmed on social media he is now a fully qualified financial planner.

2 Godden is already embarking on a career outside of football Credit: Getty

"Football taught me how quickly things can change, and how much it matters to plan ahead," Godden wrote.

"Now I help people to just that, whether you're a professional sportsperson, a family planning for the future, or a business owner looking to make the most of what you've built."

Godden added he has received a 'great response' from potential clients.

The 35-year-old's Instagram account also includes a link to the website of Investments and Pensions, where he has a profile.

Why is Matty Godden a financial adviser?

Godden qualified as a financial adviser in June and shared his certificate on LinkedIn.

When posting his achievement, Godden stated it was a 'big passion' of his to pass on experiences to 'up and coming players on how to manage their money' in their careers.

Godden's venture comes as the striker ticks towards the end of his contract at Charlton.

He is set to become a free agent at the end of the season, although Charlton have the option to extend his deal, which nets him £12,500 a week, until 2028.

How has Matty Godden played in 2026/27?

Godden has featured just four times for the Addicks this term.

The striker started and scored in Charlton's 3-1 win over Cheltenham Town in their Carabao Cup first round clash.

2 Godden has 26 goals in 64 appearances for Charlton since he joined in July 2024 Credit: Getty

He retained his spot in the line-up for the Addicks' Championship opener against Derby County, which ended in a 2-1 win for Nathan Jones' side.

Godden then picked up an injury that kept him out for two months before he made his return off the bench in a 1-0 loss to Bolton.

But the veteran striker proved he still has plenty left to give when he came off the bench to score the winner in Charlton's 2-1 win over Sheffield United last Saturday.

Godden's 79th-minute strike snapped an 11-game winless run for Charlton and moved them seven points clear of the relegation zone.

The 35-year-old will look to continue dragging Charlton further away from danger when they return to action on November 21 away to fourth-placed Wolves.

Sports.title: 2/10 Jarell Quansah leaves talkSPORT host dumbfounded as four England players get 3/10 on stale night
Sports.content:
2/10 Jarell Quansah leaves talkSPORT host dumbfounded as four England players get 3/10 on stale night

Harry Kane celebrated his record England outing with the match-winner in Thursday's 2-1 win over Croatia in the Nations League.

The 33-year-old brought up his 126th outing on the international stage - moving one clear of fellow Three Lions icon Peter Shilton.

5 No player has scored more than Kane's seven strikes in the Nations League this season Credit: Getty

And he marked the special occasion with his record-extending 92nd goal to bring his tally to seven in the competition - finding the back of the net in each of the five Group A3 matches.

It took 24 minutes for England to make the deadlock with Morgan Rogers' close-range strike deflecting off Josko Gvardiol.

A brilliant cross-field ball from Kane found Jude Bellingham by the back post, whose first-time volley somehow ended up at Rogers' feet after Gvardiol failed to clear the danger, with the Chelsea star making no mistake from a few yards out.

But a calamitous mistake from Jarell Quansah allowed Petar Sucic to equalise just before the hour mark after the Bayer Leverkusen defender's attempted headed back pass was pounced upon by the Inter Milan midfielder.

Just three minutes later and Quansah was once again in the thick of it, with VAR intervening to give England a penalty after he was hauled to the ground by Hrvoje Smolcic.

Up stepped Kane who made no mistake by calmly firing down the middle of his goal for his 27th spot-kick for England.

England held on for the victory - a month after their 7-0 win over Slaven Bilic's side in Rijeka.

And it's now four Nations League wins in a row for Thomas Tuchel's men ahead of Sunday's trip to leaders Spain - live on talkSPORT.

Sitting three points behind Spain the table with one game left, victory in Madrid will ensure they sit atop of the group.

Here is how legendary talkSPORT Adrian Durham rated and slated England's stars from the Home of Football...

5 Rogers' impressive start to the season continued as he registered his third Three Lions goal Credit: Getty

5 Kane's penalty proved the difference at Wembley on Thursday night Credit: Getty

Adrian Durham's full-time reaction "That was not convincing in any way. "And on a school night - and a chilly school night at that - these fans have come out and expect better. "Listen, these are different times for England. "You expect them to play well especially in front of a big Wembley crowd. "They got the win and that's the most positive thing you can say about tonight, but in no way was that convincing. "Where do we start with all of that? Bearing in mind they went to Croatia and we were there when they won 7-0. "You didn't expect it to be that straightforward again, obviously Croatia were going to be coming here and putting up far more of a fight. "They had some pride To show as well, and they did, they did put up more of a fight, they started very well in the game. "But at times England made it so easy for them, that defending was pretty terrible at times."

Candy Kane

Ever the man for the big occasion, Kane stepped up - quite literally - when his side needed him the most.

It was Kane's stunning pass that led to England's opener, before he sealed the hosts all three points from 12 yards.

In a game that was dominated by pre-match headlines of Kane set to become the country's all-time record appearance maker, the Bayern Munich marksman showed why he scooped the Ballon d'Or award.

Awarded a 6/10 by Durham, only Elliot Anderson [7/10] was given a higher rating than the Bayern Munich marksman.

Durham said of the ex-Tottenham centre-forward: "Big night for the main man.

"Got the winner and a terrific pass for the first goal."

Moment of madness

Quansah can have Kane to thank for bailing him out after suffering from a total lack of judgement.

A Croatia corner was whipped in, with Gvardiol's touch making it's way to Quansah inside the box.

And instead of attempting to clear the ball, he instead underhit a header back towards Jordan Pickford - giving Sucic a near open goal.

Though he did somewhat redeem himself after winning England a penalty, before making a crucial sliding challenge to deny Ante Budimir in the closing stages.

But that tackle wasn't enough for his mistake to be overlooked by Durham, who gave him a 2/10 - the lowest rating of any England player.

He simply said of the Bayer Leverkusen defender: "What was he doing for the equaliser?"

5 Quansah won't be making that mistake again... Credit: Getty

Left wanting Mor

It's been a stunning start to the season for the winger, who has eight goals for club and country [six for Chelsea, two for England].

Bringing up his third goal for England - and his second against Croatia after scoring in last month's win - the 24-year-old is arguably in the best form of his career.

But for Durham, he believed the former Aston Villa man flattered to deceive after breaking the deadlock.

It was for that reason that Rogers was given a 4/10 - the same rating as Anthony Gordon - who started on the opposite flank.

Durham simply stated: "Scored, then disappeared."

Sports.title: Jack Grealish issues apology as he makes comeback from ban in behind-closed-doors game
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish issues apology as he makes comeback from ban in behind-closed-doors game

Jack Grealish has apologised to Everton and its supporters after a spell out of the team due to disciplinary issues.

Grealish missed the Toffees' last four fixtures due to a 'breach of club discipline', a decision backed by manager David Moyes.

2 Grealish's season hasn't quite gone to plan Credit: Getty

The 31-year-old made his return to action in a behind-closed-doors match against Derby County, which Everton won 4-1.

And the star forward is hopeful it will be the start of a run of games following his off-field indiscretions.

What did Jack Grealish say about his suspension?

"Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training," Grealish wrote.

"I want to apologise to the fans n (sic) everyone at the club for not been (sic) able to help the team the last few weeks.

"I love playing for this club n (sic) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon."

Grealish's first opportunity to return for Everton in a competitive setting is on November 23 when the Toffees travel to Brentford, with kick-off set for 8pm.

Worryinfly, Grealish is yet to register a goal or an assist from six competitive appearances for the Toffees this term.

Given he is into the final year of his deal at Manchester City, Grealish will need to increase his goal contributions if he is to remain at Everton.

How Jack Grealish can recapture his best form

One figure who believes Grealish can still turn things around is former Republic of Ireland international Andy Townsend, although he knows the road back won't be an easy one for the mercurial forward.

"If you're not one of those boys that rocks up in the morning, you're in great nick from the day before, then you're not going to survive, certainly not in the Premier League," Townsend said.

2 Grealish will become a free agent at the end of the season Credit: Getty

"So Jack has got to make a decision (on) what he really wants to do, where he really wants to be and I think find something a little bit more in his game.

"A few years ago he had that one season in the treble-winning team where he was truly outstanding there.

"Give it to Jack and he'll hang onto it and he'll make something happen for us.

"That's disappeared lately. I hope he gets it back."

Grealish has 29 goals and 27 assists in 216 Premier League appearances for Villa, City and Everton.

He also boasts 39 England caps, but has not represented the Three Lions since October 2024.

Sports.title: ‘Few problems’ – Key Chelsea star sparks new concern amid injury-hit season
Sports.content:
Chelsea star Moises Caicedo has sparked fears of an injury after admitting he is 'having a few problems'.

Caicedo, who is away on international duty with Ecuador, spent a number of weeks on the sidelines earlier this season with a calf injury.



2 Caicedo has dealt with his share of injury issues this season Credit: Getty

The midfielder has since started the Blues' last six fixtures in all competitions, but his latest comments will provide cause for concern at Stamford Bridge.

What did Moises Caicedo say about his fitness?

"I'm a little... Fine, a bit tired, having a few problems, but well, I'm here," Caicedo said.

"Honestly, my national team is what matters most to me, being here with my people, with my Ecuador.



"I'm making a huge effort to be here, and I'm very happy about that."

Ecuador face Costa Rica first in the international break on November 13 and then play Bolivia four days later.

La Tri are hoping to pick up their first win since the 2-1 victory over Germany in the group stage of this year's World Cup.



Since then, Ecuador were knocked out in the round of 32 by co-hosts Mexico and failed to beat South Korea, Japan and Panama in the last international break.

Caicedo did not feature in any of Ecuador's last three fixtures.

What is Moises Caicedo's injury record?

The 25-year-old was absent from Chelsea's training earlier last week but was passed fit and went on to play the full 90 minutes in the Blues' 1-0 loss to Sunderland on Sunday.



Caicedo's injury issues this term represent a significant difference from last season.

2 Alonso will need Caicedo fully fit once the international break ends Credit: Getty

The midfielder missed just four league games in the 2025/26 campaign, with those absences down to red and yellow card suspensions.

In fact, Caicedo has largely had a spotless injury record since he joined Chelsea from Brighton in August 2023 for £115million.



Prior to this season, the midfielder had missed only two games through injury and illness.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso will hope Caicedo returns to west London unharmed from the international break ahead of a run of fixtures.

Alonso's side return to action on November 21 against ninth-placed Leeds.

Fixtures against Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace follow before a bumper stretch of three games against Liverpool, Manchester City and Aston Villa.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s A-list TV show begins filming at Premier League club
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has confirmed production of his new TV series has begun.

The show, titled 'Day 1s', focuses on a fictional football agent played by Emmy and Golden Globe winner Damian Lewis.



2 Ronaldo may be about to embark on an acting journey Credit: Getty

Also among the cast is British rapper Dave, who had a role in the smash series 'Top Boy'.

Ronaldo shared a snap of the two in a scene to his Instagram along with the caption: "Exciting news! Production of my first TV show, Day 1s, has just started. More to come!"

Another picture from Ronaldo shows a scene in the Brentford dressing room.



Ronaldo, who will act as an executive producer, is also set to play himself in the series, as will Thierry Henry.

The show is one of the first big projects to come from UR Marv Studios, a production company Ronaldo co-founded with renowned director and producer Matthew Vaughn.



What else has Cristiano Ronaldo invested in?

Ronaldo's announcement of his latest venture comes shortly after he invested around £16million into building a water bottling plant in Portugal.

The facility is being built in the small village of Gostei, located in northern Portugal.



It is hoped the site will be complete by the end of 2027.

Ronaldo also hasn't been afraid to invest in more football-related areas, either.

The 41-year-old acquired a 25 per cent stake in Spanish second tier outfit Almeria in February.

2 The 41-year-old has an eye on his post-playing career Credit: AFP

“For a long time, my ambition has been to contribute to football beyond the pitch,” Ronaldo said.



“UD Almería have strong foundations and clear growth potential. I look forward to working with the leadership team to support the club’s next phase.”

Although Ronaldo's various investments demonstrates he has an eye towards the future, the 41-year-old is still an active footballer.

Ronaldo remains a vital figure at Saudi club Al Nassr, who sit third in the Saudi Pro League this term.

However, Ronaldo's international career came to a close when he announced his retirement on November 5.



Ronaldo's retirement came after he had a public fallout with Portugal boss Jorge Jesus, with a disagreement over playing time believed to be a key part of the friction.

Sports.title: Manchester United told to raid Premier League with four-man transfer list including ‘genius’
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer. Jarrad Branthwaite. Antonio Silva. Ferdi Kadioglu.

Those are the four Premier League stars that talkSPORT host Andy Goldstein has urged Manchester United to sign in 2027 if they wish to return to former glory.

5 Mauricio Pochettino is leaving his role as USA's head coach to take charge of United Credit: Getty

A worst ever start to a Premier League season has the Red Devils fighting relegation as they languish in 18th spot having won just once of their opening ten fixtures.

Their horror form led to the sacking of Michael Carrick on Thursday, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to be whisked in during the international break.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has less than two months before he is able to dip into the transfer market to bolster the squad.

Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson, who has been coached by Pochettino during their time together with the USA national team, is one mooted target.

But United fan Goldstein has other ideas over who his beloved side should sign - with the broadcaster dreaming about an audacious swoop for Chelsea's Palmer.

Palmer, who is tied down at Stamford Bridge until 2034, is known to have been a boyhood United fan and idolised club legend Wayne Rooney in his youth.

Speaking on Drive, Goldstein ran through his four-man list of top priorities, with Palmer the first he'd go for in a move that would reunite him with ex-Blues manager Pochettino.

Who have Man United been urged to sign?

He said: "The top of that list and the reason why I would let Bruno [Fernandes] go [next summer]... I don't think he's playing his best football anymore at this club and I know he's a Man United fan, Cole Palmer.

"I would love to see Cole Palmer at Manchester United, I've always been a big fan, I think he's a genius, I've used that word before.

"I think some of his touches and his vision has been sublime, I think he's fantastic, and also, he was with him of course when he was at Chelsea, so there's that little connection.

5 Palmer has chipped in with three goals and as many assists from ten games for Chelsea this term Credit: Getty

"I'm a huge fan of Cole Palmer, he'd be number one of my shopping this."

Goldstein then reeled off three defenders to complete his wish list, which included centre-backs Branthwaite [Everton] and Silva [Bournemouth], along with Brighton left-back Kadioglu.

He continued: "I'll go for Branthwaite. Obviously we need defender, we've been linked to him a few times and he's been sort of on the fringes with England a few times, been in the squad, but I'm a big fan of his.

"I think there's a lot more to come, I know Everton fans will be screaming at the radio, but he'd certainly be my shopping list.

"Another one from Brighton, I think he can play either side actually, Kadioglu, I just think when you look at Man United's options, Luke Shaw's always getting injured - although last season he played every single league game."

Goldstein then finished off by highlighting Silva, who has impressed since joining from Benfica in a £26million deal in August.

5 Branthwaite has featured in nine of Everton's opening ten Premier League games Credit: Getty

5 Kadioglu has helped Brighton reach second spot in the table Credit: Getty

5 Silva has been ever-present for Bournemouth since swapping Portugal for England Credit: Getty

He stated: "The other one is I've gone for Antonio Silva at Bournemouth, they're producing some really good players."

It wasn't just potential incomings that Goldstein discussed, having also named five players he wants sold in the New Year.

Failing to hold back, he insisted that United should already be looking to offload midfielders Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos - despite the pair joining in £35m and £50m deals respectively in the summer.

He simply remarked: "I won't dwell on the five, I'll give the five I think should go: [Diogo] Dalot, [Mason] Mount, [Harry] Maguire, Santos and Tielemans."

Sports.title: US Soccer dream of Pep Guardiola appointment with ex-Premier League boss on shortlist
Sports.content:
US Soccer dream of Pep Guardiola appointment with ex-Premier League boss on shortlist

US Soccer want Pep Guardiola to replace Mauricio Pochettino as the men's national team head coach, talkSPORT understands.

Pochettino looks set to leave for Premier League giants Manchester United having agreed a deal in principle to replace Michael Carrick.

2 Guardiola could be on his way back into management as the United States eye a replacement for Pochettino Credit: AFP

Those overseeing the managerial change in the United States set-up want to hire Guardiola in what would be a dream appointment.

The Spaniard has been out of management since the summer when he left Manchester City after a decade at the club.

Guardiola won six Premier League titles and the Champions League, and is regarded as one of the best managers in history.

He also lifted three consecutive league trophies with Barcelona and Bayern Munich.

talkSPORT also understands former Premier League manager Roberto Martinez is on US Soccer's shortlist over potential replacements for Pochettino.

Martinez has experience managing internationally having managed Belgium as well as Portugal, whom he left following their World Cup exit in the summer.

But Guardiola is the one US Soccer really desire and it would represent his first dalliance into international football as a manager should be appointed.

However, it won't be as straightforward for the powers that be as he hinted before his City exit that he would take a break from football.

Could Guardiola join USMNT?

"After my contract with City, I'm going to stop. I'm sure," he said in May 2025.

"I don't know if I'm going to retire, but I'm going to take a break. How I want to be remembered, I don't know."

2 Guardiola is one of the most successful managers in history and would be a remarkable appointment for the United States Credit: Getty

In a separate interview, he reiterated: "So I'm not retiring, but I will take a break, for sure."

"When I finish here, I will take a break. I need to make a stop, that's all," Guardiola added.

Despite leaving the club, Guardiola has maintained support for City in recent months.

He sent an emotional message to fans after City were found guilty on all charges of Premier League financial breaches in September.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all," the 55-year-old said.

Guardiola then attended their Champions League league phase clash at home to holders Paris Saint-Germain last month.

However, he watched his former side lose 4-2 in what was their worst home defeat in the competition ever.

Should Guardiola take the USMNT job, he could be on the touchline in time for the Gold Cup next summer.

Sports.title: Inside Boreham Wood, the only unbeaten team in England's top seven tiers: Boss LUKE GARRARD explains how play-off heartache and a 'genius' owner are fuelling his swashbuckling side's promotion bid
Sports.content:
Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.

Boreham Wood are on their own crusade. And the Holy Grail is a long-coveted place in the EFL for the runaway leaders of the National League. They have 44 points from 16 games with 44 goals and are 12 points clear ahead of a trip to Yeovil on Saturday, finding success with a distinct passing style.

In a remarkable 4-3 comeback win against Hartlepool earlier this month, Luke Garrard's team made 1,022 passes, beating the Premier League record of 1,015 set by Manchester City against Swansea in April 2018.

The electric start to this campaign is, according to Garrard, fuelled by the lingering pain of defeat in the play-off final at Wembley in May when they conceded an equaliser in the seventh minute of stoppage time and lost on penalties.

'That broke me mentally for four or five days,' the Wood boss tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I reflected hugely and had a long, hard look at myself because I could not walk back for the first day of pre-season without the energy and heart for the job.

'I spoke to the owners and the staff about the first meeting I wanted to have when we came back in. It involved everyone at the club, and it was a message to tell all of them that as much as it hurt us, we needed to use the hurt as our fuel and our driving force.

'We got quite lucky getting some results on the board quite quickly and that builds momentum and belief.'

National League leaders Boreham Wood, under the guidance of their manager Luke Garrard, are the last unbeaten team in the top seven tiers of English football

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500. They share Meadow Park with Arsenal Women and Arsenal Under 21s and U18s

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500 by chairman Danny Hunter and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director and in charge of recruitment strategy. They are punching above their weight with a mid-table budget.

Hunter senior is a former props master in the film industry who worked at the nearby Elstree Studios among others, and whose father Mickey was a double promotion winning manager of club in the 1970s.

He took control in 1999 and has overseen investment of more than £14million and the rise from the depths of the Isthmian League to the brink of the EFL, forging effective relationships with local authorities and Premier League neighbours Arsenal, who use Meadow Park for their Women, Under-21 and Under-18 teams.

Arsenal ad boards surround an immaculate pitch, and work is underway at the venue on a £4m project to create a covered South Stand terrace incorporating improved 'Fan Zone' style facilities for away fans and a new first-team building.

Garrard's team train in the mornings on the artificial pitches beside the stadium, which are available for community use in the evenings and home in the afternoons to the club's academy.

Manchester City's Iliman Ndiaye and Hull's Sorba Thomas were both nurtured as young players at Boreham Wood. So was Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024 and sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5m in August.

The Abdulmalik fee shattered the non-League record set when Fleetwood Town sold Jamie Vardy to Leicester in 2012.

There was an untidy episode towards the end of the transfer window when Abdulmalik went public to plead for a move, but the Hunters secured an enviable price for their star and in another example of their good housekeeping have yet to reinvest the money in the team. It is still there as a war chest as they target promotion.

Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024, was sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5million in August

The club is run by chairman Danny Hunter (pictured) and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director. Hunter Snr is a former props master in the film industry

The windfall from Wood's famous FA Cup run in 2021-22 was invested into refitting the interiors of the ground including the dressing rooms and swish hospitality areas recognised among the best in non-League.

Meadow Park has a bar bedecked with souvenirs from those games and named in honour of Mark Ricketts, scorer of the goal to beat Bournemouth, who were at the time bound for promotion to the Premier League, and which clinched a date with Everton in the fifth round at Goodison Park.

'At no stage has the chairman given me any pressure to generate money from prize funds and cup runs,' says 41-year-old Garrard. 'It's only ever been about creating moments and memories.

'He (Hunter) is a Boreham Wood boy through and through and it's always been his greatest wish to lead the club into the EFL. He wants to leave a legacy. I adore him, I think he's a genius. We have a great working relationship. I do not take for granted the luxury of being manager here, especially after losing my job two years ago.'

Garrard has a long association with the club. First as a player, briefly in 2005 and then returning for a second spell four years later, a loan move from Wimbledon which became permanent and led him into his first coaching roles and the manager's job.

He took control in 2015 with the Wood in the top tier of non-League for the first time. Three times they reached the play-offs without promotion and there were many highs including Goodison before Garrard's tearful exit after relegation in April 2024, only for him to be back in charge by September.

During five months away, he turned down interest from one club because it took him too far from his family home and received two direct and sobering rejections from National League clubs. Feedback from the first told him he 'wasn't on the list and never would be' and from the second that he 'wasn't good enough' for them.

Perhaps it reveals some of football's inherent petty-mindedness towards Boreham Wood. They are perceived by some as upstarts with limited history and small crowds, putting the noses of 'bigger' clubs out of joint with the streamlined success of their business model and Hunter's backing, like a non-League version of Bournemouth or Brentford.

They have been known to charge scouts for tickets and charge away teams to broadcast, which some refuse to do on a point of principle. For a time, they had a reputation for pragmatic and unattractive football – but not any longer.

Garrard was rejected by two National League clubs and found himself back at Boreham Wood. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it

Prolific striker Matt Rush has is fuelling Boreham Wood's promotion push

Garrard was probably entitled to have expected more interest in his services. Instead, he spent two days following the second of those rejections in earnest conversation with his wife about the need to look for work away from football when out of the blue came a call from Boreham Wood.

Within another two days he was back in his old job. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it. 'It was the best team in the National South with the best players, the best facilities and the best budget. I had to go and deliver.'

And he did. With promotion back to the National League at the first attempt. Then the near-miss heartache of Wembley. Now this early-season surge thanks in part to the goals of striker Matt Rush. The Wood seem to have emerged stronger despite selling their most talented individual, which is a reassuring situation for any coach.

Unbeaten since April in the National League, they scored 25 goals in seven games in October and League One Wigan became the first team to beat them in any competition this season, in the FA Cup first round on Saturday.

It could yet prove a blessing in Boreham Wood's quest for the Holy Grail.

Sports.title: Revealed: The RFU's seismic plans to overhaul Twickenham - from the longest bar in the world, a roof garden and Tunnel Club to Taylor Swift and finally fixing the trains... and the bitter battle holding it all up
Sports.content:
The grand old home of English rugby is no longer fit for purpose. As the spotlight falls on Twickenham – or the Allianz Stadium as it is known these days – for this run of Nations Championship matches, it is clear that it needs to move out of the 1990s if it wants to survive.

The brutalist architecture is showing its age. Bar the redeveloped East Stand, it looks like a concrete relic – especially when compared to modern football venues like Tottenham’s shiny, new billion-pound venue on the other side of town.

The nine-to-one ratio of men’s to women’s toilets is archaic, and tackling the transport chaos, particularly around Twickenham's paltry train station, can be more painful than a hit from Ellis Genge.

Three years ago, the RFU board got together and posed the question: ‘If we had a blank cheque, what would we do to the stadium and how much would it cost?’ Their proposals came out at £660million – a figure that has since been subjected to 36 months of inflation.

Some of the longer-term, headline-grabbing plans include Tunnel Club hospitality, a roof garden on the West Stand and a 65-metre bar that would challenge Tottenham’s claim to boasting the longest stadium bar in the world.

There are proposals for a ‘sporting line’ train service that links nearby Hounslow and the rest of the UK – converting the West London Orbital freight train line that runs towards Wembley into a passenger service.

How the revamp of Twickenham's West Stand could take shape

England rugby fans flock to Twickenham but travel to and from the stadium is a nightmare and its brutalist architecture is showing its age

But the more immediate plans would could come into play next summer. Among other things, they intend to improve the toilet ratio to seven-to-three and to introduce bathroom mirrors to the stadium.

Creating a more environmentally friendly arena is another target. There are plans to replace the generators which guzzle 70,000 litres of diesel per year with a cleaner form of energy. There is also an ambition for the pitch irrigation system, which uses 1.4million litres of water, to use no mains water at all, just rain water from the stadium's underground reservoir.

Populous, the architecture giants behind Tottenham’s stadium, are already engaged. But unlike the Premier League side, the RFU are not propped up by the deep pockets of billionaire owners. They are a not-for-profit organisation whose money goes back into the sport. The stadium sits empty for 340 days a year and does not generate enough revenue to secure a bank loan to fund its modernisation masterplan.

But finding a solution that keeps England’s beloved home of rugby in Twickenham is essential.

Hosting other sports is one way of generating extra income. The RFU have a licence to host as many sporting events as they desire. The NFL already have a tie-up with Wembley and Tottenham, but there is a possibility of staging popular college football games, as Wembley did for the first time in September when the Kansas Jayhawks played the Arizona State Sun Devils.

There is not enough floorspace to install a running track for athletics and there would be objections from residents to a groundshare with local football clubs such as Chelsea, should they need somewhere else to play while redevelopment of their own stadium takes place.

Around 85 per cent of the RFU’s revenue comes through Twickenham ticket sales, hospitality and sponsorship, making the stadium its most valuable asset. Events are the biggest driver of revenue but the licence currently limits them to hosting just three major non-sporting events per year. In comparison, Wembley and Tottenham have permission to stage 54 and 30 respectively.

An upcoming council vote holds the key to Twickenham’s future. The RFU have asked for their licence to be increased to 15 non-sporting events per year. The licence would be phased over a three-year period, increasing from six to 12 to 15, and contingent on stringent reviews.

There is not enough floorspace to install a running track for athletics and there would be objections from residents to a groundshare with local football clubs such as Chelsea

Wembley opened the door to more college football games being played in the UK, with the visit of the Arizona State Sun Devils and the Kansas Jayhawks in September's 'Union Jack Classic'

Major acts could generate up to £500,000 per show for the RFU, through stadium hire fees and food and drinks sales. Music promoters Live Nation, who represent Harry Styles and Taylor Swift, are already engaged with the RFU and would have the pick of the market in 2028, when most of London’s football stadiums will be in use for the European Football Championship.

Naturally, there has been some resistance from local residents. Richmond councillor Alexander Ehmann, of the Liberal Democrats, has been the most vocal critic of the proposals.

‘There are very real ways this will affect residents’ lives,’ Ehmann tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘The act selection will be important. We had Eminem in 2018 and there was drug-taking and all sorts. If you have Metallica, you get a different crowd to Taylor Swift.

‘People plan their lives around matchday activity. They know what’s coming. They hunker down and accept it. When you have midweek concerts, that’s different. They set up and then you have the deconstruction the next day. Twickenham Stadium is the home of rugby. It’s not Twickenham Mega Bowl. It's not the home of Beyonce.

‘Do the residents want to see the RFU successful and vibrant? Yes. Do they want the stadium successful and vibrant? Yes. This isn't born of a “we want them out” narrative.

'There is a really strong recognition of the contribution that rugby plays to Twickenham's identity and its economic activity. There’s also a recognition that Twickenham Stadium almost certainly needs to modernise and provide a better matchday experience to be able to compete.

‘But the RFU have been asleep. They’ve woken up and decided they need to intensify use, but for years they've not been studiously and diligently working away to ensure they have the infrastructure.

Around 85 per cent of the RFU’s revenue comes through Twickenham ticket sales, hospitality and sponsorship, making the stadium its most valuable asset

'We have a commuter station being used as the major artery for matchday activity. It just about holds water. It just about works but when something goes wrong, the whole thing is chaos. It's kaput.

‘This is chickens coming home to roost. I've been a councillor since 2014 and the RFU have been a pretty slow-paced, not very ambitious, not very deeply ingrained participant in the community.

'What you need is capacity-enhancing transport infrastructure. Something like fighting the case for an extension of the Underground line from Richmond to Twickenham. I know that's highly ambitious but that stance would tell residents that the RFU get the challenge.

'The RFU want to generate multi-millions through intensification of their stadium, but they want to do it without effectively committing a bean to underlying infrastructure. They want everybody else to pay for their payday, which I think is quite a challenging proposition.’

Extending the Underground's District Line to Twickenham would, however, be almost impossible. Instead, the RFU believe they can make better use of the other surrounding stations. They want Hounslow East station to become a de facto Twickenham Parkway to help ease the flow after events.

‘There’s very little signage to take you to the stations other than Twickenham,’ says one source. ‘Richmond is under-utilised. The big prize is Hounslow East. It’s on the Piccadilly Line and it runs 24-7.

'It’s a 20-minute walk away but less than one per cent of supporters use it. The RFU needs planning permission to put signs up, such as near the exits saying, “30-minute queue at Twickenham, good service on the Piccadilly Line”. Everyone knows Twickenham station is maxed out. Sending alerts midway through the second half of games or towards the end of concerts about transport options could be a step forward.

‘On top of that, proposals for the West London Orbital would be a game-changer. It’s been approved for funding. It’s scheduled to go from Hounslow to north of Wembley. It would link up to an interchange at Old Oak Common, which would connect to the Elizabeth Line, rail services out to the West Country and eventually HS2. The timing for that is early 2030s. It’s a really easy project because there’s a freight line that can be turned into a passenger line without too much investment.’

Hounslow East, on the Piccadilly Line, is only a 20-minute walk from Twickenham but fewer than one per cent of fans use it on a matchday

Ehmann also made an argument for the RFU working more closely with PREM club Harlequins, who have their own smaller stadium, The Stoop, a few hundred metres away.

‘If you look at this holistically, is there not merit for a single sporting stadium that had enough flexibility to host smaller capacity Harlequins games?' he says. 'It’s strange to have a significant rugby stadium next to a gigantic international rugby stadium, completely independent, pursuing their own growth and investment sort of strategies. Harlequins need to be brought to the table.’

The RFU would be open to discussions, although Harlequins would not be able to fill out Twickenham on a fortnightly basis. Given the value of the club’s real estate footprint, however, it is an interesting idea.

In the business of sports stadiums, Twickenham is regarded as one of the better-staffed venues. There were zero community complaints after England’s thumping victory over Australia last Sunday – although that may be a different story on a Friday or Saturday night.

They close roads on matchdays and employ 160 stewards for each event. The RFU proudly claim to provide more operations outside its stadium footprint on matchdays than any other stadium in the UK. It is understood they have also offered to provide stewards for a pathway to provide a counterflow for residents.

The shape of Twickenham’s future will be tabled for a debate later this year. An RFU spokesperson said: ‘Additional concerts at the Allianz Stadium will generate vital funding to improve the stadium and strengthen community rugby clubs nationwide.

‘The proposals submitted to Richmond Council would bring more world-class entertainment to Twickenham, as well as providing significant employment and economic opportunities for our local community.

‘Any increase in the number of events would take place through a careful, phased approach, with progression dependent on demonstrating to local stakeholders that the impacts are being effectively managed.

'Plan A, B, C, D and all the way to Y is to stay in Twickenham,’ says one source. ‘But it’s a common-sense business approach to have a back-up plan'

‘Hundreds of local residents and a large number of local businesses have already written to Richmond Council in support of the proposals, and we look forward to continuing to work closely with the council, residents and other stakeholders throughout the planning process.’

As RFU chief executive, Bill Sweeney, revealed last year, the doomsday scenario would be relocating to a shared stadium in Birmingham or Milton Keynes.

‘Plan A, B, C, D and all the way to Y is to stay in Twickenham,’ says one source. ‘There is no plan to move elsewhere. But it’s a common-sense business approach to have a back-up plan if the numbers just don’t add up. It’s not pie in the sky but it’s also not an immediate plan. It’s somewhere in the middle. That’s not even a conversation if we get the right answers.’

Twickenham remains the undisputable home of English rugby. Since 1909, its global reputation has been forged by the likes of Bill Beaumont, Martin Johnson and Jonny Wilkinson. Moving elsewhere would be an assault on the sport’s history and culture.

Sports.title: 'I was one day away from falling into a coma': JAKE O'BRIEN, the Premier League's only diabetic player, on his brush with death, managing his condition in the dressing room - and why he was 'never close' to leaving Everton last summer
Sports.content:
There are few sights more incendiary to the modern manager than a footballer reaching for his phone as soon as he walks through the dressing room door. So you can imagine the reaction Jake O’Brien received when he pulled out his mobile just before one half-time team talk. But the Everton and Republic of Ireland defender had a good excuse: he’s the only Type One diabetic playing in the Premier League. O’Brien’s body is unable to create insulin, the hormone that regulates the amount of glucose in your blood. Loaded on his mobile is an app linked via Bluetooth to a circular device on his arm which gives a reading of his blood sugar levels. It is then that he takes out a needle and injects the necessary insulin dose into his thigh or stomach. ‘There was one guy who didn’t react too well. Mentioning no names! He was saying: "What are you doing on your phone?"' O’Brien recalls. ‘But he soon realised what it was for.’ It can also come as a shock to the uninitiated among his team-mates. ‘One or two are taken aback at first,’ he says. ‘It can be a bit confusing. “What’s he doing?’’ Or maybe those that are a little squeamish, but they soon get used to it. It's only a small needle.' Everton and Ireland defender Jake O'Brien is the only diabetic footballer in the Premier League O'Brien, pictured with his partner Sophie, says some of his team-mates are 'taken aback' when he injects himself with insulin (Source: Instagram/Obrienjake_) Tracking blood glucose levels is now an everyday part of O'Brien's life but it is a life that was unwittingly put in jeopardy prior to his diagnosis at 16. O’Brien was later told he had been just one day away from slipping into a coma when his concerned parents ushered him to the doctors near the family home in Youghal, County Cork, for a check-up. Their sports-mad son, who had won national titles at boxing and hurling, was tired, losing weight and had an insatiable thirst despite drinking eight to nine litres of water a day. He had lost seven kilograms in just over a week. A blood test revealed his blood sugar was ten times what was considered stable and he was rushed to hospital. ‘I was told I was a day away from a coma,' says O'Brien. 'If I had gone to sleep that night without having gone to the doctor, who knows?’ He went into hospital that night weighing 53kg, or just over eight stone. Two weeks post-diagnosis he was back up to 60kg, and within two years he had put on a whopping 30kg. 'Yeah, 30kg,' laughs O'Brien. 'I know it's not normal. It must have been some grocery bill for Mum, but I was motivated to put on the weight, going to the gym all the time. ‘I was a bit naive about it all,' he deadpans. ‘I never expected to have anything but once I knew what diabetes was, I didn’t wallow in it, I took it as a positive. Everything just clicked for me physically. I just thought, "Right, now I know what’s wrong, I can get on with my life again". ‘It was a pain going in and out of hospital, but I just took it as education and wanted to get my sport back on track. 'My family are... I wouldn't say cold, but matter of fact. Supportive, obviously, but they are all sporty too, so it was just, "Get on with it".' O'Brien's life in the Premier League would have seemed inconceivable when he fell down to 53kg as a teenager and was hospitalised He is now an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with Today, relaxing in the cafe at Everton’s Finch Farm training complex, O’Brien is an imposing 6ft 6in tall, weighing around 96kg. His physique offers no outward indication of the daily challenge he is dealing with. There’s a Cork-lilt to his softly spoken Irish tone. He’s polite and engaging and it’s clear he revels in the role of being a diabetes ambassador, spreading the message that diagnosis doesn’t have to end your dreams. Such has been his impact, he has even attracted support from fans of the other club in the city. One, six-year-old Liverpool fan Louis, reached out via Instagram to ask O’Brien how he kept up his glucose levels during a game and whether he suffered any ‘hypos’ - the expression for hypoglycemic episodes, when the blood sugar drops too low and leaves you faint or dizzy. Louis, whose siblings Paisley and Evie also have Type One diabetes, followed up by challenging O’Brien to a penalty shootout. If the Everton man lost, he faced a forfeit, he would have to shout ‘Up the Reds’ on social media. ‘You play for the wrong team but you're still a Type One hero, and Mum says you're proof that diabetes doesn't stop you from playing at the top level,’ posted Louis. Touched by the message, O’Brien asked Everton to invite the youngster and his family to training for a kickabout, although ultimately, we are assured they reached a compromise on the penalties forfeit. ‘I’ve struck up a rapport with some kids and groups here and in Ireland,' says O'Brien. 'They often have the same story as mine of not being sure what the future holds. ‘There’s a big misconception about diabetes over what it is and the limitations it brings. ‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over.’ ‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel. I may inject four times before a night game and a bit more at half-time' ‘Just because you have diabetes doesn’t mean your dreams are over,’ says O'Brien, who also excelled at boxing and hurling as a boy (Source: TikTok/Everton) The centre back credits boxing for helping discipline with his diet but underlines ‘no food is off limits, it’s just about applying common sense'. A typical day sees him eat eggs, salmon and dates for breakfast to match his insulin doses to the carbohydrates he’s taking on around 9.30am before training. Afterwards he’ll have a light lunch at 2pm then take something back from the training ground for a light evening meal. ‘I just have to watch carbohydrates. I’ll eat more of them on match day but then work out my insulin ratio to the amount I eat and whether I need to inject more. ‘Adrenaline is higher on match days so that can change how you feel, I may inject four times before a night game and inject a bit more at half-time. If it’s not quite right you may get a bit heavy-legged or if I get a few cramps I may need a gel. But I've had no dangerous episodes.' When World Diabetes Day dawns on Saturday, O’Brien will be fully focused on preparing to play for Ireland in Austria in the Nations League. It will give him a chance to revert to his favoured centre back position having been asked to fill in predominantly at right back under David Moyes. He acknowledges it's not his preferred role but dismisses rumours that he wanted to leave as a result in the summer. 'There was nothing in that,' O'Brien affirms. ‘I was never close to leaving. 'People know I'm not a natural right back but I'll play wherever I need to, to help the team. We're only a small squad so it’s important everyone chips in. ‘There’s a lot of different right backs. I see Arsenal have centre backs playing at right back so I can take pointers from them but then again, I am 6ft 6in so I’m not the average shape.’ O'Brien insists there was 'nothing in' reports that he wanted to leave Everton last summer to get more minutes at his preferred position of centre back

Your browser does not support iframes.

At least O’Brien has former Everton captain Seamus Coleman on hand for advice. ‘Seamus is a good friend. He still gives me pointers of where to be, positioning wise and seeing the game differently.' Ireland assistant John O'Shea, a versatile defender himself in his Manchester United days, is another mentor. O’Shea and Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrímsson were at Hill Dickinson Stadium to watch O'Brien play his part in Everton's recent Carabao Cup win over Newcastle. 'Heimir is a good guy,' says O'Brien. 'Very understanding. It's always a nice change of scenery to link up with Ireland. We've got a difficult couple of games (Austria and Kosovo) but hopefully if we get two wins it’s within reach.' Indeed, if there's a mantra that personifies O'Brien's outlook on life, no matter what knocks you take, it is: always believe you can still achieve. 'Don’t be afraid and don’t let anything hold you back, that's what I say.'

Sports.title: Record-breaking Harry Kane belongs in the company of greats that he keeps. There is only one gap in his record now and he remains as central to ending 60 years of hurt than he has ever been, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Only giants have trodden the path that Harry Kane walked at Wembley on Thursday when he strode out on to the pitch on a bitterly cold winter night, his four young children by his side, and beheld the array of trophies, honours, adulation and respect that awaited him.

It is just 16 days since Kane held his hands to his face, climbed up to the stage at the London Palladium and said 'wow' when Ronaldo 'Il Fenomeno' presented him with the Ballon d'Or trophy that anointed him the best player in the world.

Now, it sat before him on a plinth and Kane broke away from the England line-up and walked forward to hoist it aloft. He showed it to all the corners of the stadium and for a moment, it was framed against the giant tifo bearing his image and the words 'England's Finest' that towered over one end of the ground.

But the Ballon d’Or is old news in the flood of honours that is coming Kane’s way in this golden summer of a great career. Kane had become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or for a quarter of a century and on Thursday night he was to break the 37-year-old record held by Peter Shilton for the most England caps. He scored the winner, too. Of course, he did.

The occasion of England-Croatia in the Nations League was Kane's 126th appearance in an England shirt and Shilton stepped forward to hand him a small case containing a crest to mark the achievement. Finally, the Prince of Wales showed his appreciation to the England captain by presenting him with a commemorative shirt with 'Kane 126' emblazoned on it.

It was a night to feel the weight of football's history and the ghosts of greatness that people England's heritage. Kane belongs in the company he now keeps. He belongs in the pantheon of the game because he is one of the deadliest strikers in history. He belongs in the pantheon because of the humility he has shown and the dedication he devotes to improvement.

Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking England appearance with a finely struck penalty

Before kick-off, Kane's history-making was celebrated with a commemorative shirt by the Prince of Wales

England 2-1 Croatia: MATCH FACTS AND RATINGS England (4-2-3-1): Pickford 6; Alexander-Arnold 6 (White 78, 6), Quansah 4, Burn 6, Hall 7; Rice 5 (Garner 78, 5), Anderson 6; Rogers 8, Bellingham 6, Gordon 5 (Ngumoha 78, 5); Kane 7 Goals: Rogers 24', Kane 64' (pen) Manager: Thomas Tuchel 6 Croatia (4-2-3-1): Livakovic 5; Smolcic 6 (Marco Pasalic 76 5), Stanisic 6, Vuskovic 6, Gvardiol 5; Misic 5 (Modric 76, 6), Kovacic 6; Sucic 7 (Mario Pasalic 70, 5), Baturina 6, Vlasic 5; Matanovic 5 (Budimir 70, 5) Booked: Smolcic Goals: Sucic 59' Manager: Slaven Bilic 5 Ref: M Krogh (DEN) 7

He belongs with Billy Wright, the first England player to 100 caps, and the man who set the England appearance record at 105 when he played for his country for the last time in 1959. He belongs with Bobby Charlton, who made it to 106 before the heartbreak of the 1970 World Cup quarter-final defeat to West Germany brought his international career to an end.

Kane belongs with Bobby Moore, Charlton's rival as the greatest England player of all time, who reached the new mark of 108 caps in November 1973. That was one of the great numbers in English sport until Peter Shilton finally surpassed it. He reached 125 caps by the time he played his last game for England in the third-place play-off at the 1990 World Cup.

It is quite some lineage. And now it is Kane who holds the prize. And if this was hardly a momentous match, it was a momentous occasion. If you are tired of glorying in a player like Kane, a relentless striker, a wonderful passer, the sweetest striker of the ball you will ever see, a player of vision, a man who exudes the beauty of simplicity and the wonder of modesty, then you are tired of football.

The honours are rushing at him in a giddy, babbling flood. It may be that he reaches close to 200 caps before he retires and even if it already seems likely that that record will be broken by Jude Bellingham, who has 61 caps at the age of 23, Kane's England goals tally, which stands at 92 after another goal against Croatia, will not be under threat for a generation or longer.

The gap, of course, is a tournament victory. That is what still separates Moore and Charlton from him. Kane is a dream of a player but he has not won the World Cup or the European Championship. What remains is the hope that he will put that right in the years that he has left in the game.

Winning the Nations League would not be quite the same but it would be a start and this victory over Croatia took England a small step closer to that goal. A convincing win over Spain in Madrid on Sunday would take them closer to their aim of finishing top of this group and getting a favourable draw in the quarter-finals in the spring.

Kane made his England debut in March 2015 when he was 21 and England's future looks brighter now than it did when he broke through. More than an hour before the game, the men who will follow Kane and perhaps even chase his caps record, chatted animatedly on the pitch. Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Gibbs-White are the new breed.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour and celebrated with his trademark cold celebration

England had found themselves pegged back by Croatia after slopping defending drew the visitors level

Referee Morten Krogh was summoned to the monitor to review the penalty shout on Thursday

Kane returned to Wembley triumphant for the first time since his historic Ballon d'Or win

After the Kane festivities, the first half was an anti-climax. Twenty-four minutes of relative drudgery ensued before Kane exhibited the breadth of his talent once again to help put England ahead. He got the ball 30 yards out, looked up and drifted a beautiful diagonal pass out to the right and into the path of Bellingham. Bellingham volleyed it across goal and Rogers forced it over the line.

The second half began slowly, too, but 15 minutes into it, Croatia equalised. England failed to clear a corner, Jarell Quansah tried to head the ball back to Jordan Pickford and, as Kane watched on, Petar Sucic stole in and hooked the ball past the England goalkeeper into the roof of the net.

Quansah made some kind of amends three minutes later when he was dragged down in the box and Danish referee Morten Krogh awarded a penalty. It was Kane-time again. Kane took the kick and lifted it gently and with a touch of curl down the centre of the goal. Dominic Livakovic dived to his left and the ball sailed softly over his trailing leg and into the net.

Croatia had chances to draw level but could not take them. England made changes and young Rio Ngumoha, a winger of rare talent, another with a rich future ahead of him, another who will help to fill the void when the day comes for Kane to bid farewell to England, came on as a late substitute for Gordon.

And so Kane's night of history began to draw to a close. In a 2-1 victory, he had made one and scored one. He remains as central to England's hopes of ending more than 60 years without a trophy as he ever has been. In a career that has festooned him with garlands and left no one in doubt of his greatness, it is the only gap that remains.

KANE EYEING NEXT FEAT ALREADY Harry Kane has set his sights firmly on rapidly reaching a century of international goals after becoming England’s most-capped player of all time. The England skipper marked his 126th appearance for the Three Lions with the winner against Croatia in the Nations League – his first goal since picking up the Ballon d’Or last month. Kane was afforded an emotional presentation pre-match at Wembley to mark both achievements and is already thinking of creating more history after moving within eight goals of a ton. ‘It’s achievable,’ Kane said. ‘I’m getting closer. Breaking the appearance record is a massive thing in the history of our game, seeing the tifo at the stadium and having my kids with me was beyond dreams. ‘It’s important to recognise our great players. It’s maybe something we haven’t done so well over the years with some of our other greats. ‘It's been a crazy few weeks. I don’t know if I’ve fully taken it all in. The reception has been overwhelming. ‘Maybe during the winter break I’ll be on a beach reflecting on everything I’ve achieved, having a drink with my wife.’ Croatia legend Luka Modric, 41, was part of the presentations ahead of kick off and Kane did not rule out attempting to prolong his career in a similar vein to the AC Milan midfielder. ‘He’s an inspiration for a lot of us,’ Kane added. ‘An incredible player and a great person, he’s looked after himself and still to be playing at this level is inspiring for me to push the limits. To see where your body and mentality takes you. ‘As long as I feel I can help, I’ll be here for as long as I can. If that’s until I’m 40, we’ll wait and see.’ Now qualified for the quarter-finals, England need to beat Spain in Madrid on Sunday to top their group and Thomas Tuchel believes they can topple the world champions. ‘It’s a completely different scenario, completely different setup,’ Tuchel said. ‘But I'm very positive that we will get what we want.’ JACK GAUGHAN

Sports.title: Prince William leads tributes to Harry Kane as England captain breaks appearance record with 126th cap: Royal presents star with shirt marking occasion as Wembley celebrates milestone
Sports.content:
Prince William led tributes for Harry Kane as Wembley honoured the England captain on reaching his record-breaking 126th cap against Croatia on Thursday.

Kane, who became the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the Ballon d'Or last month, celebrated another remarkable feat as he surpassed legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history.

After walking out with his four children for kick-off, followed by his England team-mates, the Bayern Munich forward first held his Ballon d'Or trophy aloft to Wembley's buoyant crowd, soaking up the celebrations.

Shilton approached the England captain to present him with a medal displaying his achievement, before Kane's former Spurs team-mate Luka Modric continued the tributes by offering him another gift.

Prince William then walked on to the pitch to shake Kane's hand and present him with a framed shirt, bearing the words 'Kane 126'.

As well as holding the record for England's most capped player, the 33-year-old striker is also England's highest ever scorer with 91 goals, ahead of Wayne Rooney and Sir Bobby Charlton who netted 53 and 49 respectively during their careers.

Prince William shakes Harry Kane's hand as he celebrates the England captain's record cap

The Prince led tributes as Wembley honoured Kane ahead of England's clash with Croatia

Kane, accompanied by his four children on the pitch, held his Ballon d'Or aloft to supporters

Prince William applauded 'brilliant and remarkable' Kane on his Ballon d'Or triumph with a personal social media message after the ceremony in London.

The Prince of Wales, signing his message off with his personal 'W' initial, posted on Instagram: 'Huge congratulations to Harry Kane on winning the Ballon d'Or! What a fantastic achievement and so deserved.

'A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.'

Kane, who has been widely regarded as a model professional and humble superstar during his career, admitted he still has an ego of sorts in an interview on the eve of his record-breaking England cap.

Asked if he has an ego, Kane replied: ‘That's a great question. I’m sure my wife will be able to say a thing or two!

'But ego is funny, because ego is many different things. I guess I have an ego to be the best, because I want to be the best. I just don't do it in a show-off way.’

On becoming England's highest appearance maker, he joked that some of his current Three Lions team-mates might catch his total by the end of their careers.

‘Jude (Bellingham) and Declan (Rice), they're on 60-odd caps already and you look at how young they are,’ he added. ‘So I'll try and give them a good number to catch! The goal record is going to be the one that's difficult to beat. I think that’s good!

He has passed Peter Shilton as England's most capped player in history - with 126 to his name

Kane receives a gift from ex-Spurs team-mate and fellow Ballon d'Or winner Luka Modric

’In football, you’ve never completed it. No matter what you’ve achieved, there is always a trophy that someone else has won or a goal record that someone else has. This is no time to rest. If anything, I've got better year on year, and the numbers have got better.

'While I'm feeling like this, why would I put any limit on myself? I'm just on the back of scoring 73 goals in one year, which is incredible, and I want to get 100 England goals as quickly as possible.

‘My biggest fear is finishing my career and thinking I could have done a bit more. I want to make sure that I cross every bridge and do everything possible so that, whenever that day comes, I can say, “I’ve done everything possible. I have this record, I don’t have this record, but it doesn’t matter, I can sleep well at night”.’

Sports.title: England 2-1 Croatia PLAYER RATINGS: Whose position is under 'serious' threat? Which two regulars need to show more? And who was at the heart of Three Lions' best attacking play?
Sports.content:
Harry Kane scored on his record 126th appearance for England as they beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley in the Nations League.

The Bayern Munich striker, 33, scored his 92nd goal for the Three Lions from the penalty spot to give them the victory.

Morgan Rogers had opened the scoring in the first half before Petar Sucic equalised.

Thomas Tuchel's side go to Spain on Sunday, where they will be in a shoot-out to qualify for the League A finals.

CRAIG HOPE was at Wembley to bring you our player ratings.

Harry Kane scored on his landmark 126th England outing to give them a 2-1 win over Croatia

England (4-2-3-1)

Jordan Pickford - 6

Was left exposed for goal and not much he could do. Made four fairly routine saves and kicking was fine. Tuchel says he’s the No.1 but that will only become apparent should he start in Spain on Sunday. It feels like his position is under serious threat from James Trafford, not that he did anything wrong here.

Trent Alexander-Arnold - 6

A very bright start, including one delightful drop in behind for Rogers, but he faded thereafter. Not the creative force he should be in a game like this and questions remain over both Alexander-Arnold’s current level of performance and whether anyone will emerge as England’s first-choice right back.

Jarell Quansah - 4

He was enjoying a trouble-free night until mistake leading to Croatia equaliser with baffling decision to head back to Pickford amid crowded goalmouth. He did, in part, make amends by winning penalty for Kane goal, as well as timely late slide to block shot. Doesn’t convince as a starter, though.

Dan Burn - 5

Like Quansah, all was going well until Croatia goal, and he’ll be disappointed not to get the first header on the corner before ball dropped. He looked shaky after that and was nearly outdone for a Croatia equaliser late on. Could have done with a breather after 70 minutes or so given recent return from injury.

Trent Alexander-Arnold was not the creative force he should have been in a game like this

Lewis Hall - 7

In a position that is up for grabs he did his chances no harm at all and was the pick of the backline by far. Got forward at every opportunity and rarely wasted a ball. Was also there at the other end with several key interceptions. A solid night.

Declan Rice - 5

A lot of huff and puff but, as too often in an England shirt, not enough to show for it by way of creation or penetration. With some bright young midfielders like James Garner and Alex Scott emerging, Rice has to do more, you feel, to make sure he stays in the XI. This was an underwhelming night in that regard.

Elliot Anderson - 6

Lots of involvement and omnipresent across the park, as ever. One superb dribble that drew applause, but we need to see more of that inspiration higher up the pitch. A good display, but no chances created. Partnership with Rice still feels a little forced at times.

Morgan Rogers was his team's brightest player when he forced the opening goal

Morgan Rogers - 8

Was already his team’s brightest player when he forced opening goal with close-range finish. Clearly a man in form and brought that brightness to this stage. With doubts over Saka’s durability, he looks the best bet as the starting right winger. Was at the heart of all good about England in final third.

Jude Bellingham - 6

Provided assist with confident cushion for pal Rogers and he was a threat throughout, even if final shot or pass didn’t quite come off, the assist apart. Felt like he was in second gear a little, especially knowing booking would have ruled him out of Spain on Sunday in his home city of Madrid.

Anthony Gordon - 5

Didn’t happen for Barcelona winger and he’ll know he should have done better when twice cutting in on right foot and having a good sight at goal. He missed the target on both occasions. Gordon can’t get cosy knowing he’s Tuchel’s first choice on the left, and more is needed.

Anthony Gordon will know he should have done better - he can't get cosy on the left flank

Harry Kane - 7

The quarterback! Was this a glimpse of the future? Kane operated even deeper than he usually does at times and one long-range pass from 30 yards inside his own half drew gasps from the Wembley crowd. It was his playmaker’s dink in behind that led to opener. Got his goal with penalty dink on his big night.

Substitutes

Rio Ngumoha (on for Gordon 78) - 5

Ben White (on for Alexander-Arnold 78) - 6

James Garner (on for Rice 78) - 6

Manager: Thomas Tuchel - 6

A win, but it was not comfortable and Tuchel leaves this with yet more questions about how he builds a defence for the European Championship. A sold-out Wembley weren’t exactly thrilled by England’s attack, either. Job done, but it was dull.
