Sports.title: Court of Appeal to hear Audi’s case over Tsunoda decision on November 25th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has set a date to hear Audi’s appeal over the Italian Grand Prix stewards’ decision regarding Yuki Tsunoda.

Audi is challenging the decision not to penalise Tsunoda, who finished the race in 10th position, for triggering an extra formation lap before the start of the race.

The ICA will hear the case on November 25th at the FIA’s headquarters in Paris.

Tsunoda, who substituted for Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson at Monza, finished seven seconds ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto. Therefore the Audi driver could gain a point if Tsunoda is penalised.

Bortoleto previously said Audi’s case was “straightforward”.

F1’s sporting regulations state any driver who causes an extra formation lap must start the race from the pit lane and will receive a Stop-and-Go penalty if they fail to. As Tsunoda did not start from the pit lane, Audi believes he should receive a penalty.

The stewards ruled Tsunoda “was not the ’cause’ of the extra formation lap” and therefore did not have to start from the pit lane.

This is the second time this year the ICA has been asked to rule on a decision taken by the stewards at a grand prix. In September they reinstated two penalties which were originally issued to Pierre Gasly during the Monaco Grand Prix and later rescinded.

ICA hearing announcement

On 6th September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the race director ordered an additional formation lap Following the race, the stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (driver of car number 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the driver. In decision number 69, the stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. On 9th September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty.

Sports.title: Racing Bulls keep Lawson and Lindblad as Tsolov gets Red Bull reserve role | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed an unchanged driver line-up for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will continue to drive for the team next year.

The news ends speculation Red Bull’s second Formula 1 team would replace either of its drivers with Nikola Tsolov. The Red Bull junior driver lies second in the Formula 2 standings with four races remaining.

Shortly after Racing Bulls confirmed its driver line-up, Red Bull announced Tsolov as its reserve driver for 2027. Red Bull also announced Tsolov will be Racing Bulls’ reserve driver.

Racing Bulls is on course to score its best championship result under any of its identities, including its time competing as Minardi, before it was purchased by Red Bull at the end of 2005.

However Lawson’s future at the team came into doubt as Racing Bulls delayed its decision on its driver line-up for next year. Lawson made his F1 debut in 2023 and gained promotion to Red Bull in 2025 but the team dropped him after just two rounds. Lawson made a temporary return to Red Bull this year as a substitute for the injured Isack Hadjar.

During his time at Racing Bulls, Lawson has scored enough points to single-handedly put Racing Bulls fifth in the constructors’ championship. However he clashed with Red Bull driver Max Verstappen during a practice session in Mexico earlier this month, which his rival said was “not very smart behaviour” for a driver who was “fighting for [his] seat”. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies denied his team would have any say in its junior squad’s driver line-up.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said Lawson and his rookie team mate Lindblad form “the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition”.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027.”

Tsolov said he hopes to make the step up to F1 after next year. “My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver,” he said. “Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting.

“I’m confident that with the team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.”

Mekies said Red Bull has been highly impressed by Tsolov. “Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years,” he said.

“To fight for the championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

“We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1. This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.”

Sports.title: Stats: Verstappen claims second place from lowest grid position since 1983 | 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
In 2024 Lando Norris’s championship hopes suffered a fatal blow when he failed to win from pole position at Interlagos.

Max Verstappen claimed an unlikely victory in a rain-hit race from 17th on the grid, putting him on course to retain his championship crown.

Norris has made amends since then, however, winning the next two grands prix at Interlagos from pole position. Both times he prevented Verstappen from completing another impressive back-to-front charge: the Red Bull driver finished second on Sunday from the penultimate place on the grid, just as he did 12 months earlier.

However as there are two more cars in the field this year, Verstappen’s charge to second place came from 21st position on the grid (he was actually the 20th car on the grid as Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac was pushed into the pit lane). This is the lowest starting position anyone has taken second place from since the 1983 Long Beach Grand Prix, when Niki Lauda charged there from 23rd.

Lauda started one place behind his team mate John Watson, who led him home in a McLaren one-two, setting the record for the lowest grid position from which a grand prix has been won.

McLaren may not have managed a one-two last weekend but Norris took his 14th grand prix victory, giving him as many as a trio of multiple world champions: Jack Brabham, Graham Hill and Emerson Fittipaldi. This was also his 20th pole position, the latter giving him as many as Damon Hill and Valtteri Bottas.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Norris reached the podium for the 50th time in his career. Verstappen, meanwhile, took his eighth podium finish in a row, which is the longest streak any driver has managed this year.

Isack Hadjar equalled his best finish with another third place – this was his fourth. Although he briefly hit the front of the field after Norris pitted on lap 49 he did not officially lead a lap, as he pitted the next time by and Andrea Kimi Antonelli crossed the line in front.

Liam Lawson finished seventh for the second race in a row. He has now scored enough points for Racing Bulls to single-handedly put them fifth in the constructors’ championship.

Lewis Hamilton became the second driver in Formula 1 history to record his 400th grand prix start. He joins Fernando Alonso, who reached 400 two years ago:

For the second race in a row, Haas ran a new driver, but this time their rookie did not manage to bag a point. Rafael Camara made his debut in his home race, becoming the first driver to do so since Germany’s Markus Winkelhock in the 2007 European Grand Prix, held at the Nurburgring.

Camara raced with number 51 which last appeared in a grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. It was also used on that occasion by another Brazilian driving for Haas: Pietro Fittipaldi.

Lance Stroll’s race ended in retirement yet again. That was the 14th time this year he has not been classified – failing to complete 90% of the race distance – equalling the all-time record which has been set on five other occasions by four drivers.

These are Andrea de Cesaris twice (in 1986 with Minardi and 1987 with Brabham), Piercarlo Ghinzani (in 1986 with Osella), Ivan Capelli (in 1989 with Leyton House) and Rubens Barrichello (in 1997 with Stewart).

It remains possible for Stroll to match or even exceed the record for most retirements in a season. De Cesaris set this in 1987 when he started but was not running at the end of all 16 rounds. In addition to his 14 non-classifications he ran out of fuel before completing the final lap at Spa (but was classified third) and spun out with four laps to go in the final race at Adelaide, taking eighth place.

Sports.content:
Maria Theresa de Filippis, the first woman to start a round of the Formula 1 world championship, was born 100 years ago to this day.

She started 19th on the grid for the Belgian Grand Prix in 1958 (above) in a privately-entered Maserati 250F. She took the chequered flag in 10th place, but unlike today, only the top five finishers scored points.

De Filippis started two other races that year, but retired from both with engine trouble, and made two unsuccessful attempts to qualify for the Monaco Grand Prix. She died 10 years ago.

Sports.title: Willy Hutchinson Won the WBC Belt. Why Fourth?
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson did everything required to claim the No. 1 spot in The Ring’s light heavyweight rankings, except get the actual ranking. Beating Joshua Buatsi for the vacant WBC title only moved him from seventh to fourth, leaving him stuck behind Callum Smith, Anthony Yarde, and Imam Khataev. I’d favor Hutchinson against all three, as he may already be the division’s best fighter behind champion Dmitry Bivol.

The Ring’s light heavyweight rankings

Champion: Dmitry Bivol

Callum Smith Anthony Yarde Imam Khataev Willy Hutchinson Najee Lopez Joshua Buatsi Radivoje Kalajdzic Lerrone Richards Albert Ramirez Umar Dzambekov

Putting Yarde at No. 2 makes the least sense. He is coming off a stoppage loss to David Benavidez, who exited the division to move up to cruiserweight. Yarde definitely has the power to trouble Hutchinson, assuming he can actually get inside to land it. Against Buatsi, Hutchinson forced the pace on his own terms, switched stances smoothly, and timed him on the way in. Yarde would likely spend most of the night chasing shadows, which puts him closer to the bottom of the top 10.

Smith holds the best argument of the trio since he already owns a victory over Buatsi. That win keeps him near the top, yet he has mostly been sitting around waiting for a shot at Bivol while Hutchinson went out and beat that exact same opponent for a world title. Smith belongs at second, clearing the path for Hutchinson to take the top spot.

Khataev is fine right where he is at third. His heavy hands and relentless forward pressure could easily carry him past Yarde, Smith, or Buatsi. I’d still pick Hutchinson in that matchup because his sharp footwork and sudden direction changes would force Khataev to reset his attacks every time he closed the distance. Khataev would need to cut off the ring far better than Buatsi managed to do.

The Ring made the right call leaving Artur Beterbiev off the list during his layoff. His resume will still be waiting for him whenever he decides to return. Hutchinson just delivered a fresh, championship-level performance, and it was more than enough to earn the No. 1 ranking.

Sports.title: Hearn Threatens to Sue WBA Over Jack Catterall Mandatory
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn says he’ll sue the WBA if it lets Teofimo Lopez keep his welterweight belt and fight Ryan Garcia ahead of mandatory challenger Jack Catterall. If the WBA holds Lopez to the order, he has a good reason to give up the belt. The power he showed against Rolly Romero in his welterweight debut gives him little reason to count on hurting Catterall.

“I would sue them immediately,” said Hearn on Inside the Ring when asked what he would do if the WBA ruled against him. Hearn promotes Catterall and argues the WBA had already promised his fighter a shot under a resolution that was in place before Lopez won the title.

Hearn has the WBA’s own written ruling to point to if it lets Teofimo Lopez fight Ryan Garcia and keep his welterweight belt. The WBA gave Jack Catterall a route to its top title with a 180-day deadline, then said Lopez inherited that obligation when he beat Rolly Romero. Hearn says he’ll sue if the WBA goes back on its decision.

The WBA allowed Romero one optional defense, which he used to fight Lopez. In its September order, the WBA expressly said Lopez took on Romero’s obligations when he won the title. The organization reaffirmed the mandatory on November 11 and gave the camps 10 days to agree on a fight date or propose another solution. An exception for Garcia would mean setting aside a specific commitment the WBA has now upheld twice.

The timing gives Hearn leverage. Mike Coppinger said on the show that Lopez’s team was trying to finalize a February 6 fight with Garcia. If the WBA cleared Lopez to bring its belt into that fight, Hearn could seek a court order blocking the WBA from sanctioning it as a unification while the dispute is heard. Even the prospect of that fight over the belt could complicate the promotion while the two sides are trying to close a deal.

Hearn expects Lopez to give up the title if the WBA holds him to the mandatory. It’s easy to see why. Lopez beat Romero in his welterweight debut, but his punches rarely discouraged him. If he can’t make Catterall respect his power, he could spend 12 rounds leading against a southpaw who can make him reach, catch him with the straight left, and get out before Lopez can follow up.

Lopez has the speed to win that fight. He’d still be risking the Garcia payday on his ability to win close rounds against a fighter who excels at making them close.

Catterall wants the Lopez fight. If Lopez gives up the belt to face Garcia for the WBC title, Hearn expects the WBA to elevate Catterall from its secondary champion and let him make a defense. Either outcome gives Catterall a way forward. The outcome Hearn is threatening to challenge is Lopez getting the bigger fight, keeping the belt, and leaving Catterall waiting again.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia’s Left Hook Could Derail Haney’s 154 Plans
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is already eyeing a run for all four belts up at 154 pounds. Before he can even think about junior middleweight, though, he has to clear out 147.

If Ryan Garcia is still holding the WBC welterweight strap when that undisputed opportunity rolls around, Haney will have to get past the exact guy who repeatedly caught him with short left hooks every time he reached in to clinch. That tactical hurdle is a way bigger problem than whoever ends up waiting for him at 154.

Eddie Hearn brought up the plan. He talked about Jaron “Boots” Ennis and Josh Kelly fighting, the winner going on to face Sebastian Fundora, and Haney moving up to challenge whoever comes out of that with all four belts.

“I told you that that’s what I wanted to do,” said Haney on Inside the Ring. He went a step further and said it was his idea. He still has Liam Paro to fight on December 19, and winning that unification would leave him two belts short at 147.

Haney quickly co-signed the timeline, noting he had already voiced that exact goal before taking things a step further by claiming the whole blueprint was his idea in the first place. Of course, he still has to get past Liam Paro on December 19. Even if he wins that unification bout, he will still be two belts shy of clearing out the welterweight division.

Looking back at the Brian Norman Jr. fight, it is easy to see why Haney feels confident he can control the rest of the weight class.

Ryan, on the other hand, made him pay dearly. Garcia made him pay for it. Every time Haney lunged in to grab hold, he left himself wide open for a split second before tying Ryan up. Garcia didn’t need to back up or make room to throw.

Haney was practically walking right into the punch, and once Devin got hurt and started reaching out just to survive, he kept making the exact same mistake. The commission eventually changed the official result to a no contest, but everyone saw how easily Garcia cracked him.

In a potential rematch, Haney definitely has the skills to outbox Garcia for long stretches behind his jab. The real test starts the moment Garcia closes the distance and forces Haney’s instinct to grab. Will Haney step away and make Garcia chase him? Can he tie up Ryan’s left arm before that hook comes flying in? Doing either of those things is easy enough when Haney is fresh and has his wits about him. The first fight showed what happens when he gets rocked and starts grabbing out of pure panic.

Garcia has plenty on his own plate right now, and that WBC belt could easily change hands before a second fight gets signed.

Still, Haney has made it clear he wants the rematch. If beating Garcia is the final step required to collect all four welterweight titles, Haney’s grand plan to conquer 154 might completely depend on what he does the next time he reaches in to tie Ryan up while that left hand is still loaded.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Vows to Be ‘Bad for Business’ Against Boots
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly suspects promoter Eddie Hearn would rather see Jaron “Boots” Ennis win their February 27 unification fight in Atlanta. Kelly’s response to that reality is simple: he plans to be “bad for business that night.”

The subject came up during a joint appearance on Inside the Ring, where Devin Haney pressed Kelly on the politics of the matchup while Hearn sat right beside them. Thinking back to when Matchroom promoted both him and Regis Prograis, Haney recalled feeling that Hearn genuinely had his best interests at heart. He wanted to know if Kelly felt that same backing with Matchroom representing both corners.

“I know Eddie’s favorite probably Boots. He’s good for business in the U.S.,” Kelly said to Ring Magazine. “I’m going to be bad for business that night for the U.S.”

Hearn pointed to his long history with Kelly and claimed he hates matching two of his own fighters together because he can’t cheer for either side. He also insisted that Ennis and his father and trainer, Bozy, know how good Kelly is, even as talk about Boots becoming the pound-for-pound king has fans treating this like a showcase.

If Hearn does favor Ennis, it makes total sense. Ennis is a major, fan-friendly talent who closes the show, whereas Kelly’s recent run has been built on survival and generous scorecards. Kelly looked poor in his outing against Caoimhin Agyarko. Before that, he walked away with a questionable decision over IBF champion Bakhram Murtazaliev in a fight where he spent practically the entire night on his back foot.

Their shared history against David Avanesyan tells the whole story. Avanesyan stopped Kelly in six rounds; Ennis blew Avanesyan away in five.

Haney suggested on the show that a fighter who can change range, turn Ennis, and tie him up can force Boots to take his time and think his way into the fight. The problem is that Kelly’s game doesn’t center on breaking opponents down with smart boxing.

Lately, it has revolved around running around the ring and trying to steal rounds in the final ten seconds. Hearn can still steer the winner into a potential undisputed clash with Sebastian Fundora, and unless Kelly brings a completely different style to Atlanta, Matchroom’s U.S. business plans aren’t in much danger.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Won’t Touch Britain’s Harder-Hitting Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is already trying to steer Devin Haney into an in-house unification trap with Jack Catterall, hoping the matchup will eventually set up an undisputed welterweight clash with Ryan Garcia.

For Hearn’s convenient blueprint to work, he is banking on Teofimo Lopez vacating his WBA title rather than fighting Catterall, his mandatory challenger. Sitting right beside Haney on Inside the Ring, Hearn laid out his preferred path: beat Liam Paro in December, face Catterall for the vacant WBA belt, and save Garcia for all four straps.

“Fight Liam Paro, fight Jack Catterall, who I believe will be the WBA world champion because Teo will vacate now,” Hearn said to Ring Magazine. “That’s been ordered. They’ve got 10 days to make a deal.”

Hearn’s In-House Matchmaking Hits a Wall

This is classic promotional maneuvering from Hearn, who has promoted Paro and represents Catterall. Trying to slip Catterall into a vacant title spot and feed him directly into a Haney unification bout keeps all the belts and business under the Matchroom umbrella, regardless of whether fans actually want to see it. The problem for Hearn is that the fight makes zero sense for Haney.

Haney is not going to take that kind of risk for a fraction of the money he would make fighting Garcia. Catterall is essentially Britain’s version of Shakur Stevenson, able to do everything Stevenson does in the ring while carrying more pop in his punches. Asking Haney to take on a slick, heavy-handed southpaw technician with virtually no commercial pull in the United States is a terrible business move when a massive rematch is within reach.

On paper, Lopez dropping the belt to chase Garcia opens the door for Catterall, who earned his mandatory spot by beating Shakhram Giyasov after Lopez inherited the obligation from his win over Rolly Romero. If Catterall picks up the vacant strap, he could bring a third title into the ring against Haney, assuming Haney gets past Paro first.

Haney defends his WBO belt against IBF titleholder Paro on December 19 at San Francisco’s Chase Center. Hearn naturally talked up Paro as underrated, pointing to his road win over Subriel Matias in Puerto Rico before picking Haney to unify. Hearn claimed Paro lacks the power to stop Haney or the skills to outbox him. Haney sounded even more dismissive, stating Paro looks the exact same in his recent fights as he did during their past sparring sessions.

Teofimo’s Choice Could Ruin Hearn’s Plans

Even if Haney gets through Paro, signing up for Catterall next means taking back-to-back southpaws who do nothing at the American box office while stalling the Garcia rematch. Hearn’s entire four-belt pitch also assumes Garcia holds onto his WBC title, which is far from guaranteed. Insider Mike Coppinger reported during the broadcast that Garcia and Lopez are trying to finalize a February 6 bout.

If Garcia and Lopez fight and Lopez wins, Lopez walks away with the WBC belt and instantly becomes the target Haney actually wants, leaving Catterall completely out in the cold. Haney made it clear he still wants to settle the score with Garcia alongside his goal of becoming a two-division undisputed champion.

Right now, Lopez holds all the leverage. Defending against Catterall lets him carry the WBA belt into a Garcia fight, while vacating clears his path to Garcia sooner. Hearn is clearly hoping Lopez drops the title so he can manufacture an in-house unification bout, but expecting Haney to willingly walk into an ambush against a sharper, harder-hitting version of Stevenson is pure wishful thinking.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Keeps Lester Martinez Waiting as Contenders Circle
Sports.content:
Lester Martínez traveled to Acapulco hoping the WBC would mandate a clash with Canelo Álvarez. Instead, he left facing the possibility of yet another interim title defense, with zero assurance that a win would actually earn him a crack at the undisputed super middleweight champion.

During Wednesday’s convention, the sanctioning body opted to put off making a ruling. Martínez contended that holding the interim strap gives him the right to challenge Álvarez, who recaptured the WBC crown by defeating Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on October 31. Rather than ordering the bout, WBC president Mauricio Sulaimán floated the idea of Martínez making another interim defense while Canelo weighs his future options.

“I’m here to exercise the right the WBC gave the interim champion to face the full champion,” Martínez stated in Acapulco, according to translated remarks.

Martínez already has one successful interim defense under his belt, having stopped Luka Plantic in the tenth round this past August. Prior to that, he battled Mbilli to a draw last year. If the WBC needed proof that Martínez belongs at the elite level, he already proved it across ten grueling rounds against the very fighter Canelo just defeated to reclaim the title.

Sulaimán noted that Canelo is open to facing Martínez and wants the matchup to happen on the grandest stage possible. According to the WBC’s convention summary, Álvarez still has one bout left on his current four-fight deal. This leaves Canelo plenty of breathing room to explore all his alternatives, forcing Martínez to choose between sitting on the sidelines or gambling his belt once more.

Sulaimán suggested a bout in Guatemala, which would offer Martínez a hometown showcase while keeping him sharp, though his camp admitted they had no plans in place when the idea was brought up. Accepting another defense means putting his status on the line a second time without a locked-in date against Canelo. While another victory might bolster his resume, Martínez already brought a championship belt to Acapulco to prove he deserves the shot right now.

Lester is in a classic boxing catch-22. Holding the interim belt is supposed to make him the mandatory next in line, yet if Canelo chooses to use the final fight of his contract elsewhere, he is stuck either sitting on the shelf or taking high-risk fights to stay active while everyone else hunts for a shortcut to a title shot.

The real danger for Martínez is taking on a dangerous spoiler like Kevin Lele Sadjo or Diego Pacheco for a fraction of the Canelo purse, only for Canelo to vacate the belt or retire after his next fight anyway. At that point, Martínez would have risked everything just to end up fighting for a vacant title he could have claimed without taking the extra damage.

Sports.title: Pat Brown vs. Chev Clarke: Is 7-0 Too Soon?
Sports.content:
Pat Brown has stopped every single one of his seven professional opponents. Now, Eddie Hearn’s undefeated cruiserweight prospect has been ordered to defend his British title against Chev Clarke, who is coming off a huge stoppage win over former world champion Chris Billam-Smith. The British Boxing Board of Control has set purse bids for December 9.

Brown claimed the vacant British and Commonwealth belts by knocking out John Hedges back in September. Clarke, a former British champion himself, earned a seventh-round stoppage against Billam-Smith on November 7. That kind of victory makes him a serious threat for a fighter with just seven pro bouts, even for a heavy-handed Olympian like Brown.

Matchroom locked Brown into a long-term deal in November 2024 following the Paris Olympics and has guided his entire pro run. Managed by Sam Jones and trained by Jamie Moore and Nigel Travis, Brown already holds two domestic straps. Now, defending that British title puts him directly in the path of a contender who just took out a proven world-level operator.

The real test for Brown is finding out what happens if Clarke absorbs his best shots and keeps walking forward. Brown’s power has ended every fight early so far. If Clarke survives those opening rounds, Brown will have to lean on his jab, choose his moments carefully, and pace himself against a challenger who still carried plenty of danger into the seventh round against Billam-Smith. Clarke’s recent win gives him all the confidence in the world that his odds improve the deeper the fight goes.

Getting past Clarke would give Hearn a massive reason to graduate Brown beyond the domestic scene. Clarke has already worn the belt Brown is putting on the line, and his last outing proved he can take down a former world champion. Beating him would reveal way more about Brown’s ceiling than simply padding his record with another quick knockout over lesser competition.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Rages After Dana White’s Heavyweight Phenom Steals Joe Cordina’s Fury vs. Joshua Spot
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is furious that Dana White’s 21-year-old heavyweight prospect Da’Mazion Vanhouter landed the main card spot on Fury vs. Joshua instead of Joe Cordina. Hearn claims he already had terms agreed for Cordina to face 47-year-old Manny Pacquiao in Cardiff on December 11, yet putting a fresh American knockout artist on Netflix makes infinitely more sense than trotting out another nostalgia act.

“What about Joe Cordina? What about a two-time world champion from Wales?” Hearn complained to iFL TV. Let’s be honest: if Hearn wasn’t Cordina’s promoter, he wouldn’t even mention his name for this card.

Cordina’s hometown appeal and past titles give him a thin excuse for a spot, yet the 34-year-old has been largely invisible since Anthony Cacace stopped him. The two low-profile fights he has taken since barely registered with the boxing public because of the weak opposition. Among the fans who know him, he is not a popular attraction, and American viewers tuning in for the main event have zero interest in watching him.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are already carrying the promotion based on what they did at their best, while 41-year-old Deontay Wilder brings another aging veteran to the co-feature against Jai Opetaia. Fury is 38 and looks more and more like his 61-year-old father, John Fury. Loading the card with older fighters is a disaster when you are trying to reach younger fans on Netflix who cannot connect to a lineup of relics.

Throwing Cordina into the ring with a 47-year-old Pacquiao would have been pure poison for the broadcast. From Turki Alalshikh’s perspective, there is no value in burning a prime slot on a cash-grab sideshow when the sport desperately needs new blood.

The American market makes the decision even easier. Fury and Joshua easily hook British viewers, whereas Vanhouter (14-0, 11 KOs) gives the U.S. broadcast an exciting domestic heavyweight prospect to get behind. The real payoff for featuring Vanhouter comes down the road, when younger viewers remember his explosive style and tune in for his next fight.

Questions remain about whether Vanhouter is the real deal. He turned pro at 17 in the middleweight ranks before growing into a 6’3½”, 231-pound heavyweight, giving him the footwork, loose mechanics, and compact uppercut of a smaller fighter. Still, he has only logged 27 total pro rounds, meaning his stamina against a durable opponent who can take his early power is completely untested.

Facing Michael Essomba on December 11 leaves room for doubt about the quality of the matchup, and Hearn has tried to attack the competitiveness of the fight to distract from Cordina getting left off. Even with those unknowns, a 21-year-old heavyweight on the rise belongs on this stage far more than a 34-year-old former champion trying to cash out against an aging legend.

Ghana News.title: US doctor kills building manager after long-running dispute over mould, police say
Ghana News.content:
A doctor who had been in an ongoing dispute over mould and other issues at his Washington DC apartment fatally shot his building's manager and fired at four others before killing himself, police say.

Building manager James Stuart, 46, was pronounced dead at the scene, while four others were rushed to local hospitals for treatment.

The shooting began on Thursday morning local time inside a gym in an apartment building in the Logan Circle neighbourhood, which is about a mile (1.6km) north of the White House.

Police said the suspect, identified as 55-year-old doctor Matt Wade Lambert, then barricaded himself in an apartment, and later died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

While the suspect was barricaded, "he did fire through the door at officers at least on two occasions", Jefferey Carroll, the interim chief of the Metropolitan Police Department, said at a news conference.

Negotiators had been on the phone with the suspect when they heard a gunshot and he stopped communicating with them, according to Carroll.

Officers forced their way into the apartment and saw the suspect had what appeared to be a "self-inflicted gunshot wound", he said.

Authorities are still working to understand the exact timeline, suspect's motivation, and other details of the incident.

"We do know that there has been an ongoing dispute between the suspect in this case and the building, condo, homeowners association management regarding maintenance issues, mould and the like," Carroll said.

"That there was a civil case that he filed against them. So we believe that it's related to that."

Police believe that after Lambert opened fire inside the gym, he fled the scene and then shot at the four other victims, who were on the ground level, from his patio balcony area on the building's seventh floor.

One of the injured is in a critical condition, police said.

It was not immediately clear whether he had a relationship with the other victims.

Authorities recovered three firearms from Lambert's apartment,all of which he used in Thursday's incident.

"It does appear there was some level of planning associated with this," Carroll said.

It was unclear how he obtained the weapons, as he did not have any firearms registered to him in Washington DC, police said.

Lambert also had containers of flammable liquid inside his apartment.

"We do suspect that there was probably some level of accelerant. We don't know if it was gasoline or something else," Carroll said. "So we do believe there probably was some level of pouring there."

A BBC producer who lives in the building where the shooting happened, Jonathan Csapo, said a fire alarm went off. Then, as he came out of a fire escape, he heard gunshots very close by.

"I could see the smoke, I could see the flash. We just all started running. That was our first instinct," Csapo said.

"We immediately ran and took cover behind a barricade, a little brick structure just near the building."

Csapo said he was then taken back inside to a safe room by a building manager.

"And then everybody started screaming," he said.

Michael Carney told the Washington Sun he was on a treadmill at the Vida Fitness gym when the shooting started.

He said he had heard "one pop", which he assumed was an exercise ball bursting, before seeing a victim on the floor who had been shot.

"Everyone was kind of just hiding behind planters and stuff," he said, adding a fire alarm was pulled.

Once outside the gym, Carney said he heard five or 10 shots that seemed to be coming from a nearby alley.

Another witness told the Washington Sun that she heard "an enormous, loud thing" in the fitness centre and more shots outside the gym after being evacuated.

"I thought something had crashed or fallen," she said. "I didn't know it was a gunshot until later."

Washington DC Mayor Muriel Bowser called it a "senseless act of gun violence" and said the White House had been briefed.

Lambert had been locked in a bitter legal dispute with the Metropole Condominium Association and the building's property manager for more than a year, according to the Washington Sun.

He told the newspaper's reporter, who was then working with another media outlet, that his million-dollar penthouse had been rendered unliveable after building renovations led to severe water leaks and black mould.

"It's affected every part of my life - my sleep, dietary habits," Lambert reportedly said in December.

"I pride myself on my resilience, and I've been kind of surprised at how much it has been affected."

Lambert's former lawyer, Joel Braithewaite, who represented him in the civil case against the building's management, told NBC News that the legal dispute and home maintenance cost his client $300,000 (£227,000).

Braithewaite said his client considered the DC apartment "his prized possession". But soon after moving in, he reported mould and water issues, and spent thousands on mould mitigation, according to the civil case.

He said his client felt wronged and as though the condo association took no ownership for the issues he had with the unit.

Ghana News.title: Microsoft struggling to restore service as global outage affects Outlook and Teams
Ghana News.content:
Microsoft is struggling to fix a major global outage of its service that is reportedly affecting tens of thousands of users.

Services including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot have been affected by "connectivity problems".

"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," the company wrote on X.

Reports of problems with Outlook peaked globally at nearly 140,000 around 18:00 GMT on Thursday, according to monitoring website Downdetector.

The BBC understands there is no indication the outage was caused by a cyber-attack.

The disruption affects programs that are part of Microsoft 365 – a popular online service among businesses that allows them to use workplace tools like Outlook, Teams and OneDrive.

For international organisations, this platform is essential for connecting and collaborating with colleagues around the world.

Among the issues, users may be unable to view certain files or details on their calendar apps, Microsoft said.

Its AI platform, Copilot, may also be unable to work properly.

Messaging and online meetings were largely functional, the firm added.

Microsoft said on X that the outage was caused by a number of servers "being unexpectedly unavailable", straining its remaining systems.

The company is working to address the issues with its services, said a Microsoft spokesperson.

"We appreciate our customers' patience while we work to restore services as soon as possible."

The company later warned that some services that had been restored "can become unresponsive again", adding that customers "in any region" could be affected.

Users around the world including the US, Japan and Singapore have reported facing disruptions.

AI companies feel the impact

The outage has hit other companies, including AI giants Anthropic and OpenAI, which work with Microsoft's systems.

ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected.

Microsoft last month reported an outage of its Azure cloud platform that affected the tech giant's suite of productivity tools and companies worldwide.

Electric truck maker Workhorse Group, which was expected to report third-quarter results on 12 November, rescheduled it to 16 November, citing business disruptions caused by the global Microsoft outage.

Ghana News.title: NaBCo and YEA models cannot deliver lasting jobs – Ato Forson
Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana must restructure its economy to create lasting employment, rather than rely on temporary jobs under models such as NaBCo and the Youth Employment Agency (YEA).

Speaking in an interview on Thursday after presenting the 2027 Budget to Parliament, he argued that the economy must expand its capacity to provide decent work for a growing population.

“You end up creating temporary jobs like NaBCo, which is not a solution, or YEA models. They are temporary jobs,” he said.

Dr Forson said the government’s new economic policy would focus on modernising the economy to support the country’s current population.

He argued that an economic structure designed for far fewer people could not adequately meet the needs of about 35 million Ghanaians.

“The focus of this new economic policy is to tackle the structure of the Ghanaian economy, to modernise it into a modern economy, to be able to support 35 million people, and not 6 million people.”

The minister said the next phase of policy would look beyond macroeconomic indicators to address the economy’s underlying capacity to absorb workers.

He presented the four-year focus as an opportunity to build on stability while pursuing bigger economic changes.

“What again can we do beyond macroeconomics to tackle the structure of the economy?”

Dr Forson maintained that this shift would require continued fiscal discipline. He said the government had inherited persistent inflation and an unresolved economic crisis in 2025.

According to him, failing to act would have put the economy at risk of crashing by 2026.

The government therefore constrained spending and tightened public finance management, he said.

“There was a lot of disorder; we brought order to the public financial management system.”

He cited currency stabilisation and primary surpluses as evidence of the results. He put the primary surplus at 2.5% of GDP in 2025 and 1.5% in 2026.

Dr Forson said the government now intended to lower that target as it pursued the next phase of its economic agenda.

“Now I need to reduce the primary surplus from 1.5% of GDP to 0.5%.”

His central argument was that stabilisation must be followed by structural change that supports decent employment. He maintained that temporary job schemes could not substitute for that transformation.

Ghana News.title: Telecel Cash launches E-wallet and Telecel Shop to advance digital commerce
Ghana News.content:
Telecel Mobile Financial Services has introduced the Telecel Cash E-Wallet and Telecel Shop, bringing shopping, payments and digital financial services together in the Telecel Play App.

The Telecel Cash E-Wallet lets customers on any mobile network use Telecel Cash services through the Telecel Play App, with no Telecel SIM required.

Users can send money across networks, buy airtime and data, pay utility bills and subscriptions, pay merchants, withdraw cash at Telecel Cash agent points, and manage transactions securely in a simple interface.

Alongside it, Telecel Shop is a digital marketplace within the app where customers can buy from local and international sellers.

Ghanaian sellers get discovery, payment and fulfilment in one place, while customers enjoy a wider choice of products from Ghana and abroad, paid for securely with Telecel Cash.

The launch comes as Ghana remains one of Africa's most mobile-money-driven economies, yet many businesses still lag behind consumers in digital payments.

The Bank of Ghana reports that mobile money transactions reached GHC4.54 trillion in 2025, up 50.8% from 2024.

Even so, only 37% of Ghanaian businesses accept or use digital payments, according to the latest Integrated Business Establishment Census data published in 2025 by ReFinD and ISSER with the Ghana Statistical Service. This gap presents an opportunity to drive merchant adoption and deepen financial inclusion.

Speaking at the launch, Philp Amoateng, Managing Director of Telecel Cash and Digital Transformation, said, “We are focused on making customers’ lives easier and widening access to digital services.

Telecel Shop and the Telecel Cash E-Wallet combine commerce and payments in one ecosystem, offering greater choice, convenience, and flexibility. From shopping with local and international merchants to making everyday payments, customers can enjoy a seamless, secure experience on one platform."

Telecel has partnered with Trade Enablers Group and Flood Pte Ltd to power the local marketplace, connecting customers with Ghanaian merchants and products, and to provide access to international merchants and cross-border shopping. Together, the partnerships has widened product choice from Ghana and global markets.

Speaking at the launch, Derrick Yeboah Atakora, Country Manager of Flood Pte said, “Ghana has always demonstrated a remarkable appetite for innovation.

From introducing the Sika Card in 1997 to E-zwich in 2008 and mobile money interoperability in 2018, our country has consistently embraced technologies that make everyday life and commerce easier.

Through Telecel's extensive network and trusted infrastructure, even the smallest neighbourhood shop can participate more fully in our digital economy.

For us at Flood, this partnership is more than launching a marketplace. It is about giving the businesses that form the backbone of Ghana's economy a greater opportunity to thrive”.

Representing Trade Enablers Group a Danish company, Priscilla Nana Yaa Opoku, Senior Economic Diplomacy Adviser for Tech and Digitalisation and Regional Lead for Sub-Saharan Africa at the Trade Council of Denmark remarked, “Denmark has a strong tradition of digital innovation, entrepreneurship and technology development.

The partnership between Telecel and Trade Enablers Group is a practical example of how Danish expertise and international collaboration can contribute to opportunities in the Ghanaian market.

It brings together the reach and established customer ecosystem of one of Ghana's leading telecommunications operators with the international digital commerce expertise of a Danish-founded company.

This is precisely the kind of private-sector collaboration that we seek to encourage: partnerships that translate innovation into tangible commercial opportunities”.

By serving customers on other networks, the Telecel Cash E-Wallet advances financial inclusion and helps more people join Ghana's growing digital economy without changing networks.

Owureku Asare, Head of Fintech and Innovation at the Bank of Ghana, congratulated Telecel Cash on launching Telecel E-Wallet and Telecel Shop. He said, “This is innovative and will provide clear opportunities for MSMEs in Ghana”.

Customers on any network can now use Telecel Cash through the Telecel Play App, without a Telecel SIM. To get started with the Telecel Cash E-Wallet and Telecel Shop, they only need to download or update the app from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store.

Ghana News.title: NHIS quiz: Young people are powerful agents of change —NHIA Deputy CEO
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy CEO in charge of Administration and Human Resources at the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), has called on students to become ambassadors of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) by helping to educate their families, friends and communities about its benefits.

Raphael Segkpeb said young people play an important role in raising public awareness of the scheme and supporting efforts to ensure access to quality, affordable healthcare for all Ghanaians.

Mr Segkpeb made the appeal during the Greater Accra Regional NHIS Inter-School Quiz Competition, where he highlighted the importance of equipping students with accurate information about the scheme and its contribution to healthcare delivery.

He explained that the NHIA organised the competition to promote awareness and deepen students' understanding of the NHIS, including its benefits and role in improving access to healthcare.

According to him, young people could effectively disseminate information about the scheme if they had the necessary knowledge and understanding.

“We believe at the National Health Insurance Authority that young people are powerful agents of change. By equipping you with the right information, you can become National Health Insurance Scheme ambassadors, and help educate families, friends and communities,” he said.

Addressing the participating schools, Mr Segkpeb encouraged contestants to give their best, demonstrate teamwork and uphold the principles of fair competition throughout the contest.

He, however, reminded them that the competition's significance went beyond winning or progressing to the next stage, stressing that the knowledge gained during the exercise was the most valuable reward.

He urged students to approach the contest as a learning opportunity and appreciate the broader educational benefits of participating, irrespective of their eventual performance.

“Beyond winning, the most important thing is the knowledge you acquire today,” he emphasised.

The Deputy CEO also encouraged contestants who might not qualify for the next rounds, assuring them that failing to advance in a quiz competition did not make them failures.

Drawing on his experience as a secondary school student, he said he had participated in several quiz competitions, but never won

He shared this experience to show that not winning a competition shouldn't discourage students or make them feel inadequate, especially when they've gained valuable knowledge and experience.

“If you do not make it to the next round, it doesn't make you a failure. Let me tell you, when I was in secondary school, I probably participated in several quizzes; I won none. I don't think I'm the worst for it,” he said.

Mr Segkpeb further commended the Greater Accra Regional Office of the Ghana Education Service (GES) and the entire organising team for their commitment and efforts towards making the NHIA initiative a reality.

He acknowledged their contribution to the organisation of the competition and encouraged continued collaboration in promoting health insurance education among students.

He said initiatives of this nature were important in ensuring that young people understood the NHIS and could contribute meaningfully to raising awareness about its benefits within their respective communities.

Reaffirming the Authority's message, he urged stakeholders to sustain efforts to promote the scheme as an important means of facilitating access to healthcare.

“Let us continue to promote our message, the National Health Insurance Scheme, your access to healthcare,” he stated.

He wished all participating schools the best of luck as they prepared to respond to questions from the quizmasters, expressing hope that the competition would be memorable and successful.

At the end of the competition, Accra High School emerged winners with 42 points after four rounds of questions.

Accra Academy finished second with 40.5 points, while Ebenezer Senior High School placed third with 40 points.

The final scores were as follows:

Position School Round 1 Round 2 Round 3 Round 4 Total 1st Accra High School 12 12 8 10 42 2nd Accra Academy 12 12 8 8.5 40.5 3rd Ebenezer SHS 12 12 8 8 40

The Greater Accra Regional NHIS Inter-School Quiz Competition is part of the NHIA's efforts to strengthen health insurance education among students, promote understanding of the scheme and encourage young people to become advocates for wider public awareness.

Ghana News.title: Ghana must modernise economy to meet growing population’s needs – Ato Forson
Ghana News.content:
Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, Finance Minister.

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana must reshape its economy to support 35 million people and create decent jobs, rather than rely on temporary employment programmes.

Speaking in an interview on Thursday after presenting the 2027 Budget to Parliament, he argued that the country’s economic structure had not kept pace with its population.

“We are 35 million people and counting.”

Dr Forson said an economy designed for a much smaller population could not adequately meet today’s employment needs without fundamental changes.

He described the government’s New Economy policy as an effort to address that mismatch through structural reform and modernisation.

“The focus of this new economic policy is to tackle the structure of the Ghanaian economy, to modernise it into a modern economy, to be able to support 35 million people, and not 6 million people.”

The minister argued that temporary employment schemes could not replace an economy that generates sustainable opportunities.

Referring to NABCO and Youth Employment Agency models, he said such interventions did not resolve the underlying problem.

“They are temporary jobs.”

For Dr Forson, the next phase of economic policy must therefore go beyond stabilising headline indicators. It must strengthen the economy’s capacity to absorb people into decent employment.

“What again can we do beyond macroeconomics to tackle the structure of the economy?”

He said the government’s immediate priority after taking office in 2025 had been to restore fiscal discipline and prevent a deeper crisis.

According to him, persistent inflation and disorder in public financial management required difficult decisions to constrain spending.

“There was a lot of disorder; we brought order to the public financial management system.”

He attributed the subsequent currency stability and primary surpluses to those measures.

Dr Forson cited a primary surplus of 2.5% of Gross Domestic Product in 2025 and 1.5% in 2026 as evidence of the fiscal adjustment.

He said the government now intended to lower the target as it pursued the next stage of its economic programme.

“Now I need to reduce the primary surplus from 1.5% of GDP to 0.5%.”

The minister maintained that structural transformation must proceed alongside continued discipline. His central argument was that restoring stability created the opportunity to tackle deeper weaknesses that limit employment and economic opportunity.

Ghana News.title: Dangote eyes 500,000-tonne cocoa processing deal in Ghana – Ato Forson
Ghana News.content:
Nigerian billionaire and industrialist Aliko Dangote is seeking to establish a major cocoa-processing operation in Ghana, with a proposed arrangement that could involve the local processing of 500,000 metric tonnes of cocoa, Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson has disclosed.

He said Mr Dangote had personally contacted him and President John Dramani Mahama to express interest in using Ghana as a processing hub, in what could become a significant investment in the country's drive to retain more value from its cocoa industry.

The two sides are currently discussing the terms of the proposed arrangement, which the minister said could help Ghana meet its target of processing more than half of its cocoa locally by 2028.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Thursday, November 12, after presenting the 2027 Budget to Parliament, Dr Forson said the prospective investor was prepared to commit to a large-scale operation rather than a modest venture.

“I don't want to mention names, but already a major businessperson operating in the sub-region has reached out to me to sign a contract for 500,000 metric tonnes of cocoa value addition here in Ghana to process it locally in Ghana,” he said.

He subsequently identified Mr Dangote as the businessman behind the proposal, adding that the Nigerian industrialist had personally reached out to him and the President.

"I think it would not hurt if I mentioned Dangote has reached out to use Ghana as a hub to process cocoa locally," he disclosed.

“He reached out to me. He reached out to His Excellency the President. He's ready to come to Ghana,” Dr Forson said.

According to the Finance Minister, Mr Dangote believes he could help Ghana process more than 50 per cent of its cocoa locally by 2028.

The proposal comes as the government intensifies efforts to move the country away from exporting largely unprocessed cocoa beans and capture a greater share of the value generated from the commodity.

Presenting the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy, Dr Forson announced a target to process at least 50 per cent of Ghana's cocoa locally by 2028 and increase that proportion to 100 per cent by 2030, paving the way for a ban on raw cocoa exports.

The planned expansion is expected to cover not only the grinding of beans but also the production of cocoa liquor, butter, cake, powder, chocolate, cosmetics and other finished products.

The government says the country that produces the cocoa should also retain a larger share of the income, industrial activity and employment generated from processing it.

The initiative forms part of the government's US$3 billion commercial agriculture programme under its wider US$10 billion, four-year economic transformation agenda, which seeks to expand domestic production, strengthen agro-processing and create jobs.

Ghana has also been working to make more cocoa beans available to domestic processors. In February 2026, Cabinet directed that at least 50 per cent of cocoa beans be processed locally from the 2026/27 crop season, alongside plans to revive the state-owned Cocoa Processing Company.

Dr Forson said the proposed engagement with Mr Dangote could give further impetus to the government's ambition to establish Ghana as a major cocoa-processing centre in the sub-region.

However, the proposed 500,000-tonne arrangement remains under discussion, with the terms yet to be concluded and a contract yet to be signed.

Ghana News.title: Ghana’s economy would have crashed in 2026 without tough decisions – Ato Forson
Ghana News.content:
Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson

Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson says Ghana’s economy would have crashed in 2026 if the government had not taken tough decisions to restrain spending and restore discipline in public finances.

Speaking in an interview on Thursday after presenting the 2027 Budget to Parliament, he defended the fiscal measures the government has taken since assuming office in 2025.

He said the administration inherited persistent inflation and an economic crisis that required an immediate change in direction.

“In 2025 we inherited a situation where inflation had become sticky, the economic crisis was still around,” he said.

According to Dr Forson, continuing with business as usual would have pushed the economy into a crash by 2026. He said the government responded by tightening fiscal policy and addressing disorder in public financial management.

“There was a lot of disorder; we brought order to the public financial management system,” he said.

He pointed to currency stabilisation and primary surpluses as evidence of the results.

Dr Forson cited a primary surplus of 2.5% of GDP in 2025 and 1.5% in 2026. He said the next step was to reduce the target to support the government’s economic programme.

“Now I need to reduce the primary surplus from 1.5% of GDP to 0.5%.”

The Finance Minister said restoring stability was only part of the task. The government now needed to restructure the economy to create sustainable employment.

He argued that Ghana’s economic foundations had not evolved sufficiently to meet the needs of its growing population.

“We are 35 million people and counting.”

Dr Forson said the country could not keep relying on an economic structure designed for a much smaller population.

He described temporary employment programmes as inadequate substitutes for the structural changes needed to generate decent jobs.

He explained that the New Economy policy would focus on modernising production and expanding the economy’s capacity to absorb workers.

“The focus of this new economic policy is to tackle the structure of the Ghanaian economy,” he said.

He framed the programme as a four-year effort to move beyond macroeconomic stabilisation while maintaining the discipline that had helped secure it.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Finland detects strike on Russian warship as Zelenskyy meets US envoys
World.content:
Reports of alleged incident follow US envoys’ meetings with the Russian and Ukrainian president.

Finland’s military says its forces have detected a rare strike on a Russian navy vessel in the Baltic Sea as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy praised mediation efforts led by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.

A spokesperson for the Nordic country’s military said in an email to the Reuters news agency that its forces “detected … a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and has monitored the development of the situation”, adding that Finland is not under “any immediate military threat”.

The statement did not provide further details on where the strike originated, the location or timing of the incident, or how it was detected.

Reuters said it was not immediately clear if there were any casualties or what had caused Wednesday’s strike.

Estonia shares a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea with Finland. Local media reported that the vessel was a small Russian navy ship which had returned to Saint Petersburg after the alleged attack.

Ukraine’s Security Service has said it carried out the attack, according to Finnish broadcaster Yle. In recent days, Russia said it had intercepted at least 146 Ukrainian drones in the northwestern Leningrad region.

On Wednesday, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania had issued warnings to citizens to take shelter due to drones in their airspace, and NATO warplanes were scrambled in response.

Shuttle diplomacy

On Thursday, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow before meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ireland.



The US shuttle diplomacy followed trilateral negotiations in the United Arab Emirates this week, which produced no major breakthrough, aside from an agreement to swap a large number of prisoners.
