Russia’s state-run news agency TASS reported that the prisoner exchange should happen in two to three weeks. If finalised, it would be the latest in a long line of such exchanges.

“We are also working toward what would be the largest prisoner exchange of the war, potentially reuniting thousands of people with their families,” Kushner said on X on Thursday, following his meetings.

World.title: Trump moots toppling Cuba authorities before leaving office
World.content:
Saying it’s ‘a failed nation’, the US president considers military intervention in Cuba before he leaves office.

US President Donald Trump has said he would “certainly consider” using military force against Cuba, adding that he wants to “get Cuba done” before he leaves office in 2029.

In a phone interview on Thursday with conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt, of Salem News Channel, Trump was asked whether he was considering “freeing Cuba” through a military intervention.

“I want to get Cuba done before I leave,” he said, adding that the administration was “watching it very closely”.

Trump called the island “essentially a failed … place, nation, whatever you wanna call it”.

Politico reported that it was the first time Trump had put a timeline on a possible operation.

Trump said Secretary of State Marco Rubio, whose parents are from Cuba, “would love to do it”.

“I’d love to be able to do it for the people, for the Cubans that came and were treated really badly, and they came to America,” Trump said. He added that he won the Cuban vote in Florida by a wide margin.

Pressure campaign

Trump has repeatedly threatened to topple authorities in Cuba.

On Monday, he said Cuba “will fall fairly soon” and that the US would help it “on a humanitarian basis”.

In March, he said he believed he would have “the honour of taking Cuba”, making the remarks as the island’s power grid collapsed.

Trump put Cuba under a de facto oil blockade in January, after the US seized Venezuela’s president, Nicolas Maduro, and cut off Venezuelan oil to the island.

He signed an executive order declaring Cuba an “unusual and extraordinary threat” to the US and threatened tariffs on any country that supplied it with fuel.



The blockade has caused repeated nationwide blackouts, fuel and food shortages, and a humanitarian crisis.

Cuban officials have called it “collective punishment”.

Washington has added sanctions, including on Cuba’s state oil company, President Miguel Diaz-Canel and relatives of former President Raul Castro, and announced a new round this month targeting 10 people and entities tied to the government, military and oil industry.

The US has also issued an arrest warrant for Castro. Officials from both sides have held talks on the blockade, but Cuba’s foreign minister said in June there had been “no progress”.

In March, the head of US Southern Command told senators that US troops were not rehearsing for an invasion of Cuba.

Cuban officials said the island was ready for any attack.

World.title: After Iraq ex-MP’s killing, Lebanon asks Syria to extradite suspects
World.content:
Lebanese authorities have asked Syria to hand over two Syrians suspected of involvement in the killing of former Iraqi MP Ahmed al-Alwani, who was found dead in an apartment in Beirut earlier this week.

A Lebanese judicial source told the AFP news agency that preliminary findings indicate al-Alwani was strangled to death, but the perpetrators and motives remain murky.

Hailing from Ramadi in Iraq’s Sunni heartland, al-Alwani was a vocal critic of Iranian influence over Baghdad and had served more than a decade in prison after an initial death sentence on “terrorism” charges in his home country.

Investigators at the Lebanese Public Prosecutor’s office had asked Damascus to arrest and hand over two Syrian nationals, the source added, who are suspected of involvement in al-Alwani’s killing.

The source said the identities of the two suspects are yet to be determined, and that a Lebanese national had been arrested and is being interrogated.

In a separate case, the Information Branch of the Internal Security Forces is investigating five Hezbollah members who were arrested in the Batroun highlands in northern Lebanon, according to the public prosecutor’s media office.

The official National News Agency said Lebanon’s top prosecutor, Judge Ahmed Rami al-Hajj, is personally overseeing the investigation into al-Alwani’s killing, which is being carried out by the Information Branch of Lebanon’s Internal Security Forces.

Motives investigated

Investigators are still trying to ascertain the possible motives behind the killing, but the initial inquiry reveals a financial angle, sources told AFP.



Al-Alwani’s body was found on Tuesday evening in an apartment in the Tariq al-Jdideh neighbourhood of Beirut, according to Lebanese media.

Al-Alwani had arrived in Beirut from Erbil airport on a Middle East Airlines flight on the evening of November 5 and was driven to a hotel, according to the head of the Iraqi Security Media Cell, Lieutenant General Saad Maan, who is following the investigation in Lebanon.

Maan told the Iraqi News Agency (INA) that al-Alwani left the hotel less than an hour after checking into his room, telling staff at the reception that he was leaving with friends.

The hotel staff told investigators that the people who were accompanying al-Alwani were speaking with a Syrian accent, according to Maan.

INA reported that al-Alwani left the hotel in a white Range Rover vehicle, after which he made two calls to relatives back in Iraq before contact with him was lost.

Death sentence

Iraq’s President Nizar Amedi has called for a swift investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the killing and identify the perpetrators, after meeting Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam in Turkiye on Wednesday.

Al-Alwani, a Sunni politician, formerly represented the western province of Anbar in Iraq’s parliament. He rose to prominence during the protests of 2012 and 2013 against the Shia-led government of then-Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki, whom critics accused of sectarian policies marginalising Sunnis.

He was also a vocal critic of Iran’s influence in Iraq and of Iranian-backed Shia armed groups in the country.

Al-Alwani was arrested in December 2013 during a security raid on his home in Ramadi, during which his brother and several others were killed.

He was sentenced to death in 2014 on “terrorism” charges, but released in April 2025 under Iraq’s General Amnesty Law after more than a decade in prison.

Iraq’s Ambassador to Lebanon Mohammed Reda al-Husseini said on Tuesday that the Iraqi embassy was following the case closely.

He said the embassy is awaiting the final report from the Lebanese security agencies to “disclose the circumstances of the crime”.

World.title: Albania’s PM says 2027 NATO summit will not be held in Tirana
World.content:
Albania has faced criticism over low defence spending, as Rama is also under pressure at home after months of protests.

Share Albania’s PM says 2027 NATO summit will not be held in Tirana on social media

NATO will not be holding a summit in Albania next year as planned, Prime Minister Edi Rama has said, as his government faces criticism over its defence spending and protests at home.

Speaking in Dublin on Thursday ahead of a gathering of European leaders, Rama said there was “not yet [a] common position on when the summit will happen, for sure not in 2027”.

He added: “And in 2028, if it will be a summit, it will be in Tirana.”

A NATO official said the next summit “will be held in Albania”, with a decision on the date yet to be made.

Summit doubts

Reuters reported in June that plans for a summit in Albania had been thrown into doubt by resistance from the administration of US President Donald Trump and dissatisfaction among NATO members with Tirana’s low defence spending.

NATO leaders said in a declaration at their June 2025 summit in The Hague that they looked forward to meeting in Turkiye in 2026, “followed by a meeting in Albania”. But the declaration from the July summit in Ankara made no mention of a time or place for the next meeting.

NATO has been considering ending its recent practice of holding annual summits, which could avoid a potentially tense encounter with Trump later in his term.

Diplomats say the alliance could still hold a summit at short notice this year, but not in Tirana, Reuters said.

Domestic pressure

Rama, who has been in office for 13 years, has faced months of protests.

They began in May after he gave preliminary approval to a luxury resort backed by Jared Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, in the protected Vjosa-Narta wetland at Zvernec, on Albania’s southern coast, and on nearby Sazan Island.



Dubbed the “Flamingo Revolution”, they grew into wider anti-government protests demanding Rama’s resignation over alleged corruption, and into violent student protests in October over conditions at universities.

Opposition lawmakers led by Sali Berisha disrupted a session of parliament with flares and smoke bombs on October 29 in support of the protesters.

Rama has refused to resign and says the resort complies with Albanian and European Union law. His government has dismissed the protests as orchestrated by political rivals.

World.title: Iran war live: Trump says Gulf allies urged pause in Iran strikes
World.content:
blinking-dot Live updates Live updates,

Iran war live: Trump says Gulf allies urged pause in Iran strikes

Trump says Gulf countries asked him to hold off on further attacks against Iran as Tehran targets US radar in Bahrain.

World.title: Yemen’s Houthis renew strikes on Saudi Arabia as UNSC extends sanctions
World.content:
Saudi-led coalition forces have said they intercepted suspected Houthi drones over Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh region and Eastern Province, as the UN Security Council agreed to extend sanctions on the Iran-allied group.

Major General Turki al-Maliki, the spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition, announced the interceptions of suspected Houthi drones on Thursday, in a statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency.

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group had targeted oil infrastructure and military assets in the kingdom, including a pumping station on the East-West Pipeline with a drone as well as the Yanbu oil facility on the Red Sea.

Riyadh says it has rerouted about 4 million barrels of crude per day via its East-West Pipeline to Yanbu, equivalent to about 4 percent of global supply.

Saree further claimed a military cargo plane at Sharurah airport close to Yemen’s border was targeted with a drone, while a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait airbase “scored a direct hit”.

The Houthi spokesperson added that their forces had targeted the Saudi Aramco headquarters in the capital, Riyadh, but rejected as a “grave falsehood” a Saudi assertion that the group had targeted the kingdom’s Mecca region on Wednesday.

Saudi-backed coalition forces fighting on behalf of Yemen’s internationally recognised government say they continue to confront the Houthis across all frontlines, targeting leaders, vehicles, reinforcements, weapons and positions.

Yemen’s Defence Ministry, citing the Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council, said the battle against the Houthis was moving towards its “desired objectives”, according to Yemen’s official pro-government Saba news agency.



A meeting convened by the Defence Ministry was held in the Marib governorate to discuss the ongoing operations against the Houthis, where ways to enhance coordination and integration between various military units that are part of the Dawn of Yemen offensive were also discussed.

Security Council extends sanctions

On Thursday, the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) unanimously voted in favour of extending sanctions related to Yemen for one more year, including freezing assets and enforcing travel bans, while demanding an end to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

The mandate for the UN Panel of Experts on Yemen, which made the recommendations, was also extended.

UNSC members called on “all parties to refrain from escalatory actions and to resolve differences and disputes through negotiation”, while also backing the territorial integrity of both Saudi Arabia and Yemen.

“The resolution condemns the military escalation by the Houthis, their maritime and cross-border attacks against Saudi Arabia, and their threats to commercial shipping vessels,” the UNSC statement said.

The resolution emphasised that measures taken for the purpose of maintaining sanctions “shall not apply to humanitarian assistance or supplies for basic needs of civilians, without negatively affecting legitimate trade activities”.

“The council sanctions are merely a means, not an end in themselves,” said Ambassador Fu Cong, China’s envoy to the UN, who hoped that “the situation in Yemen will de-escalate as soon as possible”.

333,000 displaced

On Thursday, the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) said more than 333,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since the beginning of August, including more than 24,000 displaced in the past week.

Civilians “continue to pay a heavy price as violence damages health facilities, forces families from their homes, and hinders the work of humanitarians”, OCHA said.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia is pressing the European Union to adopt an EU Parliament resolution to designate the Ansar Allah Houthi movement as a “terrorist organisation”, according to the Reuters news agency, citing sources familiar with the drive.

But European officials told Reuters the bloc is concerned this could undermine a future peace process.

EU foreign policy spokesperson Anouar El-Anouni said the bloc was in regular contact with Riyadh on regional developments, but declined to comment on any specific discussions under way, according to Reuters.

World.title: Russian court jails rights lawyer for 12 years on treason charge
World.content:
Prosecutors say the woman shared security details with Ukraine, while her lawyers argue the information wasn’t secret.

A court in Russia’s Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad has sentenced a 66-year-old rights lawyer to 12 years in prison for treason, after prosecutors accused her of passing sensitive information to Ukraine.

The court imposed the sentence on Thursday on Maria Bontsler, according to the rights group Slovo Zashchite, which said she had worked with a number of defendants accused of political offences in Kaliningrad.

The territory sits on the Baltic Sea between Lithuania and Poland.

A court statement posted on Telegram did not name her, but said she had been detained by the FSB intelligence agency on allegations of passing information to Ukraine beginning in 2024 about security officers in Kaliningrad.

Prosecutors also alleged she gave Ukraine information on criminal cases in the exclave that were of interest to Kyiv, the statement said.

She was also given an extra year of restrictions on her activity. Prosecutors had sought 15 years, according to Slovo Zashchite.

Closed trial

Slovo Zashchite said the trial was held behind closed doors, with Bontsler and her lawyers prevented from attending, and that she was allowed only to make a closing statement. It said her lawyers argued that none of the information cited by prosecutors was secret, and that she had been in ill health in detention.

Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, parliament has approved laws that make public actions aimed at “discrediting” the army illegal and ban the spread of “fake news” about the armed forces.



Russian courts have also jailed lawyers who took on politically sensitive cases. In January 2025, a court sentenced three lawyers of the late opposition leader Alexey Navalny to between three and a half and five and a half years on “extremism” charges, in a case widely seen as an effort to discourage defence lawyers from taking political cases.

World.title: Italy fight back to beat France 3-1 and move top of Nations League group
World.content:
Michael Olise gives France the lead, but double from Pio Esposito and one from Davide Frattesi secures win for Italy.

Francesco Pio Esposito struck twice to inflict a first defeat on Zinedine Zidane as France’s head coach, while Italy stormed back to win 3-1 at San Siro and top their Nations League group.

Michael Olise profited from a Gianluigi Donnarumma error to put the visitors in front after 10 minutes on Thursday, but Italy hit back through Esposito and Davide Frattesi either side of half-time.

Inter Milan striker Esposito’s second came from the penalty spot after his brother Sebastiano had earlier fired a spot kick wide, while France were twice denied by the woodwork in an entertaining encounter.

The result sent Italy top of Group A1 on 10 points, level with France but above them on head-to-head record, while Belgium are third on nine points after inflicting a fifth straight defeat on rock-bottom Turkiye.

France were without star attackers Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele through injury, but it did not show as they made an electric start in pouring rain in Milan.

Desire Doue hit the side netting and first-time captain Adrien Rabiot tested Donnarumma before Lucas Da Cunha’s rasping half-volley flew narrowly wide.

But the opener was gifted to France when Donnarumma passed the ball straight to Olise, who skipped past a defender before firing home his fifth goal in five Nations League games – a record only bettered by England captain Harry Kane’s seven.

The hosts struck back in the 26th minute with their first chance of the game when Nicolo Cambiaghi drove to the byline and cut back a cross, which Esposito converted with a deft touch.



The goal brought San Siro to life as the older Esposito sibling, Sebastiano, threatened a quickfire comeback two minutes later, forcing a sharp save from Mike Maignan.

Bradley Barcola came closest to a third goal before the break with a curling shot from the edge of the box that struck the foot of the far post.

The end-to-end nature of the game continued in the second half as Rayan Cherki’s rasping strike was tipped onto the post by Donnarumma before Italy charged up the other end and forced Maignan into a point-blank save from Cambiaghi.

Italy had a glorious chance to go in front when Cambiaghi was tripped by Malo Gusto to earn a penalty, but Sebastiano Esposito failed to join his brother on the scoresheet as he hammered his spot kick wide on the hour mark.

The Azzurri did not dwell on the disappointment for long, taking the lead just three minutes later when Frattesi drilled in a shot from a Federico Dimarco cross moments after the Inter Milan wing-back was brought off the bench.

Fellow substitute Antonio Vergara earned the home side another penalty when he was tripped by Dayot Upamecano, and this time Francesco Pio Esposito stepped up to drill a shot into the bottom corner.

The result continued a strong start to Roberto Mancini’s second spell as Italy coach as his side stretched their unbeaten run to four matches and notched their first home win over France since 1962.

Belgium host Italy and Turkiye travel to France in the final round of group games on Sunday.

Elsewhere, captain Harry Kane celebrated his record 126th cap for England with a match-winner from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 at Wembley on Thursday to qualify for the Nations League last eight.

The 33-year-old followed a script that seemed destined to happen when he stepped up in the 64th minute to put England ahead in front of an 80,400-strong crowd after the hosts had conceded a sloppy equaliser five minutes earlier.

It was the Bayern Munich forward’s 92nd England goal, and there was never any doubt from the moment he placed the ball and sent it straight down the middle as goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic dived to his left.

Kane had started a night of celebration as the centre of attention, handed a commemorative token by former goalkeeper Peter Shilton, the previous record holder since 1989, when he surpassed Bobby Moore’s 108 caps.

World.title: Scandal-hit Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang quits, plunging AI chipmaking giant into turmoil
World.content:
And US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on Thursday the Department of Justice had not yet drawn any conclusions about whether Alice Huang was engaged in espionage for Beijing.

Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Coons, along with other Democrats on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, publicly demanded that Huang brief Congress on the matter.

If he refuses to appear voluntarily before any committee that calls him, he could be subpoenaed, one Senate staff member told the BBC.

Nvidia officials have repeatedly declined to comment since Wednesday. A personal representative of Huang also declined to comment on Thursday.

According to US media, Huang's alleged second affair was with a long-time Nvidia executive, Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to him within the company.

Sources have told the BBC that Nvidia employees had noticed the pair were unusually close.

Huang had been widely expected to weather the storm after the first affair became public, even as Nvidia announced it had launched an investigation into whether its CEO had been "the target of a foreign intelligence effort".

One current Nvidia staff member told the BBC that the initial reports of his infidelity were more or less brushed off by rank-and-file workers inside the company.

It wasn't until Huang's alleged affair with the Nvidia executive became public that workers started to feel "this is crazy", the person said.

Another Nvidia employee said they had been told not to speak with the press or otherwise comment on the situation in public.

Many staff have earned millions of dollars in compensation through their ability to cash out their Nvidia shares as the stock soared.

Nvidia has said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised", but pledged that its independent inquiry would look at all available information.

The company's meteoric rise had been led by Jensen Huang, who became a major booster of the AI industry, which relies on Nvidia for the powerful computer chips it manufactures.

Initially those chips were designed for computer gaming.

But as AI technology evolved in the last four years into chatbots and large language models, companies building AI tools suddenly required huge numbers of the Nvidia computer chips that could process large amounts of data.

Nvidia is now hunting a permanent replacement for Huang. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named on Thursday as interim CEO.

Several tech insiders that the BBC spoke with this week noted that Huang's downfall has been a major topic of conversation in San Francisco Bay area circles, an area filled with tech employees, industry executives and billionaires.

He is far from the first tech titan to become embroiled in revelations of infidelity.

Bill Gates of Microsoft and Jeff Bezos of Amazon had affairs exposed in the last decade. Both men are now divorced from their wives.

Huang has been married to Lori Huang for 40 years. Both of their children are also executives at Nvidia.

Nvidia's stock fall this week is the most significant five-day drop the company has seen since going public 27 years ago.

Its market value rose by more than 470% in the past five years, peaking just a few weeks ago. It is now down by 31% against a backdrop of wider uncertainty in the tech sector.

Because of Nvidia's size and success in recent years, such a drop can have a direct impact on the savings accounts of ordinary Americans.

Nvidia's value makes up about 7% of the S&P 500 index. That index is offered as a popular index fund in US retirement savings accounts.

Those account balances rise and fall with the changes of the stock market.

World.title: Zelensky welcomes US bringing Europe into Russia-Ukraine peace talks
World.content:
Zelensky has for several years been calling for European delegates to be included in the peace talks, and says it makes sense because of Kyiv's longer-term ambition to join the European Union.

On Thursday, Kushner said that the US has been "working very, very closely over the past several months with Europeans and I think that that's been very important."

He added that he had stressed to Putin how important it is to have European delegates "at the table".

"He's willing to give it a try," Kushner added.

Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US government's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin.

Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent.

Earlier on Thursday, Vice President of the European Commission Kaja Kallas, the EU's top diplomat, told BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player".

Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal.

Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) MicheÃ¡l Martin told a host of Euro leaders gathered in the Irish capital on Thursday that he believed the security of the region has been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war.

"Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters.

Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine remains under control of Russian forces, and cross-border incursions are increasingly common.

Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky.

Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.

The technology owned by Elon Musk's SpaceX company has played a vital role in government and military connectivity in Ukraine, and increasingly assists in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

World.title: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
World.content:
State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say.

More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau.

"The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman.

This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) from the company.

US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim.

Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software.

According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet.

Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call â except that the audio would appear to malfunction.

A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims.

Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities.

The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user".

"It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday.

"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

World.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
World.content:
Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.

Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast.

The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes.

Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war.

Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast.

The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic.

Defence officials are understood to have stressed to Kyiv that the Gulf is a relatively narrow waterway used by oil tankers and civilian vessels, and is also home to subsea data cables.

Ukraine's SBU described the Russian ship as a Buyan-M type small corvette that carried Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. There were also unconfirmed reports of Russian combat helicopters being destroyed.

Martin Herem, the defence minister of Estonia, which borders the Gulf, told public broadcaster ERR that the ship was hit at about 05:30 (03:30 GMT) on Wednesday but did not say how it was attacked: "We know that smoke came from the ship afterwards. The ship itself went back towards St Petersburg."

The extent of casualties or damage sustained by the Russian navy ship remains unclear, and Moscow rarely gives such details.

World.title: Neither war nor peace in Tigray - is Ethiopia's latest conflict really over?
World.content:
Running a hair salon in Mekelle, capital of Ethiopia's troubled northern Tigray region, is not easy at the moment.

"People can't prioritise beauty over daily basic needs. For many residents, thinking about self-care is a luxury, at a time when they can't feed their kids," Firut Me'ar, who runs a salon in the city, tells the BBC.

After a brief war, the city is under the control of the national army but life is far from normal, says Firut, a single mother of a 10-year-old daughter.

"Things are better than during the war, but people still have no money, no morale. Business is almost non-existent," she says, her voice shaking with emotion.

Above all, she says people are worried about what the future holds. "There is uncertainty about what comes next."

Fighting broke out in late September between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that had run Tigray for decades, and the national army - a resumption of the two-year civil war that officially ended in 2022.

But within less than two weeks, federal forces marched triumphantly into Mekelle. The TPLF made what it called a "strategic withdrawal" from the city and Tigray's other main towns so the army encountered little resistance. Hundreds of people are reported to have died in the conflict, including dozens killed by drone strikes and bombing raids by the air force.

Ethiopian government officials and supporters argue that the war is effectively over and that the only remaining task is to clear Tigray of TPLF elements.

Getachew Reda, a senior TPLF official who switched sides and is now an adviser to the prime minister, declared that the war in Tigray had ended and that stabilising the region should now be the immediate priority.

Cameroon Hudson, an analyst and consultant on African peace and security, says there are various reasons for the TPLF's rapid defeat.

"The TPLF has lost popular support at home. It is fragmented, it does not possess the advanced military technology necessary to match the ENDF [Ethiopian National Defence Forces]," he says. "It has lost many of its generals, strategic thinkers, finest diplomats and fighters, either through defections or arrests. The infighting within the TPLF leadership has caused significant damage."

Abraha Hailezgi, a scholar at Mekelle University, agrees. "The army lacks a clear political vision. In recent years, it has become associated with coercion, abuses, forced recruitment and arbitrary actions. As a result, many people have come to view the TPLF army as an adversary rather than a force acting on their behalf," he says.

Speaking by telephone from an undisclosed location, TPLF spokesperson Mikael Asgedom denies that the group has lost.

Instead, he describes it as a deliberate tactical and strategic retreat. "This is not a defeat," he tells the BBC.

World.title: Suspected bomb hoax threats force fresh evacuations of Italian schools
World.content:
Schools across Italy have received bomb threats for the second day in a row, sparking fresh panic and evacuations.

Some 3,778 schools, from Milan in the north to Sicily in the south, reported similar threats to one that created chaos on Wednesday - even though no explosive devices have been found.

The government has advised schools that "in the absence of concrete evidence beyond the simple receipt of a mass email indicating a danger, buildings must not not be evacuated". Unlike a day earlier, only 77 schools were evacuated on Thursday, authorities say.

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says her government will come up with "sector-specific" advice to help those facing this kind of threat.

Schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland received threats on Wednesday, too. It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.

On Thursday morning, a bomb alert at a Calais rail station delayed international and national train services in northern France.

The latest incidents follow a series of bomb hoaxes last week against airports and airlines in a number of European countries.

Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.

Wednesday's email threat - sent to 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 Italian state schools - was said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan".

Some officials say it originated in Taiwan.

A similar message sent to Italian schools on Thursday, again signed by Mikhail Andropov, is said to have been sent from the account of a teacher in the Philippines whose account is believed to have been hacked.

World.title: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
World.content:
Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said.

After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement.

Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August.

The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking.

Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are looking into civil action.

"Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday.

A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police.

A lawyer for one of the women said she was "devastated" by the police decision.

Jackson Pannam, of Slater and Gordon law firm, added that the move "does not amount to a finding that the incident our client reported did not occur, nor does it diminish the seriousness of what she says happened or its profound impact on her".

John Karantzis from Carbone Lawyers, acting for the other two women, told the ABC his clients were "very disappointed and distressed".

They would "vigorously pursue" a civil action, he said.

"My clients' civil claim is based on a different burden of proof, it is based on the balance of probabilities," he said.

Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me".

"To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued.

The Swans said in a statement that it had been "clear from the outset" that its decision to suspend the players was "separate from the police investigation, and it stands by that decision".

"The Club has commenced a comprehensive examination of its AFL program and is committed to acting on the findings and implementing meaningful change to build an environment that players, staff, members, supporters and corporate partners can be proud of," it said.

Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich told reporters it was "not a day for anyone to really celebrate" and "we're still looking very hard at the programme and understanding where we need to get better".

He said the club would be doing everything to "restore the standards that this club has held for a long period of time".

In a separate statement the AFL acknowledged the police decision and said it reserved the right to investigate should any further relevant information come to light.

World.title: Hegseth awards medal to war memorial guard who reprimanded him and group
World.content:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group at Arlington National Cemetery.

A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet.

In a statement, the Pentagon later announced that Hegseth had given Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier".

Photos shared on the defence secretary's X account showed him presenting the medal to Iglesias.

He was accompanied by others whom the Pentagon identified as members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, which is responsible for holding vigil over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

"We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots," the accompanying text on Hegseth's post reads.

In the video, the army sentinel on duty later identified as Iglesias can be seen stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times."

World.title: Makinde’s campaign group demands probe of Tinubu’s N11.2trn crude oil-backed loans
World.content:
The presidential campaign organisation of Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has called for an open investigation into the federal government’s reported commitment of about 340 million barrels of Nigeria’s future crude oil production to secure loans estimated at N11.2 trillion.

The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of committing future oil revenues to debt obligations without sufficient public disclosure, warning that the arrangements could constrain Nigeria’s finances for years.

In a statement on Thursday, the organisation’s Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, said the reported loans were obtained through four financing arrangements: Project Gazelle, Project Gazelle II, Project Leopard and Project Leopard II.

It demanded that the federal government disclose the identities of the lenders, the amounts borrowed, interest rates, management fees and repayment schedules, as well as the precise volume of crude oil committed under each arrangement.

“President Tinubu should give a public explanation on the loan arrangements,” the organisation said.

It also called for the disclosure of the pricing formula for the crude oil deliveries, the outstanding liabilities being refinanced and the full financial implications of the transactions.

The campaign organisation described the reported arrangements as fiscally reckless, arguing that the government was committing future oil revenues to finance present expenditure without demonstrating corresponding investments in industrial development, infrastructure and improved living standards.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

It warned that fixed repayment obligations could limit Nigeria’s ability to benefit fully from increases in international crude oil prices, potentially reducing future government revenues and restricting the country’s fiscal flexibility.

The organisation also recalled its earlier warning that Mr Tinubu was leading Nigeria towards what it likened to the financial predicament of 19th-century Egypt under Khedive Ismail.

It said excessive foreign borrowing and spending under the Egyptian ruler eventually contributed to British occupation of the country in 1882.

“A nation that repeatedly pledges its future revenues to finance present excesses risks surrendering its economic independence,” the campaign organisation said.

Calls for National Assembly scrutiny

The organisation said the reported borrowing arrangements were particularly concerning amid the economic difficulties facing Nigerians, including hunger, poorly funded public hospitals and deteriorating highways.

It argued that commodity-backed financing arrangements should be subjected to public scrutiny and demonstrate clear economic returns and measurable benefits to citizens.

“We therefore task the National Assembly to subject these financing arrangements to rigorous legislative scrutiny including an open public hearing,” the campaign organisation stated.

It said such a hearing should establish the full extent of Nigeria’s crude oil commitments and assess the implications for Federation Account revenues and the country’s long-term fiscal sustainability.

“Economic success is not measured by borrowing or debt restructuring, but by tangible gains in production, jobs, infrastructure, industry and living standards,” it said.

PREMIUM TIMES reported Thursday how Governor Makinde, who is contesting next year’s presidential election on the platform of the Allied People’s Movement (APM), criticised the handling of the economy by President Bola Tinubu who is seeking reelection as the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress.

Mr Makinde, who will complete his second and final term as governor in May 2027, recalled supporting Mr Tinubu to win the 2023 presidential election. He said he withdrew his support for Mr Tinubu and decided to vie for the presidency himself after being disappointed by the president’s performance.

World.title: COP31: African youths map water challenges in 51 countries, seek greater role in policy decisions
World.content:
Across Africa, communities face growing difficulties accessing reliable drinking water, and the people experiencing these challenges are not always adequately represented in decisions about how to address them.

An initiative by the Green Africa Youth Organisation (GAYO), in partnership with the Children’s Investment Fund Foundation (CIFF), is seeking to change that by documenting young people’s experiences of water insecurity and bringing their proposed solutions into policy discussions.

The initiative, known as the African Youth Water and Climate Engagement Initiative, has reached 51 African countries, with more than 1,200 young people participating in a preliminary survey and over 900 others taking part in consultations across the continent’s five regions.

Baliqees Salaudeen-Ibrahim, GAYO’s Climate Director, disclosed this in an interview with PREMIUM TIMES on the sidelines of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.

She said the research was designed to understand how water challenges affect young people in their communities and to identify solutions they are already developing.

“What we’re trying to understand is what the current water challenges are on the continent of Africa and how young people are responding to this problem,” Ms Salaudeen-Ibrahim said.

According to her, the consultations reinforced concerns raised during the preliminary survey and also highlighted community-based initiatives led by young people.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She said the organisation intends to identify promising practices from the research, mobilise resources for them and explore how successful interventions could be replicated across communities.

The findings are expected to be officially presented at the UN Water Conference in Abu Dhabi in December.

Beyond participation to influence

The initiative comes amid persistent inequalities in access to drinking water across Africa.

The 2025 WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme report found that only 32 per cent of people in sub-Saharan Africa had access to safely managed drinking water in 2024. The disparity was particularly pronounced between rural and urban communities, with coverage at 16 per cent in rural areas and 52 per cent in urban areas.

In Nigeria, the 2024 Demographic and Health Survey found that 71 per cent of the population had access to at least basic drinking water services. However, only 38 per cent of households had water on their premises, while 66 per cent had sufficient quantities when needed.

For Ms Salaudeen-Ibrahim, addressing the challenge requires more than encouraging young people to participate in climate discussions. Governments must also help develop and implement solutions.

According to her, the research was prepared ahead of COP31 so young people’s findings and recommendations could be presented to the conference leadership for consideration.

She added that collaboration with government institutions could help young people navigate administrative barriers, access communities, and hold public authorities accountable for their water-related commitments.

Beyond policy participation, the initiative raises another question: whether community-led water solutions can attract the resources needed to expand their reach.

Ms Salaudeen-Ibrahim said GAYO intends to identify projects that are bankable, scalable and replicable, to mobilise resources to support their implementation.

The financing question

Kate Hampton, Chief Executive Officer of CIFF, said the organisation was interested in bringing the experiences and ideas of children and young people to policymakers.

In an interview with PREMIUM TIMES, Ms Hampton said climate change was disrupting children’s lives through its effects on food security, water security, health and education.

She said the foundation was working with organisations such as GAYO to connect climate change and water-related concerns, while ensuring young people’s experiences and proposed solutions informed policy discussions.

Ms Hampton also described young people as contributors to climate solutions rather than merely participants in discussions about them.

“They have actions that they’re taking in their communities, so we’re trying to show how young people are driving solutions, not just talking about solutions,” she said.

She said the foundation was also looking towards the next climate conference in Ethiopia, where it hoped young people across Africa would have greater opportunities to influence the policy agenda.

While the partnership provides a platform for young people’s ideas, the scale of financing available for the identified projects and the mechanisms for distributing such resources will be important measures of the initiative’s impact.

Government interventions

In Nigeria, water access challenges are particularly relevant as state governments try to expand public water infrastructure amid growing urban populations and pressure on existing facilities.

Bankole Michael, Director of Climate Change and Environmental Planning at the Lagos State Ministry of Environment and Water Resources, said in an interview with PREMIUM TIMES that the state government is rehabilitating waterworks and working with development partners and private-sector organisations to improve water supply and wastewater management.

Mr Michael identified the rehabilitation of the state’s water infrastructure, including the waterworks he mentioned during the interview, as part of efforts to expand access to water.

He also said the Lagos State Water Regulatory Commission was working with water providers to improve sector oversight.

The official acknowledged that population pressures and vandalism remained challenges but said the state was working to improve access to water for residents.

“We are on the road to having solutions to the problems that we have,” he said.

Mr Michael also identified partnerships with WaterAid and other private-sector organisations as part of the state’s efforts to address water and wastewater challenges.

However, he did not provide specific figures on the amount committed to the projects or the number of residents expected to benefit.

Without these figures, it is difficult to assess the scale of the interventions or how quickly they could improve access to reliable water.

From evidence to implementation

The African Youth Water and Climate Engagement Initiative is expected to provide a platform for identifying community-led solutions ahead of the UN Water Conference, scheduled for 8 to 10 December in Abu Dhabi.

The conference is expected to bring governments, development organisations and other stakeholders together to accelerate progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 6, which seeks to ensure access to water and sanitation for all.

For African communities facing water insecurity, however, the significance of the discussions will ultimately depend on whether the evidence gathered translates into practical interventions.

World.title: 2027: Tompolo leads grassroots mobilisation for Tinubu in Jigawa, Zamfara, unveils 56 vehicles
World.content:
The Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, alongside the Jigawa State Governor, Umar Namadi, and Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, have called on voters in the two states to massively support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

They made the call on Thursday during the inauguration of the Jigawa and Zamfara State chapters of the Movement as part of efforts to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and consolidate support for President Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The ceremonies also featured the unveiling of 56 campaign vehicles, comprising 31 vehicles for Jigawa State and 25 for Zamfara State.

Tompolo, who was represented at both inaugurations by the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services, Kestin Pondi, said the Movement was committed to complementing the efforts of the state governments and mobilising widespread support for President Tinubu through direct engagement with residents.

Mr Pondi explained that the vehicles were provided to strengthen the Movement’s operations, ease transportation challenges and enable members to reach more communities with information about the policies and achievements of the Tinubu administration.

He added that governors would control them and deploy them to convey the Movement’s message across the state.

He urged Nigerians to remain patient with the Tinubu administration’s economic reforms, noting that the benefits would take time to reach individual households.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the economy is stabilising, and state governments now have more resources to execute development projects and meet their obligations, including paying workers’ salaries.

Mr Pondi also commended the people of Jigawa State for their massive turnout and show of solidarity during President Tinubu’s recent visit, describing the reception as a demonstration of confidence in the president’s leadership.

He urged them to sustain the support by voting for President Tinubu and Governor Namadi in 2027, insisting that both leaders deserve another four years to consolidate their achievements.

He recalled that Jigawa and Zamfara States were among the states that contributed significantly to President Tinubu’s victory in the last presidential election, urging residents to surpass their previous electoral performance in 2027.

Mr Namadi reaffirmed the state’s commitment to President Tinubu’s re-election, saying the state remained firmly behind the president’s second-term ambition.

The governor thanked the people for their overwhelming turnout during President Tinubu’s recent visit, noting that the president was delighted and appreciative of the massive reception accorded him.

He described the presentation of the 31 campaign vehicles as a significant boost to the Movement’s mobilisation efforts. He urged members to use them judiciously to reach communities across the state.

The governor challenged party supporters to translate their enthusiasm into electoral victory, reminding them of the state’s earlier commitment to deliver two million votes for President Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election.

“Jigawa State is an APC state and a state fully in support of President Tinubu. With your support, Allah will grant our wish,” Mr Namadi said.

In Zamfara, Governor Lawal thanked Tompolo and the Movement for supporting President Tinubu’s re-election campaign and assured the visiting delegation of the state’s commitment to the president.

He urged the Movement’s state leadership to take charge of its operations and assured them of his administration’s support, declaring that Zamfara was for the APC.

Earlier, the National Coordinator of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, Sunday Asuku, commended the people and leadership of both states for their support and commitment to the Movement’s activities.

Mr Asuku thanked Jigawa residents for their overwhelming support for President Tinubu and urged them to translate that solidarity into massive votes in 2027.

He also called on eligible voters to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and participate actively in the forthcoming general elections.

In Zamfara, the National Coordinator commended the state leadership for its work and mobilisation efforts, declaring that Nigeria had the right people in leadership positions at both national and state levels, a situation he described as unprecedented since the return of democracy.

He urged supporters not to be distracted by opposition tactics but to remain focused on mobilising support for President Tinubu and sustaining the Movement’s grassroots engagement ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: ICRC seeks stronger partnership with PREMIUM TIMES on humanitarian reporting
World.content:
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has expressed interest in strengthening its partnership with PREMIUM TIMES to improve humanitarian and conflict reporting in Nigeria, particularly in communities affected by armed conflict and displacement.

The organisation’s delegation proposed this during a visit to the newspaper’s Abuja headquarters on Thursday.

The delegation included Usman Kundili, ICRC communications officer, and Aliyu Dawobe, ICRC public relations officer. They met with Idris Akinbajo, Managing Editor of PREMIUM TIMES; Adeyemi Adesomoju, Deputy Managing Editor; Nike Adebowale-Tambe, Editor of the Health and Development Desk; and Willie Obasi, the newspaper’s Admin Manager.

Speaking during the meeting, Mr Kundili described PREMIUM TIMES as an important media organisation for the ICRC, particularly in its coverage of investigative, conflict and human rights issues.

“For us, PREMIUM TIMES has been a key source and the top media we reference, especially for investigative, conflict and human rights issues,” he said.

He said stronger collaboration would help journalists report more extensively on the humanitarian consequences of conflicts, including displacement, food insecurity, malnutrition, missing persons and restricted access to healthcare.

He also called for increased media attention to the protection of healthcare workers and medical facilities and possible violations of international humanitarian law (IHL).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

ICRC explains humanitarian mandate

Mr Kundili said the ICRC’s mandate derives from the 1949 Geneva Conventions and includes addressing the humanitarian consequences of armed conflicts.

He explained that the organisation works to protect people affected by hostilities, including detainees, displaced persons and people separated from their families.

The ICRC also visits places of detention, particularly in north-eastern Nigeria, to monitor the treatment of detainees and help them maintain contact with their families.

Mr Kundili said the organisation’s neutrality is essential to gaining the trust of parties involved in conflicts and securing access to people in need of assistance.

“Neutrality is what allows us, in fact, to be able to carry out this mandate given to us by all countries, including Nigeria. Our goal is to reach people who need aid, and to do that, we need to talk to both sides,” he said.

He explained that neutrality does not mean indifference to suffering or support for armed groups but enables the ICRC to engage different parties and negotiate humanitarian access.

ICRC’s operations in the north-west

Mr Dawobe said the organisation is providing humanitarian assistance to internally displaced persons and communities affected by prolonged insecurity in north-eastern and north-western Nigeria.

Its interventions include distributing essential and non-food items, promoting hygiene and supporting access to water and other basic services.

He said assistance was not restricted to people living in displacement camps, as the organisation also supported displaced persons living within host communities.

He cited interventions at the Ramunkura camp in Sokoto State, where the ICRC provides non-food items, hygiene promotion services and access to water.

Mr Dawobe said the organisation is expanding its operations in Sokoto and other locations in response to growing humanitarian needs.

He also addressed concerns that humanitarian supplies sometimes find their way into the hands of armed groups, prompting accusations against aid organisations.

He explained that the ICRC engages state and non-state armed actors to promote respect for international humanitarian law, including protecting captured combatants and their fundamental rights.

Mr Dawobe also commended PREMIUM TIMES for its fact-checking reports and efforts to combat misinformation.

“PREMIUM TIMES is one of the leading organisations in fact-checking. We appreciate all your reports and the efforts you put into combating misinformation,” he said.

Promoting transparency

Responding to the proposed partnership, Mr Akinbajo welcomed the planned collaboration, saying the engagement provided useful clarification about the distinct mandates of the ICRC, the Nigerian Red Cross Society and the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

He said the newspaper is open to working with organisations committed to promoting transparency, accountability and a better society.

“Our goal at all times is to ensure that we use the tools to make Nigeria more open, more transparent, and a better country for the majority of the citizens,” he said.

He said PREMIUM TIMES wanted the ICRC to support journalists’ access to conflict-affected communities and internally displaced persons’ camps to obtain first-hand information about humanitarian conditions.

The ICRC delegation said an international humanitarian reporting workshop is scheduled for Abuja from 1 to 3 December, with editors and journalists expected to participate.

World.title: Lee Group’s $1.8b industrial park to create 15,000 jobs, boost Ogun’s manufacturing base — Abiodun
World.content:
Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, has said the $1.8 billion Lee Group First Industrial Park will create about 15,000 direct and indirect jobs, accommodate 29 manufacturing companies and further strengthen the state’s position as Nigeria’s leading industrial destination.

Abiodun stated this on Thursday at the groundbreaking ceremony of the 450-hectare industrial park, describing the investment as a major boost to Ogun’s industrialisation drive and a strong endorsement of the state’s business-friendly environment.

The governor said the project would significantly expand manufacturing activities, stimulate economic growth and create opportunities for thousands of people, particularly young Nigerians.

He noted that the decision by Lee Group to locate its first industrial park in Ogun reflected growing investor confidence in the state’s economic potential, strategic location and expanding infrastructure.

“Your decision to establish this first industrial park in our dear state is a clear demonstration of confidence in our economic potential, our industrial climate and the enormous opportunities that Ogun State offers,” he said.

Abiodun explained that the project’s economic benefits would extend beyond the 29 factories planned for its first phase, creating opportunities for small and medium-scale enterprises involved in logistics, transportation, warehousing, packaging, equipment maintenance, catering, security and construction.

He added that increased industrial activities would stimulate demand for housing, retail businesses, transportation and other essential services, with surrounding communities also benefiting from the investment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, Ogun’s proximity to Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial and financial hub, coupled with access to major domestic and international markets, gives the state a competitive advantage as an investment destination.

“The choice of Ogun State for this investment is neither accidental nor surprising. Our state occupies a strategic position in Nigeria’s economic geography. We share a significant boundary with Lagos, the financial capital of Nigeria, and enjoy close proximity to a major domestic and international market,” he said.

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to providing the infrastructure, policies and business environment required to sustain investments and support industrial expansion.

“Our focus is not simply to attract industries to Ogun State, but to build an interconnected industrial ecosystem where large manufacturers, SMEs, service providers and communities can all benefit from increased economic activities,” he said.

He expressed confidence that the project would attract additional local and foreign investments and consolidate Ogun’s growing reputation as a major manufacturing hub.

In his remarks, the Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, John Enoh, said the Federal Government’s Nigerian Investment Policy was designed to attract domestic and foreign capital, diversify the economy and encourage the development of industrial parks.

He disclosed that the Federal Government would, within the next month, undertake another groundbreaking ceremony in Niger State for a 17,000-hectare integrated sugar farm.

Enoh said investments such as the Lee Group industrial park would help Nigeria move beyond exporting raw materials to producing and exporting finished goods.

“With organisations like the Lee Group, Nigeria will move away from exporting raw materials to producing and exporting finished goods, thereby creating and sustaining millions of jobs,” he said.

He commended Abiodun for creating an environment conducive to investment, describing Ogun as the industrial hub of the country.

Earlier, Chairman of Lee Group of Companies, Sheau Fung Lee, said the project represented another significant milestone in the company’s investment journey in Nigeria, which began in 1962 with the establishment of an enamelware factory in Port Harcourt.

He disclosed that the group, which currently employs approximately 26,000 people, had expanded its operations across several sectors of the economy.

Lee said the new industrial park, valued at $1.8 billion, would occupy 450 hectares and accommodate 29 manufacturing companies, generating approximately 15,000 direct and indirect jobs.

He listed food and beverages, industrial support products, footwear, personal care products, automation and plastics recycling among the sectors expected to operate within the park.

The chairman attributed the investment to the group’s confidence in Nigeria’s market size, population and economic potential, while commending Governor Abiodun for facilitating the project and former President Olusegun Obasanjo for his encouragement and support.

Also speaking, the Akarigbo and Paramount Ruler of Remoland, Oba Babatunde Ajayi, commended the company for choosing Remoland for the investment and assured it of the support of the traditional institution and host communities.

The monarch, however, urged the company to ensure that the host communities enjoyed tangible benefits through employment opportunities, local contracts and corporate social responsibility programmes.

World.title: PREMIUM TIMES journalist, others shine at Global AMR Awards
World.content:
PREMIUM TIMES journalist Mariam Ileyemi has emerged as the third-prize winner in the Nigeria AMR Media Awards (NAMA), recognising her reporting on antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

The NAMA is a national category of the 2026 Global AMR Media Awards (GAMA), which recognises journalists and other media professionals whose work raises awareness of drug-resistant infections and promotes action against the growing public health threat.

The 2026 awards received 382 entries from four global regions, with Africa accounting for 193 submissions. Asia-Pacific followed with 134 entries, while Europe and the Americas recorded 28 and 27 entries, respectively. Nigeria submitted 96 entries for the global and national competitions, representing about a quarter of the total submissions.

Ms Ileyemi was recognised for her report examining the gender dimensions of AMR, including how gender-based violence, social inequalities and barriers to healthcare affect women’s exposure to drug-resistant infections and access to treatment.

In the report, published in March 2026, she highlighted calls by health experts for gender-responsive policies to address antimicrobial resistance.

The recognition adds to her reporting on AMR. In November 2024, she collaborated with Nike Adebowale-Tambe, the PREMIUM TIMES Head of Health and Development Desk, on a special investigation examining the experiences of Nigerians affected by drug-resistant infections and the challenges they face when medicines fail.

In the NAMA category, Kazeem Biriowo of Nigerian Tribune won first prize, while Julian Adetinuyo of News Scope Africa came second.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Seven other journalists received special mentions: Folashade Akpan of the News Agency of Nigeria, Chioma Obinna of Vanguard, Helen Oji Emmanuel of Blueprint, Fatima Saka of DistinctNews, Chinyere Okorafor of Nigeria Health Times, Laide Akinboade of Daily Asset and Odimmegwa John Peter of New Africa Horizon.

The winners in the Nigerian category will receive certificates and cash prizes supported by the Art for Health Initiative, a non-profit organisation.

The awards were announced on 11 November during the Sixth Global Media Forum on AMR, ahead of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week, observed annually from 18 to 24 November.

Nigeria is scheduled to host the Fifth Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR in Abuja from 6 to 8 December 2026. The conference, the first of its kind to be held on African soil, is expected to bring together government representatives and other stakeholders to strengthen global action against antimicrobial resistance.

Other Nigerian winners

Other Nigerian journalists also received recognition in the global award categories.

In the category for reporting on the Fifth High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR, Annabel Nwachukwu of the Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria won first prize, followed by Edward Samuel Ikpete of Voice of Nigeria in second place and Doris Obinna of The Sun in third. Alice Etuka of The Fact Daily received a special mention.

In the People’s Reporting category, Isioma Appiah-Yeboah of Clean Beat Radio won first prize, Racheal Abujah of NAN won second, and Helen Shikanda, a Kenyan, came third. Princess Ekwi-Ajide of the Anambra Broadcasting Service, Smith Nwokocha of Port Harcourt Wakawaka Blog and Chioma Vivian James of True Verdict received special mentions.

Patience Ihejirika of Leadership Newspaper and Benedict Ifeanyi Chukwu of Kaftan TV also received special mentions in the Africa category.

The Global AMR Media Awards are organised by the Global AMR Media Alliance, a network of media professionals working to raise awareness of antimicrobial resistance and promote its visibility within global health security and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

Media coverage of AMR

Speaking after the announcement, Shobha Shukla, chairperson of the Global AMR Media Alliance, congratulated Nigerian journalists and commended Ojoma Akor, founding chairperson of the Nigeria AMR Media Alliance, for highlighting the effects of AMR and strengthening media efforts to address the problem.

Ms Shukla said AMR was not merely a medical or scientific issue but also a societal and development challenge that required action beyond laboratories and hospitals.

“We need an informed public, accountable governments, and responsible practices across human, animal, and environmental health,” she said.

She said the media has the power to connect these issues, amplify the experiences of affected communities and turn public awareness into action.

Ms Shukla urged journalists to move beyond reporting AMR solely as a health news issue and help build public support for responsible antimicrobial use and stronger health systems.

Ms Akor, in her comments, described the inaugural NAMA awards as an important milestone for health and science journalism in Nigeria, noting that AMR had received insufficient attention in newsrooms despite its implications for public health, healthcare delivery, food security and national development.

She said the awards recognised journalism’s role in making an often-unseen public health threat visible, translating complex scientific evidence into accessible information, amplifying the experiences of affected communities and holding institutions accountable.

“As an alliance, we remain committed to building the capacity of journalists, encouraging investigative and solutions-oriented reporting, and ensuring that AMR receives the sustained attention it deserves,” she said.

Chidera Rosecamille Aneke, founder of the Art for Health Initiative, said AMR is one of the organisation’s focal areas and explained that its support for the NAMA awards was intended to encourage innovative storytelling.

“AMR is one of our organisation’s focal areas, and we are glad to support the NAMA awards to push innovative storytelling to communicate AMR in ways the audience can understand,” she said.

She said the initiative works at the intersection of storytelling, media and the arts to promote public understanding and action on critical health issues.

Understanding antimicrobial resistance

Antimicrobial resistance occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites change over time and no longer respond effectively to medicines used to treat infections. This makes infections harder to treat and increases the risk of severe illness and death.

The problem affects human and animal health, food production and the environment, making it a One Health concern.

Nigeria’s National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2024–2028 cites estimates that 64,500 deaths in the country were directly attributable to AMR in 2019, while 263,400 deaths were associated with it. The country has also acknowledged surveillance gaps that make it difficult to establish the full scale of drug-resistant infections.

About Mariam Ileyemi

Mariam Ileyemi is a Nigerian journalist on the Health and Development Desk at PREMIUM TIMES. Her reporting covers antimicrobial resistance, disease prevention, and primary healthcare.

She was named PREMIUM TIMES Reporter of the Year 2025 and is a fellow of the Africa Health Communications Fellowship and Media-EIS Fellowship, among others.

She was recently nominated for the Outstanding Health Investigation Award at the Private Sector Health Alliance of Nigeria (PSHAN) Annual Awards. She is also a recipient of the Mamman Marshall Scholarship for Women in Journalism.

World.title: AHF launches comic book to tackle menstrual stigma among Nigerian girls
World.content:
The AIDS Healthcare Foundation (AHF) Nigeria has launched a 26-page comic magazine titled ‘Amina’s First Flow’ to improve menstrual health education among adolescent girls and address the stigma surrounding menstruation in Nigeria.

The magazine, unveiled on Thursday in Abuja, uses illustrations and relatable stories to explain menstrual hygiene, correct misconceptions, and encourage open conversations about menstruation.

Speaking at the launch, AHF Nigeria’s Senior Advocacy and Marketing Manager, Steve Aborisade, said the initiative was designed to make menstrual health information more accessible and appealing to adolescents and young women.

Mr Aborisade said the stigma associated with menstruation remained a major challenge to menstrual health education, particularly in communities where cultural beliefs discourage open discussions about periods.

“We reckon that the target audience for the comic magazine would find the message in it interesting and easily embrace it for their benefit, and they too can help share the message accordingly,” he said.

Addressing menstrual stigma

Amina’s First Flow highlights some of the challenges girls face in managing menstruation, including limited access to accurate information, harmful cultural beliefs and misconceptions about menstrual health.

It also provides practical guidance on maintaining personal hygiene during menstruation and encourages boys and men to support menstrual health education.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to AHF, menstrual health education is important in addressing the shame and discrimination experienced by girls and young women.

The organisation noted that cultural taboos in some communities prevent girls from discussing menstruation openly, accessing reliable reproductive health information or seeking appropriate care.

It said the comic format was intended to make the information easier for young readers to understand and share with their peers.

Globally, nearly two billion people menstruate, while an estimated 500 million experience period poverty.

Period poverty refers to inadequate access to menstrual products, sanitation facilities, and information needed to manage menstruation safely and with dignity.

Plans for local language versions

The AHF Nigeria Country Programme Director, Echey Ijezie, said the organisation planned to translate the magazine into several Nigerian languages to reach more girls, particularly those who may have difficulty accessing menstrual health information in English.

Mr Ijezie said AHF would also explore collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Education to distribute the publication through educational and community outreach programmes.

“It is imperative to ensure that our target audience is reached in the near future. We would work with the Federal Ministry of Education and explore the outreaches to use them as education and awareness tools,” he said.

He explained that producing the magazine in local languages would help broaden its reach and make the information more accessible to its intended audience.

Government pledges support

Also speaking, the Minister of Women Affairs, Imaan Suleiman-Ibrahim, said the ministry would support AHF’s efforts to improve girls’ welfare and development in Nigeria.

READ ALSO: Experts call for wider adoption of proven health innovations in Nigeria

Mrs Suleiman-Ibrahim, who was represented by Osaro Osa-Jarikre of the Child Development Department, said the ministry intended to incorporate AHF’s programmes into a forthcoming policy initiative.

“Our ministry has resolved to carry the AHF along in the various programmes we have designed for the girl child in Nigeria, and we are also ready to offer needed support to the foundation in its quest to upgrade the Nigerian young generation,” she said.

She described the foundation as an important partner in advancing programmes aimed at improving girls’ wellbeing.

The launch was attended by representatives of civil society organisations, health professionals and youth-focused groups.

Among those present were AHF Nursing Manager Charity Awunor; AHF State Clinical Coordinator Ugochi Ajaero; Binta Suleiman Jalo of the Kids & Teens Resource Centre, Abuja; and Taiwo Ajani of Lawyers Alert.

World.title: EFCC arraigns businessman over alleged £122,000 investment fraud
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned a businessman, Ashley Oshin, over allegations that he obtained £122,000 from two investors under the guise of investing the money in a fund.

Mr Oshin was arraigned on Thursday before the Lagos State High Court in Ikeja on one count of obtaining money by false pretence.

The EFCC alleged that he collected the money from Oluwafemi Fajana and Abiodun Adeogun between 2009 and 2010, promising to invest it in a debenture fund operated by Oschards Limited.

The alleged offence contravenes Section 1(3) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006.

Mr Oshin pleaded not guilty when the charge was read to him before Justice Ismail Ijelu.According to the charge, he promised the investors an annual return of 40 per cent, although he allegedly knew the representation was false.

Prosecution lawyer, M.S. Owede, told the court that the charge was filed on 29 June and requested a date for trial.

He also asked the court to remand the defendant in a correctional centre, explaining that the EFCC detention facility was full and had no available space.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Owede further sought time to respond to the bail application filed by the defence.

Defence lawyer, Samuel Umoren, said he had filed a bail application dated 10 November 2026, which had been served on the prosecution. He urged the court to hear the application and sought an early date.

Mr Umoren also asked the court to remand his client in EFCC custody.
