Mr Ijelu adjourned the case until 18 November for trial and hearing of the bail application.

The judge ordered that Mr Oshin be remanded in a correctional centre pending further proceedings.

The alleged 40 per cent annual return is also relevant to warnings issued by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) about investment schemes promising unusually high returns.

In a November 2023 advisory, the commission urged investors to be wary of schemes offering returns above 20 per cent annually and to verify whether investment operators are registered.

Under Section 1(3) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006, a person convicted of the offence faces between seven and 20 years’ imprisonment.

World.title: Lagos taskforce raids Cele, Itire, Ilasamaja, arrests 3 suspected drug peddlers
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Taskforce has raided suspected criminal hideouts in Cele, Itire, Ilasamaja and other parts of the state, arresting three suspected drug peddlers in an operation aimed at curbing illicit drug activities and other forms of criminality.

The operation was led by the Chairman of the agency, Chief Superintendent of Police (CSP) Adetayo Akerele, who personally supervised the enforcement exercise across locations identified as hotspots for drug-related activities, public disturbances and other criminal tendencies.

During the operation at Itire, Akerele commended the whistleblower and residents for their vigilance and cooperation, saying public participation and timely intelligence-sharing were essential to identifying and dislodging criminal elements from communities.

The taskforce said the operation led to the arrest of three suspects allegedly involved in the sale and distribution of substances, including marijuana, Colorado and Indian hemp, to adults, underage persons and street urchins around Cele Bus Stop, Itire and Ilasamaja.

It added that the activities had reportedly contributed to public disturbances, street fights, cult-related activities, youth violence and other criminal tendencies in the affected communities.

The suspects were identified as Bello Musa, 18; Abubakar Musa, 27, both of No. 23, Adebayo Street, Cele-Ijesha; and Agboola Fuad, 24, of No. 4, Sewage Street, Abaranje, Ijegun, Lagos.

According to the agency, the suspects have been arraigned before a court on three counts bordering on possession and sale of illicit drugs, inciting members of the public against officers performing lawful duties, and conduct likely to cause a breach of the peace.

They all pleaded not guilty to the charges, while the case was adjourned until December 9, 2026, for further proceedings.

Akerele reiterated that active citizen participation, alongside sustained enforcement operations by the taskforce and other relevant security and regulatory agencies, remained essential to maintaining public order, environmental sanitation and lasting peace across the state.

He warned that individuals found engaging in criminal activities or violating applicable environmental laws would be made to face the full weight of the law.

Speaking at the agency’s headquarters in Bolade, Oshodi, the taskforce chairman urged residents to take responsibility for the security of their communities by reporting suspicious activities and cooperating with law enforcement agencies.

He also cautioned young people against involvement in illicit drug activities, street violence and cultism, warning that such conduct could jeopardise their future and undermine the development of their communities.

Akerele further advised residents to be careful about their associations and avoid keeping company with individuals whose activities could expose them to criminality.

He said the Lagos State Government, through the taskforce, remained committed to its zero-tolerance stance against drug peddling, environmental nuisances and criminal activities as part of efforts to build a cleaner, safer and drug-free state.

World.title: Italy stun France 3-1 to hand Zidane first defeat as Les Bleus coach
World.content:
France’s midfielder #14 Adrien Rabiot fights for the ball with Italy’s defender #05 Riccardo Calafiori during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 5 group 1 – football match between Italy and France, at San Siro Stadium in Milan on November 12, 2026. (Photo by Alberto PIZZOLI / AFP)

Italy came from behind to beat France 3-1 in Milan and hand Zidane his first defeat since taking charge of Les Bleus.

France were without Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele due to injury but Michael Olise pounced on a loose pass from Gianluigi Donnarumma to fire them ahead on 10 minutes.

Francesco Pio Esposito steered in Nicolo Cambiaghi’s pass to bring Italy level before France twice hit the post through Bradley Barcola and Rayan Cherki.

Sebastiano Esposito blazed a second-half penalty wide for Italy, but Roberto Mancini’s side did not rue that miss as Davide Frattesi powered home Federico Dimarco’s cut-back.

Francesco Pio Esposito then doubled his tally for the night, succeeding where his older brother had failed by converting a penalty after Dayot Upamecano fouled substitute Antonio Vergara.

Italy climbed above France at the top of Group A1 on head-to-head record. Both teams have 10 points going into the final round of games, with Belgium just one point adrift.

Belgium host Italy on Sunday and France are at home to Turkey.

Turkey slid to a fifth straight loss as they went down 2-1 to Belgium in Izmir.

Arda Guler’s magnificent free-kick put Turkey ahead under new coach and former midfielder Sergen Yalcin, but Belgium struck twice in quick succession with goals from Kevin De Bruyne and Charles De Ketelaere to come away with victory.

World.title: Spain beat Czech Republic to retain perfect Nations League record
World.content:
Spain’s defender #02 Marc Pubill (2L) celebrates after scoring his team’s second goal with team-mates during the UEFA Nations League Group A3 football match between Czech Republic and Spain in Prague on November 12, 2026. Spain won the match 2-0. (Photo by Michal Cizek / AFP)

Alex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat ten-men Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League in Prague on Thursday.

The win leaves Spain unbeaten in 44 competitive games in a row, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season.

Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game.

Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czech midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box.

The Atletico Madrid winger blasted his spot kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it.

Czech captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernandez on a counter-attack.

It was a deja-vu for the Wolverhampton defender who also got a red card at the end of Spain’s 3-1 home win over the Czechs last month.

Pubill, another substitute, beat Kovar with a low shot deep into stoppage time after the Czech back four left him alone facing the Eindhoven goalkeeper.

Luis de la Fuentes missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric Garcia over injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu for the Prague game.

Spain got off to a slow start on the chilly evening but never really let the hosts get close throughout the first half.

They gradually stepped up their pressure, often confining the Czechs to their box and looking for chances.

Fabian Ruiz hit the post with a curling right-footer three minutes from halftime, while Dean Huijsen’s header found Kovar’s arms.

Yeremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half.

The Czechs showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima tipped the ball over the bar from close range on 50 minutes and Adam Hlozek’s glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar.

The Czechs lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar who also denied Fernandez from close range.

The hosts, led by de la Fuente’s long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season.

They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competititon for the next edition.

World.title: Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts
World.content:
Croatia’s midfielder #17 Petar Sucic scores the equalising goal during the UEFA Nations League, League A – Group 3 football match between England and Croatia at Wembley Stadium in London on November 12, 2026. (Photo by Ben Stansall / AFP) / NOT FOR MARKETING OR ADVERTISING USE / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE

Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England appearance with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

Slaven Bilic’s team were determined to avoid the embarrassment of their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kick-off.

But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in their group, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March.

Neither side got out of second gear in the opening stages of the match at Wembley.

Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute and Croatia’s Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half.

Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion following a neat move by the home side.

Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball first time across the area towards Rogers.

Manchester City’s Josko Gvardiol had a chance to clear but got in a tangle and Chelsea’s Rogers poked the ball past goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic.

England started to find some rhythm as they went in search of a second goal but failed to add to their tally before half-time.

Thomas Tuchel’s men were again the more potent team at the beginning of the second period.

But the visitors levelled against the run of play just before the hour mark after a glaring error by England defender Jarell Quansah, who misdirected a header from close range towards Jordan Pickford following a Croatia corner.

The ball fell to Petar Sucic, who stabbed home.

Minutes later England were back in front, with Bayer Leverkusen defender Quansah again at the heart of the action after his shirt was tugged in the penalty area.

Referee Morten Krogh initially did not award a penalty but he was sent to the monitor by the VAR and pointed to the spot.

Kane made no mistake, drilling home for record-extending 92nd England goal.

Nikola Vlasic gave England a scare, firing just wide of Jordan Pickford’s goal as Croatia showed they were still alive.

James Garner thought he had scored a third for England after a Bellingham cut-back but Bellingham was in an off-side position when he received the ball.

Ballon d’Or winner Kane won his 126th cap when the game kicked off — taking him clear of his tie with former goalkeeper Peter Shilton.

A giant banner was raised before kick-off with a picture of the 33-year-old and the words “England’s Finest”.

Shilton was part of a pre-match presentation to honour the Three Lions skipper, along with Football Association patron Prince William.

England remain second in Nations League Group A3, after leaders Spain beat the Czech Republic 2-0 but are now assured of a place in the quarter-finals.

Spain and England face each other in Madrid on Sunday.

World.title: Online safety concerns are reshaping how people meet strangers
World.content:
It’s hard to ignore how meeting new people online has changed in the past decade. With so many platforms connecting millions, the possibilities feel endless, but the risks have become more visible too.

Stories about scams, harassment, and data breaches are everywhere, and they’ve made people think twice before reaching out to someone they don’t know. Safety concerns aren’t just in the background anymore—they’re shaping the way we start conversations, choose platforms, and decide how much to share.

As awareness grows, so do new habits and expectations for digital introductions. This shift doesn’t just affect individuals; it’s influencing whole communities as we all adapt to a more cautious, connected world.

Changing first steps: why some users now engage with strangers differently online

That growing caution is easy to spot in the way people now approach first interactions with strangers online.

Instead of jumping right into open conversations, many start by looking for platforms that let them control who they talk to, or give them the option to remain anonymous until they feel comfortable.

Features like one-click exit buttons, video previews, or private chat rooms have become popular for exactly this reason.

Women, in particular, are leading this change. They’re more likely to say safety is a top concern, which shows up in everything from avoiding certain apps to using aliases or insisting on in-app messaging only.

The choice of platform matters too. Video chat sites, for example, offer a sense of control because users can see and hear who they’re talking to—and can leave the conversation instantly if something doesn’t feel right.

For many, getting to know LuckyCrush and similar services is part of this shift toward safer, more controlled first steps when meeting someone new.

It’s a sign that concerns are not stopping people from connecting, but are changing the rules for how those first moments happen.

a shift in trust: navigating caution in the age of digital introductions

That change in first steps is really about trust—how it’s built, how it’s lost, and why it matters so much now. People aren’t just jumping into conversations and sharing details the way they might have a decade ago.

Instead, there’s this sense of needing to pause and check for warning signs. With more stories surfacing about online fraud and harassment, it feels riskier to let your guard down. A lot of users now watch for inconsistent stories, pressure to move chats off-platform, or requests for private information as red flags that something isn’t right.

Some of the ways people protect themselves include sticking to messaging within the app, looking for verification badges, or even googling someone before agreeing to meet. These habits are becoming more common, especially as platforms roll out tools designed for safer interactions.

The numbers back up this shift in attitude. In 2023, just under half of U.S. adults said they felt online dating was safe, down from a few years before. Women, in particular, tend to feel more uneasy about sharing personal details, which lines up with reports of higher rates of harassment.

For anyone wanting to understand why trust is changing, the Pew Research on online dating safety is a helpful resource. It highlights how both optimism and skepticism shape the way people meet and interact online now.

Safety in practice: behaviors and community responses on Nigerian social platforms

That skepticism and caution show up in everyday choices for users in Nigeria too. The reality of scams and harmful encounters is hard to ignore, so both individuals and communities have started to change how they approach online connections.

People are much more likely to double-check who they’re chatting with, sometimes even asking for proof of identity before sharing anything personal. It’s now common for users to avoid giving out phone numbers or addresses until they’ve built enough trust within the platform’s chat feature.

Platforms play a role by offering safety tools, but users often take things further by joining moderated groups or relying on word-of-mouth warnings. These groups work together to flag suspicious behavior and alert others, building a sense of collective vigilance that can help everyone feel a little safer.

Community-driven warnings have become especially important after a series of incidents have made headlines. Stories like Rivers Police nab kidnappers serve as stark reminders that online risks have real-life consequences, motivating even more caution among regular users.

The combination of individual caution and group action is changing the culture of meeting strangers online in Nigeria. People are still eager to connect, but staying safe is now a shared priority, not just a personal one.

Looking ahead: the enduring tension between connection and caution

This shift toward community vigilance hasn’t erased the basic human urge to connect online. People still want to meet, form friendships, and build relationships across digital spaces, even as they weigh the risks involved.

The real challenge now is finding a balance between openness and caution. Many users are adapting by taking advantage of improved verification processes, using reporting tools, and staying informed about possible threats. These steps aren’t just about individual safety—they’re shaping the culture of online interaction overall.

Platforms are also responding to these pressures. High-profile actions like WhatsApp bans scam accounts show that companies are working to remove bad actors and create safer environments. These crackdowns send a message that security isn’t optional, but a shared responsibility between users and service providers.

Even with new tools and policies, the tension between wanting to connect and needing to protect yourself is likely to stay. Ongoing education, clear safety features, and active moderation will remain important as the way we meet strangers online continues to evolve.

World.title: UNN Deaths: Gov Mbah mourns, orders investigation
World.content:
Governor of Enugu State, Dr Peter Mbah, has expressed deep grief over the deaths of four students of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, UNN, who reportedly died during an off-campus sign-out party organised for one of their friends, describing the incident as a heartbreaking loss.



Mbah described the deaths as a grievous loss, not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to Enugu State as a whole.

He called for a ban on sign-out parties among undergraduates, noting that the practice had brought too much sorrow to families and tertiary institutions across the country.



This was contained in a press statement issued by the governor’s media aide, Mazi Uche Anichukwu, on Thursday.



“I received with rude shock and deep sense of loss the news of the off-campus sign-out party leading to the death of four students of the University of Nigeria Nsukka, and hospitalisation of six others.



“This is a grievous loss not only to the immediate families of the deceased and the university, but also to us as a state. Losing them in their prime and along with their promising future cuts as deeply as a sharp knife. We, therefore share in this grief and pray God to grant their families, friends, and the UNN community the equanimity to bear the heartbreaking loss.



“Our hearts go out to their parents in particular, who sacrificed personal comforts to sponsor their children through the university, but only to face this sad turn of events.



“As a government, we have ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding their deaths and will work closely with the university authorities and security agencies to get to the roots of the sad development and forestall a recurrence.



“In the meantime, I have suspended my scheduled town hall meeting with the UNN community on Friday, November 13, 2026, as we join the university in mourning the dead.



“Going forward, we will work with the authorities of tertiary institutions to enforce a full ban on sign-out parties and other excessive celebrations, a trend that has cost more lives and brought more sorrows than joy to families and higher institutions of learning,” the governor stated.



Mbah also called for increased public enlightenment campaigns by relevant agencies and institutions on the consequences of drug use and abuse.



He prayed for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased.

World.title: 2027: ‘Arrest perpetrators’, Senate condemns political violence nationwide
World.content:
Senate

By Henry Umoru

AHEAD of 2027 Presidential and general elections, the Senate has condemned in very strong terms, cases of political violence, attacks and disruption of political activities across the country.

The Senate has thus taken a swipe at acts of violence, intimidation, assault and destruction of property associated with political rallies, meetings, processions and other lawful political activities, irrespective of the political parties or individuals affected.

The Senate has urged the security agents to as a matter of urgency apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act in order to serve as deterrent to others.

The Upper Chamber has called on all political parties, candidates and their supporters to reject inflammatory rhetoric, discourage violence and cooperate with security agencies in maintaining public peace.

Speaking with Vanguard yesterday, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Media and Public Affairs, Senator Yemi Adaramodu, APC, Ekiti South, said, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is preaching peace and national harmony, the National Assembly is in support of Mr President on this.

“We thus condemn in totality any act of political violence and urge the security agents to apprehend whoever is culpable in such heinous act.”

Vanguard News

World.title: NSIB: Aircraft door that fell off Abuja-Lagos flight had all locks open
World.content:
By Folarin Kehinde

The Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) has disclosed that all locking mechanisms of the passenger-cabin door that detached from a Bombardier Challenger 604 aircraft mid-air during an Abuja-Lagos flight were found in the open position after the incident.

The Bureau also disclosed on its website that the aircraft’s door indicator displayed an ‘UNLOCKED/RED’ warning, while both the internal and external door handles were found in the open position.

These findings were contained in the preliminary investigation report released by the NSIB on November 11, following the October 15 incident involving an aircraft operated by Triton Aviation Limited.

The aircraft, with registration number T7-SEI and operating as flight DWC052, was carrying nine persons, comprising two pilots, one cabin crew member and six passengers, when its passenger-crew door detached during initial climb after take-off from the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja.

Interestingly, the flight crew told investigators that they did not receive any aural or visual door warning before the door separated from the aircraft.

The bureau further disclosed that no door-related faults or warnings were recorded in the aircraft’s downloaded Maintenance Diagnostic Computer (MDC) data.

According to the report, the incident occurred at approximately 5:19 p.m. when the flight crew observed an abnormal increase in cabin altitude and suspected a pressurisation problem.

The captain subsequently instructed the cabin crew to double-check the main cabin door by pushing and pulling it.

However, the cabin crew member told investigators that as she approached the passenger-crew door, it opened without her touching it.

Some passengers also reportedly said they could not recall seeing the cabin crew member touch the door.

The door subsequently detached from the aircraft and struck its lower fuselage, damaging a VHF antenna.

Following the occurrence, the captain took over control of the aircraft while the first officer assumed pilot-monitoring duties.

The pilots declared an emergency and coordinated with Abuja Air Traffic Control for an immediate return to the airport.

The aircraft eventually landed safely on Runway 22 at approximately 5:34 p.m., with all nine occupants disembarking without injuries.

The report also revealed that during the final approach, the pilot monitoring unfastened his seat belt and attempted to close the passenger-crew door by pressing the DOOR CLOSE button.

The detached door was subsequently recovered from a cornfield in Gui Village, Abuja Municipal Area Council, approximately five miles southwest of the airport.

Meanwhile, the NSIB said further investigations would focus on determining whether structural or mechanical failure contributed to the door separation.

It listed metallurgical testing and detailed examination of the detached door, its associated assemblies and locking mechanisms among the next investigative steps.

Investigators will also conduct detailed analysis of the Flight Data Recorder (FDR), particularly the passenger-crew door warning and indication parameters.

The Bureau said the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) would also undergo further analysis, including spectral examination of a recorded mechanical clicking sound to establish its source.

Other areas of investigation include examination of the door-warning and indication system, associated electrical circuits and their functionality at the time of the occurrence.

The NSIB, however, cautioned that the preliminary report contains factual information and initial findings only, stressing that it does not establish the causes or contributing factors responsible for the incident.

It said the final report, containing the investigation’s analysis, conclusions and further safety recommendations, would be published upon completion of the investigation in accordance with Annex 13 of the Convention on International Civil Aviation.

World.title: NIMASA, China MSA Sign Memorandum of Understanding on Maritime Cooperation
World.content:
Eromosele Abiodun

The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), and China Maritime Safety Administration, China MSA have strengthened bilateral maritime relations with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Maritime Cooperation in Shanghai, People’s Republic of China.

The MoU establishes a framework for cooperation in six key areas: maritime safety and navigation, marine environmental protection, seafarer training, certification and rights protection, marine casualty and incident investigation, maritime transportation facilitation, and maritime security.

Speaking at the signing ceremony held at the Shanghai Seafarers Assessment Model Centre, Director General of NIMASA, Dr. Dayo Mobereola, described the agreement as a historic milestone in the relationship between both countries, stressing the need to translate the MoU into practical programmes and tangible benefits for their respective maritime sector.

“This Memorandum of Understanding represents more than a formal agreement; it is a commitment to translate our longstanding relationship into practical maritime cooperation, shared expertise and measurable benefits for both countries. We are determined to ensure that this partnership delivers tangible outcomes for our maritime industries,”Mobereola stated.

Mobereola further stated that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, values Nigeria’s longstanding relationship with China and is committed to deepening bilateral cooperation, particularly in the maritime sector, in line with the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda and the objectives of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, under the Leadership of Adegboyega Oyetola.

On his part, the Director General of China MSA, Mr. Xu Wei, reaffirmed China’s commitment to strengthening maritime cooperation with Nigeria, noting the country’s interest in Nigeria’s maritime development and commendable progress in the sector. He pledged China’s continued support towards advancing bilateral collaboration and promoting sustainable growth in both countries’ maritime industries.

The agreement is expected to facilitate technical cooperation, knowledge-sharing, capacity development and the exchange of best practices, while strengthening institutional collaboration between NIMASA and China MSA.

The signing marks a significant step towards deepening Nigeria-China maritime cooperation and advancing the development of Nigeria’s maritime industry.

World.title: Stakeholders: NAMA Can Earn $1.5bn Revenue Annually with Improved Infrastructure
World.content:
Chinedu Eze

Aviation industry stakeholders are of the view that the Nigerian Airspace Management Agency (NAMA) can scale up its revenue from overfliers to $1.5 billion annually if it improves its airspace infrastructure to boost radar and communications coverage of the nation’s skies.

In aviation, overfliers (also called overflights) are aircraft that fly through a country’s sovereign airspace without taking off from or landing within that country.

Currently, NAMA earns about 50 per cent of the projected $1.5 billion annual revenue due to inadequate coverage of the airspace occasioned by ageing equipment, even though overflight charges form the bulk of NAMA’s self-generated revenue.

Insider source revealed that NAMA’s actual total revenue and remittances, such as clearing house figures handled via the International Air Transport Association (IATA), have historically fallen vastly short of such high figures, often collecting only a fraction of what is needed to cover multi-billion naira operational and personnel overheads (which crossed over N43 billion annually).

NAMA collects between $75 and $195 per flight for regional and international overfliers and overflight, en-route, and terminal navigation fees collectively make up roughly 75 per cent of NAMA’s total income, while the statutory Ticket Sales Charge (TSC) accounts for the remaining 25 per cent.

Speaking at the 55th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the Nigerian Air Traffic Controllers’ Association (NATCA) in Lagos, the stakeholders said there was urgent need to upgrade ageing communication equipment, complete on-going projects and also train key personnel to man the equipment.

They said that despite promises from NAMA management, little or none was seen being done.

President of NATCA, Edino Ilemona Amos, expressed frustration that despite numerous procurement announcements and regulatory approvals by the government, controllers on the frontlines continued to operate with inadequate equipment.

“Despite the considerable challenges faced by members across the length and breadth of the country, there has been no significant improvement in our communication and surveillance infrastructure. We acknowledge the approvals and procurement milestones that have been announced. However, these are yet to translate into a material improvement in the equipment available to controllers at the console,” Amos said.

He President revealed that persistent equipment failures have pushed the association to its breaking point.

He said, “It is with a deep sense of responsibility that I state that this frustrating engagement is pushing the association towards considering the withdrawal of our services, should there be no clear strategic plan for the total overhaul of communication and surveillance infrastructure in Nigeria,” Amos warned, clarifying that the call is made not as a threat, but as “patriots who sit daily before screens and failing frequencies to keep this country safe.”

“For NAMA to improve communication in the airspace, it needs the installation and factory testing of new Very High Omnidirectional Radios Range (VHF) voice communication and control systems across 14 operational sites to streamline air-to-ground communication. It also needs extended Very High Frequency (E-VHF) Radio System. So, there is need for a nation rollout of E-VHF systems (previously deployed in northern stations like Abuja and Kano) to eliminate airspace communication blind spots,” the stakeholders said.

They added, “NAMA needs Voice Communication and Control Systems (VCCS), which is upgrading regional voice switching and localised emergency power integrations to maintain continuous communication windows. To enhance communication and radar coverage across Nigeria’s airspace, NAMA and the federal government however said they were upgrading and procuring specific critical systems, which includes the Total Radar Coverage of Nigeria (TRACON) alternative.

“This needs comprehensive overhaul and modernisation of the nine-station primary and secondary surveillance radar network to replace aging components, clear out-of-date software, and resolve the lack of spare parts. NAMA is also working on Automatic Dependence Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) equipment and the deployment of ADS-Btechnology as a vital modern surveillance backup to significantly improve tracking accuracy, reliability, and signal processing across regional radar gaps.”

However, it was learnt that the agency has indicated strong plan to replace TRACON.

“It has made firm move to acquire Indra radar Sistemas Radar Systems from Spain. While some staff members of NAMA argued that TRACON could be upgraded with modern software equipment, the management disagreed, “an official of the agency told THISDAY THISDAY adding that TRACON has been there since 2010 and that it has become outmoded.

“You may continue to upgrade these systems but there will come a time when you will have to change everything completely. This is because we have to move on with other jurisdictions. Aviation is global; we cannot afford to be left behind,” the official said.

NAMA has in the past 10 years, embarked on the automation of Aeronautical Information Service (AIS), which provides information necessary for the safety, regularity and efficiency of international air navigation.

The Air Traffic Controllers said the services provided by AIS were invaluable and include flight information service like the traffic information, meteorological information, information on runway state (condition) and other information useful for the safe and efficient conduct of flight.

“It is also the channel for dissemination of information on weather and weather report, among others. Some years ago, hopes were raised that the project would be completed but it has not till date. In 2023, NAMA claimed it had put to an end the perennial problem of communication in Nigeria’s airspace as it had put things in place to complete the project,” they added.

Reacting to the demand of Air Traffic Controllers, the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, said: “The Total Radar Coverage of Nigeria system has outlived its design life, and Mr. President has approved its overhaul. While that work continues, NAMA has begun deploying ADS-B as a surveillance backup. New VHF radios and voice communication and control systems for fourteen sites have passed factory acceptance testing in Norway. In Abuja, work has begun on a new NAMA headquarters and Air Traffic Management Centre, which will bring the Lagos and Kano Area Control Centres under one roof.”

Industry stakeholders however said that if critical equipment were provided, the Nigerian airspace would have effective communication, navigation and surveillance system that would enable NAMA to boost its revenue, especially from overflights.

World.title: Cost of Living Crisis: America, Europe and Nigeria
World.content:
Pope Leo to Donald Trump “Woe to those who manipulate religion and the very name of God for their own military, economic or political gain”

Beyond Nigeria, there are people and institutions whose fortunes I follow with an emotional investment that defies explanation. Roger Federer was one. No one ever wielded the tennis racket with such skill and aplomb. Arsenal Football Club is another. A Federer victory could brighten my day; Arsenal defeat could spoil it. Such attachments are harmless enough in sport. In politics, they invite a sterner reckoning. Barack Obama inspired a different kind of investment. His election offered the exhilarating possibility that America might, at last, begin to outgrow the racial poison that has accompanied it from its founding.

Eight years later, in a cruel twist of irony, fate dealt America, a supreme antithesis of Obama with the election of Donald Trump as American president. In its recurrent flirtation with the politics of hate, racism, misogyny and white nationalism, the Republican party played John the Baptist to the arrival of Trump. He was the logical consummation of a trend that was set in motion by the dog whistle of his Republican forebears. It was from the ranks of the party I first learnt the espousal of the cruel misogyny “doctrine’ of legitimate rape’. Meaning you must always have your way with your spouse regardless of her feelings.

Trump was a gifted dissembler who gainfully pandered to the raucous glee of the Republican party base in search of their 21st century McCarthy. No one needs to believe in conspiracy theories to share the concern about his fidelity to his sworn oath of office where Vladimir Putin is concerned. If the latter ever wished for a corrosive and polarising agent in America and the Western democracies, he could not have gotten a better client than the American president. James Carvile was on a CNN Smerconish show the other day, lamenting that Trump was a traitor and if he wasn’t, then he was surely behaving like one. As the wit goes, “If it looks like a duck, walks like a duck, and quacks like a duck, it’s probably a duck”.

Let us dispense with the polite fiction that Trump is merely a politician with an abrasive manner. He recognised the resentment provoked by Obama’s presidency and made himself its political beneficiary. His birther campaign was a racist lie, sustained for years in the service of one message: that a Black president could be made to seem foreign in the country whose people had elected him. It was an assault not just on Obama but on the idea that Black citizenship could ever be accepted without qualification.

If, as some have noted, Trump’s rise to the presidency was a racist backlash against the emergence of Obama, his recent repudiation in the mid term American elections was no less a counter backlash (to this backlash) in which America rediscovered the legitimacy and utility of its diversity.

America will, for long, replay the iconic scenario of the election of Keisha Lance Bottoms as the first black female governor (of Georgia) in American history coupled with the simultaneous election of seven other African American ladies to high executive offices in the state. There was the unprecedented election of a Latino lady as governor of Texas, four black governors, an elected Muslim to the Senate and another elected black Senator ever from the state of Mississippi. To Trump belongs the credit of helping to categorically clarify the choice before the American electorate with the subtlety of epic fury.

So profound was the danger he posed to society that Pope Leo had to insinuate himself into the election (and broke with the papal tradition of political abstinence) to exercise his civic responsibility to vote, leaving his fans and followers to second guess his preference and take a cue therefrom.

Europe presents its own warning. Rising costs of food, energy and housing have put intolerable pressure on households that did what they were told to do: work, pay their bills and expect a modest degree of security in return. When that bargain fails, the far right arrives with its well-rehearsed list of culprits. The migrant is blamed for the housing shortage; the foreigner for the wage packet that no longer stretches far enough. It is easier to find a vulnerable person to accuse than to repair an economy.

For a number of years now, Nigeria has been grappling with a similar cost of living crisis which has occasioned sporadic street protests and demonstrations. With the 2027 general elections in view, a standard bearer of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, Prince Justice Faloye has attributed the Nigerian instance to the adoption and pursuit of Neo Liberal economics policy.

“2027 Presidential elections feels like a death sentence when one realizes that the three major contenders all support Neoliberalism, the political and economic ideology behind Nigerians’ poverty and underdevelopment ever since the former head of State, General Obasanjo started with the removal of education subsidies. Since then, subsidy removals, devaluation and privatization has pushed two third of Nigerians into poverty, lowered infant mortality and life expectancy, as neoliberalism policies continued to kill the common citizens”.

The removal of the petrol subsidy and the liberalisation of the foreign-exchange market have brought immediate pain. Any supporter of these policies who cannot say so plainly has forfeited the right to ask Nigerians for patience.

Nonetheless, while accepting the premise that the most vulnerable segment of the population deserve concomitant mitigation measures to cushion the hardships attendant on the policy deployment, I will argue that these neo liberal policies reserve the potential to set the political economy of Nigeria on the path of progress and development consistently pursued. At the root of the free market philosophy is the ethic of a positive correlation between productivity and reward otherwise understood as the work ethic. Subversive of the work ethic is the resource curse and the rentier economy syndrome within which Nigeria has been mired for the better part of its post colonial existence. The underlying logic of the syndrome is that you do not need to work to make money.

I do not intend to reopen the redundant debate on doctrinaire political ideology (a subject) to which I lay no exemplary expertise or originality. I claim no more than the indulgence to speculate on the merits of the specific macro economic stability measures that the present government has doggedly embarked on for the past three years namely the twin policies of the floatation of the naira and the removal of the oil subsidy. Both measures are predicated on market efficiency and they have been efficient in stabilising the Nigerian economy.

I have long argued for constitutional reform, particularly decentralisation and the devolution of powers. Too much of our national life depends on access to the centre. Even before that deeper reform is achieved, we can insist on economic rules that diminish the power of patrons and gatekeepers. A Nigerian should not have to know the right person to obtain an opportunity that ought to be available by right.

In this regard, those measures constitute a unifying instrument. No section is more favoured than the other. As we gradually reduce the areas in which the discretionary power of the government is reduced the more cohesive and coherent the society becomes. I know of no government in ancient and modern history (other than that of the delinquent Jewish king, Rehoboam) which purports to impose pain and distress on the people as an instrument of governance. If these are the inevitable consequences of a policy in the short term, then they must be measured against the objectives they are intended to serve.

This is why I resist the suggestion that our choice is between compassion and reform. We need both. Preserving a system of privilege because dismantling it hurts the poor is not compassion. Dismantling it while leaving the poor to absorb the shock is not justice. In a discussion about the alleged lack of patronage for the Yoruba, my principal observed that the better service would be a level playing field on which any Nigerian could earn an income without let or hindrance. I agree. The objective should not be to secure a more generous patron for our own people. It should be to build a country in which patronage matters less to everybody.

World.title: WPRF2026: A Global PR Forum In Africa, But Where Is Africa’s Voice?
World.content:
Guest Columnist By Adetokunbo Modupe

As Nigeria prepares to host the world’s public relations community, the opportunity goes beyond global recognition. It is about reclaiming Africa’s narrative and challenging longstanding stereotypes.

From November 15 to 21, 2026, Nigeria will welcome public relations professionals, communication leaders and reputation management experts from across the world for the World Public Relations Forum (WPRF2026) at the Transcorp Hilton Hotel, Abuja.

Hosted by the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR), in partnership with the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, the forum represents a significant milestone for Nigeria’s public relations industry and Africa’s growing relevance in global strategic communication.

NIPR’s leadership, particularly its President, Dr Ike Neliaku, deserves commendation for bringing this prestigious gathering to Nigeria. His leadership has significantly elevated the visibility, ambition, and international relevance of Nigerian public relations.

Beyond professional recognition, WPRF2026 offers Nigeria an invaluable opportunity for national reputation management.

International delegates experiencing Abuja firsthand, interacting with Nigerians and discovering our hospitality and cultural richness, could become informal ambassadors for the country.

Their experiences may challenge longstanding perceptions of Nigeria as an unsafe or unstable destination.

After all, national reputation is not built through government pronouncements alone. It is shaped by lived experiences, credible endorsements and the stories people tell after encountering a country.

But there is a bigger question.

WHY IS AFRICA NOT THE CENTRAL CONVERSATION?

The theme of WPRF2026, “Responsible Communication: The Voice of the World,” is undoubtedly relevant to contemporary global communication challenges.

However, I find it curious that a global reputation management event hosted on African soil would adopt a theme that does not explicitly place Africa’s communication challenges, opportunities and aspirations at the centre of its agenda.

Admittedly, the programme includes an Africa-focused day on November 19, themed “Africa, the Voice of the World.” This is commendable and demonstrates recognition of the continent’s strategic relevance.

But there is a fundamental difference between giving Africa a place on the programme and giving Africa a central place in the conversation.

Africa should not merely be a geographical host or thematic component of a global PR gathering. Its longstanding reputation challenges, narrative inequalities and enormous communication opportunities deserve to influence the forum’s overarching direction and outcomes.

Perhaps no continent has endured more persistent stereotyping, misrepresentation and externally constructed narratives than Africa.

For generations, Africa’s international image has been disproportionately shaped by stories of conflict, poverty, disease, corruption and political instability.

These challenges exist, but they do not represent the full African experience.

Africa is equally a continent of innovation, entrepreneurship, cultural influence, intellectual excellence and extraordinary human resilience.

Yet these stories frequently struggle for comparable visibility within global information systems.

If any continent urgently needs a coordinated reputation repositioning conversation, surely it is Africa.

RESPONSIBLE COMMUNICATION MUST INCLUDE RESPONSIBLE LISTENING

The responsibility for Africa’s reputation does not rest exclusively with African governments, institutions or communication professionals.

International media organisations, global corporations, development institutions and influential commentators also have responsibilities in how they frame and communicate African realities.

Responsible communication should extend beyond truthful storytelling to fair representation, contextual accuracy and the willingness to challenge inherited prejudices.

More importantly, it must include responsible listening.

Africa does not merely need the opportunity to speak. The world must also demonstrate a willingness to listen without predetermined conclusions.

Imagine a global declaration on responsible communication about Africa, developed in Abuja and supported by communication professionals across continents.

Imagine practical commitments to balanced reporting, ethical representation, stronger African participation in global narrative development and measurable collaboration between African and international PR institutions.

Such outcomes could give WPRF2026 an enduring identity beyond speeches, networking sessions and ceremonial declarations.

BEYOND A SUCCESSFUL EVENT TO AN AFRICAN LEGACY

Nigeria’s hosting of WPRF2026 deserves celebration. However, successful event management must not become the ultimate measure of its impact.

Global conferences often produce inspiring conversations without translating their resolutions into meaningful institutional action.

The NIPR and its global partners have an opportunity to establish an African reputation agenda that outlives the conference itself.

An Abuja Declaration on Responsible Communication and Africa’s Reputation, supported by continuing dialogue and measurable commitments, could become a defining legacy.

Such an initiative would not diminish the forum’s global character. Rather, it would give its global theme compelling African relevance.

The world is coming to Nigeria. That alone is an achievement.

But the greater achievement would be ensuring that the world leaves Abuja with a deeper understanding of Africa and a renewed responsibility for how its stories are told.

Africa must not simply provide the venue for the world’s conversation about responsible communication. It must help define that conversation, influence its conclusions and shape its enduring legacy.

Let Abuja 2026 be remembered not merely as the year Africa hosted the world’s PR community, but as the moment the world began listening to Africa differently.

•Adetokunbo Modupe is the founder/Chief Consultant, TPT International Limited

World.title: Abraham Otti: Turning Wealth into a Tool for Humanity and Community Development
World.content:
Chief Abraham Ikechukwu Otti, popularly known as Mighty-Mighty, is a Nigerian billionaire businessman, oil and gas merchant, entrepreneur and philanthropist whose commitment to humanity extends beyond business success. Through Allied Victory Nigeria Limited and several humanitarian interventions, including providing furnished homes for 10 indigent widows, installing solar-powered street lights and supporting education and empowerment initiatives, the Ikenga Umuchu title holder has continued to demonstrate his passion for community development and service to humanity. Bukola Lasisi writes

In a society where success is often measured by wealth, influence and business accomplishments, Chief Abraham Ikechukwu Otti stands out for his efforts to translate personal prosperity into meaningful contributions to humanity.

Popularly known as Mighty-Mighty, Otti is an entrepreneur and oil and gas merchant who has established himself in Nigeria’s business community. An illustrious son of Umuchu in Aguata Local Government Area of Anambra State, he holds the traditional title of Ikenga Umuchu, reflecting his standing and contributions to his community.

As founder of Allied Victory Nigeria Limited, he has built business interests around developing sustainable enterprises, particularly in the oil and gas sector. However, his activities outside the business environment reveal another dimension of his pursuits: a commitment to improving the welfare of people, especially those in his immediate community.

For Otti, wealth carries responsibilities, and success should create opportunities to improve the living conditions of others.

A Commitment to Community Development

Otti’s contributions to his community span road infrastructure, street lighting, educational support, empowerment programmes, financial assistance and the distribution of palliatives to individuals and families facing economic difficulties.

One of his notable interventions is the installation of solar-powered street lights from Ibubu Junction to different parts of Achalla Village.

The project has helped illuminate roads and streets, improving visibility and providing residents with a greater sense of security, particularly at night. It also creates a more conducive environment for social and economic activities.

In communities where inadequate public infrastructure remains a challenge, access to reliable street lighting can make a practical difference to everyday life.

The initiative reflects Otti’s understanding that community development involves addressing basic needs and supporting projects that directly benefit residents. It also demonstrates how private individuals can complement government efforts through targeted interventions.

Providing Homes for 10 Indigent Widows

Perhaps one of the most significant expressions of Otti’s humanitarian commitment is his provision of homes for 10 indigent widows.

In an intervention aimed at supporting vulnerable members of society, he provided, furnished and handed over homes to the beneficiaries.

For widows dealing with the emotional and financial difficulties that often accompany the loss of their spouses, securing decent accommodation can be a major challenge. By providing fully furnished homes, Otti sought to address not only their housing needs but also the comfort and dignity that come with having a secure place to live.

The intervention goes beyond a symbolic gesture. A home provides security, stability and a foundation from which individuals and families can rebuild their lives.

At a time when many Nigerians struggle to meet basic needs, the initiative highlights the role philanthropy can play in supporting people who may otherwise be overlooked.

It also demonstrates the importance of directing resources towards interventions that have lasting benefits for beneficiaries.

Empowerment, Education and Humanitarian Support

Otti’s philanthropic activities also extend to education, individual empowerment, cash donations and the distribution of palliatives.

His educational support reflects an appreciation of the role education plays in building individuals and communities. By assisting people who may struggle to pursue their academic aspirations, such interventions contribute to opportunities for future generations.

His empowerment initiatives similarly recognise the importance of helping individuals improve their economic circumstances.

Beyond these programmes, he has continued to provide financial assistance and palliatives to individuals and families experiencing hardship.

These interventions form part of a broader approach to philanthropy that combines immediate assistance with support for community infrastructure and individual development.

A Businessman With a Humanitarian Vision

Building successful enterprises in Nigeria’s competitive business environment requires vision, resilience and the ability to identify opportunities.

Through his activities as an oil and gas merchant and entrepreneur, Otti has demonstrated an interest in creating business value through Allied Victory Nigeria Limited.

His approach also reflects the possibility of combining commercial success with social responsibility. Rather than limiting his ambitions to business expansion, he has channelled resources into initiatives that address the needs of people within his community.

Private-sector contributions remain important in communities where developmental needs often exceed available public resources. Through investments in infrastructure, housing and social support, individuals and businesses can help address some of these gaps.

Otti’s interventions provide an example of how personal resources can be deployed to support community welfare alongside commercial activities.

Recognition for Service to Humanity

His contributions have earned him several honours and recognitions over the years.

Among the most recent is the prestigious The Sun Humanitarian Service Award, which recognises his contributions to humanity and commitment to improving the welfare of others.

While public recognition provides an opportunity to acknowledge philanthropic efforts, the impact of such interventions is also reflected in the experiences of beneficiaries and the communities they serve.

His traditional title of *Ikenga Umuchu* equally carries expectations of responsibility and service to his people. Through his community interventions, Otti has continued to demonstrate the importance of translating social recognition into practical contribution.

A Legacy Beyond Wealth

The story of Chief Abraham Ikechukwu Otti combines entrepreneurship with a commitment to humanitarian service.

From his business interests in the oil and gas industry to his interventions in housing, infrastructure, education and empowerment, he has demonstrated an approach to success that extends beyond personal prosperity.

The provision of furnished homes for 10 indigent widows and the installation of solar-powered street lights across parts of Achalla Village stand among the practical expressions of this commitment.

Ultimately, the measure of his contribution lies not only in his business accomplishments or the honours he has received, but also in the opportunities created and the lives touched through his interventions.

His journey reinforces the idea that while wealth may establish a person’s social standing, its impact on others can give it a deeper meaning.

World.title: NAFRC Commandant Gives Account of Stewardship, Inaugurates New Projects
World.content:
Victoria Ojiako

As he prepares to leave the Nigerian Armed Forces Resettlement Centre (NAFRC), Oshodi, Lagos as its commandant, to assume office as the Air Officer Commanding, Tactical Air Command, Air Vice Marshal Nnaemeka Ignatius Ilo, yesterday gave account of his stewardship as he also inaugurated the newly completed infrastructure projects and initiating another development project before handing over.

AVM Ilo inaugurated a 150-seater headquarters canteen, renovated classrooms and toilet facilities at the Command Children School, as well as street lighting installations, just as he also performed the groundbreaking for a new warehouse.

Reflecting on his tenure, the Air Vice Marshal said infrastructure renewal, personnel welfare and the provision of a conducive environment for training, administration and accommodation were among the priorities he identified on assumption of command.

He said the projects represented part of the deliberate efforts made to address infrastructure deficiencies and direct available resources towards facilities that would improve the centre’s operations and the well-being of its workforce.

According to him, the achievements were not the efforts of one individual but the result of the cooperation and commitment of officers, servicemen, servicewomen and civilian employees.

Ilo, who described the occasion as an opportunity to reflect on his time at the Centre, expressed appreciation to the Deputy Commandant, directors, deputy directors, commanding officers and heads of departments for their contributions to the actualisation of his vision.

He urged personnel to sustain the achievements by ensuring that the facilities were properly utilised and maintained, stressing that their benefits should extend beyond his tenure.

The Commandant also acknowledged President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his support under the Renewed Hope Agenda, as well as the contributions of the Minister of Defence, Chief of Defence Staff, Service Chiefs and Chief of Defence Intelligence.

A major highlight was the inauguration of the 150-seater headquarters canteen, conceived as one of the legacy projects of his administration.

Ilo performed the exercise on behalf of the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, who was initially scheduled to attend but was unable to do so because of service exigencies.

At the Command Children School, the administration’s intervention covered two classrooms and an abandoned toilet facility which the Commandant had identified during an inspection visit.

He subsequently directed its remodelling to modern standards and approved funds for the renovation. Street lighting installations were also unveiled.

The groundbreaking for the new warehouse marked the commencement of another project aimed at addressing the centre’s operational requirements.

Earlier, the Centre Maintenance Officer, Major U. Otagbo, said the projects reflected the outgoing Commandant’s commitment to addressing infrastructure gaps and improving the working and living conditions of personnel and their families.

He urged personnel to take collective responsibility for the facilities through proper use and regular maintenance.

The inauguration exercises provided an opportunity for Ilo to present some of the infrastructure milestones recorded under his leadership as he prepares to proceed to his next assignment.

World.title: Super Eagles Gun for Maximum Six Points against Tanzania’s Taifa Stars
World.content:
*Madagascar hold G’Bissau 1-1 to boost Nigeria’s chances in Group L

Duro Ikhazuagbe

Nigeria’s Super Eagles have been handed a lifeline ahead of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying clash with Taifa Stars of Tanzania in Uyo this evening.

Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau on six points were held 1-1 by Madagascar yesterday in neutral Morocco to narrow the gap at the top to just four points before Super Eagles take on Tanzania. A win today for Nigeria will reduce the gap to just one point ahead of Tuesday’s Match day 4 fixtures.

Another win for Super Eagles on Tuesday 17th November at the Amman Stadium in Zanzibar would have taken the pressure off Eric Chelle and his glory seeking stars.

Tanzania are assured of a place at AFCON 2027 as tournament co-hosts, with the other three sides battling for one qualification spot.

With the good news from Morocco, Super Eagles on three points now know they cannot afford any slip-up in the current international window if they are to keep their campaign on track for the 2027 AFCON to be jointly-hosted by Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

Coach Chelle knows that there cannot be a repeat of the lackluster that happened in their first game last September when Eagles had to come from behind to defeat Madagascar’s Barea at the same Uyo’s Godswill Akpabio Stadium. It is also unthinkable for Nigerian ball fans to be subjected to the kind of excruciating pains they suffered when Guinea-Bissau handed out a 3-0 whipping to Eagles away in Bissau.

Earning the maximum six points against Tanzania – in Uyo on Friday and in Zanzibar on Tuesday – would re-ignite high hopes of a place in the PAMOJA finals, depending on how Madagascar cope against Guinea Bissau’s Wild Dogs in their own quickfire-double.

Coach Chelle and Captain Wilfred Ndidi have reiterated the need for the three-time African champions to obliterate their loss to Guinea Bissau with a credible six-points grab against the Taifa Stars.

“We must work hard in these two matches and do everything to win. It is important to sustain the hope and all the players are in that mood to banish the memory of that defeat to Guinea Bissau and show their true quality.

“The spirit in camp is high and everyone is focused on achieving victory in both matches,” Chelle said.

Former junior international Benjamin Fredricks, Chibuike Nwaiwu and Abdullahi Ibrahim Bewene provide exciting options for Coach Chelle at the rear, while the presence of Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, Samson Tijani and Tochukwu Nnadi could mean a fresh-look midfield for the Super Eagles.

The Super Eagles will again be without ace forward Victor Osimhen, who sustained an injury in a Turkish league game with his club Galatasaray, days before Chelle unveiled his roster for the two matches.

In his absence, the Franco-Malian tactician will most likely rely on the combined strength of Atletico Madrid’s Ademola Lookman, Italy-based Akor Adams and Ajax Amsterdam of The Netherlands’ Tolu Arokodare, who has netted 13 goals across the Dutch League and the UEFA Conference League this season.

Veteran Moses Simon, who plays his club football in France like Tanzania’s most experienced and dreaded striker Mbwana Samatta, is one of the on-field marshals that Nigeria will look to for inspiration on Friday.

Simon Msuva, Selemani Mwalimu and Bernard Kamungo are the other aces that Taifa Stars’ Argentine Coach Miguel Ángel Gamondi will rely on to deliver at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium.

After Friday’s encounter, both teams will again square up to each other on Tuesday, 17th November at the Amman Stadium in Zanzibar, which is part of Tanzania.

World.title: Rivers to Host National Top 16 Table Tennis Championship
World.content:
The Nigeria Table Tennis Federation (NTTF) has announced that the National Top 16 Table Tennis Championship will take place in Ogu community in Ogu/Bolo local government area of Rivers State, from December 11-14, 2026, in a move aimed at expanding the sport’s popularity and developing talents in the South-South region.

The championship, which is being sponsored by the Fifika Chiri Foundation, according to the President of the NTTF, Dr Adesoji Tayo, would mark the beginning of a sustained effort to promote table tennis beyond its traditional stronghold in the South-West and establish the South-South as a major centre for the sport.

Tayo spoke during a visit to Ogu community, where he inspected facilities for the proposed competition and commended the President of Fifika Chiri Foundation, Alabo Boma Iyaye, for supporting the development of table tennis.

He described table tennis as a sport for everyone, irrespective of age, saying its benefits extended beyond competitive sports to recreation, physical fitness and healthy living.

“Table tennis is a game for all, and it is a game that can be played even till old age,” he said.

According to him, the sport could be played competitively, recreationally and as a means of livelihood, adding that it offered opportunities for young people to develop their talents and become internationally recognised athletes.

“Coming to Rivers State is not just to talk about competition; it is to talk about table tennis and how table tennis can help us to live a good daily life,” Tayo said.

The NTTF president expressed satisfaction with the facilities inspected in Ogu, describing the proposed venue as suitable for the championship.

“I’m happy that a beautiful edifice could be here. It’s good for the competition,” he said.

Tayo disclosed that the federation would facilitate the participation of the country’s top 16 male and female players, who would converge on Ogu to showcase their skills.

Speaking while hosting the NTTF president during a courtesy visit in Ogu, Alabo Boma Iyaye, who is also the Executive Director, Finance and Administration, Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC), said his passion for table tennis was rooted in his childhood experiences and longstanding involvement in sports.

“Growing up in Port Harcourt, we all played table tennis. You cannot grow up in Port Harcourt and not play table tennis,” he said.

Iyaye said he subsequently decided to revive interest in the sport in his community by organising a local Christmas table tennis competition, which later expanded to attract players from across Rivers State.

He said the competition, which had been sustained for several years, inspired him to seek a national-level event for Ogu.

“At the local level, we started, and then we transcended to the state level. We have state players that come in here every Christmas to play table tennis. But this year, I said, ‘Can’t we make it a national competition?'” he said.

The foundation president described the decision to bring the National Top 16 Championship to Ogu as a major achievement for the community and Rivers State.

“I want to specially thank you for accepting to come, not only to Rivers State, but to Ogu, to host the National Top 16. That is a major feat,” he said.

He assured the federation that the community would provide the necessary facilities and logistical support to ensure a successful competition.

According to him, Ogu has hotels, a good road network, a memorial hall suitable for indoor sports and reliable electricity supply through the Port Harcourt Electricity Distribution Company and solar power systems.

“We will do everything within our means to make sure that this competition is not only held in Ogu once, but will continuously hold in this part of the world,” Iyaye said.

He added that the initiative was not only intended to develop table tennis but also to place Ogu on the international sporting map.

Also speaking, the South-South representative on the NTTF board, Ama-ebi Ebikpolade, described the decision to host the competition in Rivers State as a significant development for the region.

He said the South-South had not hosted a major NTTF competition in a long time, despite Rivers State’s reputation as a sporting destination.

“For the first time, I think for the first time, a tournament of that level is coming to Rivers State,” Ebikpolade said.

He commended Iyaye for providing the support needed to bring the championship to Ogu, describing the development as the first step towards making the community an annual host of the competition.

“Today, we have started. We have taken the first step towards the annual hosting of the Nigerian National Top 16 in Ogu, courtesy of Alabo Boma Iyaye, and we cannot thank him enough,” he said

World.title: Ex-Sundowns star signs with agency as he steps into coaching
World.content:
Former Mamelodi Sundowns star midfielder Surprise Ralani has signed a contract with prominent sports agency ProSport International.

Ralani, who enjoyed a long playing career, ventured into coaching in November 2025, and he joined his home town club Gaza United.

Gaza United are competing in the ABC Motsepe League, and Ralani took up the role in order to gain coaching experienced.



Now, the aim with this new deal is to help Ralani move up the ladder in the coaching ranks, and perhaps in the Motsepe Foundation Championship or the Betway Premiership.

ProSport International took to their social media platforms on Thursday to announce the acquisition of Ralani as their client.

Ex-sundowns star signs new deal with prominent agency

Ralani’s playing career…

Ralani, 39, spent almost a decade in Europe playing for a number clubs between 2009 and 2017.

He then returned to South Africa to join Cape Town City in 2018 where he spent four years before moving to Sundowns in 2022.

Ralani would spend just over a season with the Brazilians as game proved hard to come by, and he joined Cape Town Spurs in 2023.

He was also on the books on the likes of Hungry Lions and Orbit College before retiring from professional football.

World.title: Where is John Steenhuisen?
World.content:
John Steenhuisen has kept a low profile after he was effectively demoted from his position as Minister of Agriculture during a cabinet reshuffle in June.

Just two months earlier, the politician – who made headlines for allegedly splurging his party credit card on Uber Eats orders – handed over the reins of the Democratic Alliance to current leader Geordin Hill-Lewis.

WHERE IS JOHN STEENHUISEN?

In June, John Steenhuisen was removed from his post as Minister of Agriculture and seemingly demoted to Deputy Minister of Trade and Industry by DA leader Geordin Hill-Lewis during a cabinet reshuffle.



In the months leading up to this, John had stepped down as president of the DA to focus his attention on agricultural issues, such as the rampant spread of foot-and-mouth disease.

He was replaced by Willie Aucamp as the new minister.

John Steenhuisen was sworn in to his new post on 1 July.

Since his move, John has gone completely silent on his social media platforms, prompting many South Africans to question where he is.

What happened to John Steenhuisen? 🤔 — Penuel The Black Pen (@penuelist_) November 11, 2026

However, he continues to perform his public duties.



In recent months, the 50-year-old has been active in various sectors within his department, including campaigning for local job creation in the automotive industry, encouraging European trade and investment and commenting on US-SA trade relations after SA’s exit from AGOA.

The Deputy Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, Mr John Steenhuisen, is in Pietermaritzburg today as a guest of KwaZulu-Natal Member of Executive Council (MEC) for @KZNPublicWorks Mr Martin Meyer for the launch of the province's Government Property Finder Portal. pic.twitter.com/jvZckjznBC — the dtic (@the_dtic) October 7, 2026

Africa's blue economy is not merely a future opportunity; it is a present investment opportunity. This was the message from Deputy Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, Mr John Steenhuisen, during his keynote address at #BlueInvestAfrica2026 in Cape Town today. pic.twitter.com/6oLIT6StSc — the dtic (@the_dtic) November 2, 2026

Deputy Minister of Trade, Industry and Competition, John Steenhuisen visited the Denel stand today at AAD where he was taken through our capabilities, projects and the people behind the work. pic.twitter.com/c3DI3xa36V — Denel (@DenelSOC) September 18, 2026

FALLOUT WITH DA STALWARTS

In recent months, John Steenhuisen is believed to have fallen out with former DA federal finance chair and environment minister Dion George, who was accused of misusing his party-issued credit card for personal expenses, including household and Uber Eats food delivery.

John – who accused the party of “betraying” him – was cleared of these allegations in an internal investigation.

He also accused ex-party leader Tony Leon of using his political connections to aid his PR company, Resolve Communications – a claim the latter denied.
