World.title: Baltic communal singing may no longer bring everyone together, study finds
World.content:
Communal singing across the Baltics may not be as inclusive today as its reputation suggests, with a new study finding some groups are increasingly left out of the experience.

The Integration Foundation presented the findings Wednesday from "Crises Established Singing: investigating the inherent potential of collective singing in times of social crises in the Scandinavian and Baltic regions" (CRIES), a research project involving cultural scholars from the Baltic states and Denmark.

The study examined how communal singing, long seen as a force for bringing people together, can also exclude certain groups.

Researchers found that growing numbers of people in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania do not identify with the idea of being a "singing people."

Those who do not speak the local language also take part in communal singing less often, as do unemployed and older people, who may lack the means or money to attend public gatherings and large events.

Generations of men's choir singers performing at the XXVIII Song Festival in Tallinn. July 6, 2025. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

In Estonia, choral singing is even losing ground in larger cities, where residents have more leisure activities to choose from.

Chances for 'not good' singers

"We're used to thinking that singing together includes everyone and that everyone in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania sings," said Rūta Muktupāvela, a lead researcher and professor at the Latvian Academy of Culture who led the study.

Each country, however, is also home to people who don't belong to its primary ethnic group and are less likely to take part in communal singing or song and dance festivals, she added.

Muktupāvela likewise noted that some people would like to take part but feel like they aren't good enough singers.

She said opportunities should be created for those who may not consider themselves talented enough but would still like to join in communal singing.

Choir singers of all ages and backgrounds at the XXVIII Song Festival in Tallinn. July 6, 2025. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

World.title: Estonian pilot: We keep our jets at least a kilometer from Russia's border
World.content:
Estonian pilots stay at least a kilometer from the Russian border, never flying east of Lake Peipus, one Air Force flyer told Maaleht.

In an interview with the weekly, Second Lieutenant Jasper Vimm, a 28-year-old captain, said no aircraft takes off without a planned route; pilots keep away from the border once airborne, and as GPS signals are liable to evaporate once you near Russia, flights are planned around ground landmarks.

Estonia's Air Force (Õhuvägi) is small compared with some other countries', but has four main aircraft: two Czech-made L-39 Albatros trainers leased from an Estonian firm, one of which is currently undergoing maintenance, and two Polish PZL M28 Skytruck transport aircraft used for maritime patrol and exercises.

The L-39s date from the 1980s and 1990s, fly at subsonic speeds of about 700 km/h, carry no weapons, cannot climb vertically, and have airframes with a service life of 5,000 flight hours, of which this one has a little over half left.

The Air Force currently has between 10 and active 20 pilots, Vimm said, though changes are afoot - the Estonian National Defence College will graduate its first class of pilots next year, after which new Air Force pilots will come through every year.

With its relatively compact size, flying from one end of Estonia to the other takes 30–40 minutes in a trainer; about half that in a larger fighter at cruising speed.

There have been proposals recently for Estonia to take on light fighters, what type is not yet known, but Vimm said once in country these would perform the same roles as the full-blown fast jets, differing mainly in size and speed.

He said new aircraft would be "a source of joy" for pilots, who would be able to do more in the air and practice using aircraft weapons using their own aircraft.

As for drones, Vimm said 'these are suited to destruction and reconnaissance and are replacing some missile roles, but pilots are not going anywhere for the time being: human-piloted planes perform a wider range of tasks and someone must still sit in the cockpit to achieve this.

While the disparity of state of the art fighters costing millions going out to intercept cheap drones, Vimm said the cost of human lives lost, infrastructure destroyed, far outweighs aircraft maintenance and the cost of air time; Ukraine has even mounted machine guns on slower, old piston-driven aircraft to hunt quadcopter-type drones, he noted.

The original Maaleht interview is here.

Since the Air Force, organizationally a part of the Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) currently has no fast jets, NATO allies provide that capability flying out of Ämari and from Šiauliai in Lithuania. Turkey's Air Force currently holds that role at Ämari with its F-16s.

World.title: ‘Inside Gaza’: Reporting a war when it hits home
World.content:
Los Angeles – How do journalists report on a war when they become victims of the violence, and when their proximity to the conflict is used to paint them as unreliable witnesses?

That’s the issue explored in “Inside Gaza,” a new documentary that follows journalists from global news agency AFP who were trapped in the territory as Israel exacted a fearsome revenge for Hamas’s October 7 attack.

Director Hélène Lam Trong brings these news industry veterans in front of the camera, showing how they balance the difficult task of reporting on the massive military response with their own survival, as it destroys their city, killing family, friends and colleagues.

“Most international correspondents… cover a war or a news event and then return home to safety,” freelance journalist and documentary filmmaker Lam Trong told AFP in Los Angeles, where the film was shown as part of The American French Film Festival.

“Palestinian journalists could not do that. They were trapped alongside the civilian population of Gaza, with no way out; as the days passed, they themselves became victims of the war.”

– Questioned –

The Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, killed more than 1,200 people, the vast majority of them civilians. Armed men also took more than 200 people hostage.

Israel almost immediately sealed the borders of the Gaza strip and barred international journalists from entering.

It then launched an enormous military response, pulverising swathes of Gaza in attacks that have left 73,000 people dead, according to the Hamas-run Gaza Health Ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Unable to send a team of reinforcements, AFP was solely dependent on the work of its local staff — experienced reporters, photographers and videojournalists, many of whom have worked internationally — to document Gaza’s subsequent descent into violence and despair.

Without journalists like these, whose work was transmitted to AFP’s thousands of media clients, the outside world would have had no idea what was happening inside Gaza, Lam Trong said.

In the film, which was compiled from material produced by the team on the ground, as well as from interviews conducted after they finally left, the journalists speak of the frustration of seeing their work either called into question or simply never broadcast or published.

In one sequence, the team describes their frustration at the way in which Israeli propagandists claimed genuine photos of a dead child were staged using a doll.

“At AFP, our photos, news reports and videos are used by world media outlets. But in this war, some of our images were never used,” says Gaza bureau chief Adel Zaanoun.

“It worried us, even terrified us, because from the very first days, the thousand of Palestinians killed didn’t count for the media.”

– The costs of reporting –

At a time of declining engagement for traditional journalism as audiences migrate to unmoderated social media platforms and politicians seek to demonize any outlet publishing stories they do not like, Lam Trong says it is vital the public understands how newsgathering works — including the costs and the risks to those who do it.

That includes becoming targets themselves. According to the Committee to Protect Journalists and Reporters Without Borders, approximately 200 journalists have died in Gaza since the war began.

AFP’s office in Gaza, which was broadcasting a live feed to clients, was hit, likely by Israeli tank fire, according to an investigation by the agency and other international media outlets.

“In Gaza, in particular, journalism and journalists have become central issues, as they have been killed, attacked and persecuted,” Lam Trong said.

“We do not deserve to be accused of propaganda when we conduct on-the-ground reporting,” she said.

Lam Trong, a recipient of the Albert Londres Prize — often described as the French equivalent of the Pulitzer — hopes the film, which has won numerous international awards and is eligible for Oscar contention, will spread the message of the importance of journalism.

The awards season campaign is “an opportunity to bring a very important message to Hollywood… that freedom of the press is under threat and that we must defend journalists — not just journalism, but the journalists themselves.”

AFP’s staff left Gaza in 2024. The agency continues its impartial coverage of the region using trusted freelance contributors.

World.title: Zidane says Italy defeat ‘part of the process’ for France
World.content:
Milan – Zinedine Zidane was unimpressed with his side’s defensive display after suffering his first defeat as France head coach against Italy on Thursday, but described the setback as “part of the process”.

Les Bleus took an early lead at San Siro through Michael Olise to put one foot in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, but were pegged back by a Francesco Pio Esposito double and Davide Frattesi strike.

Italy seized control of the game in the second half after the two sides went in level at the break following an opening period dominated by Zidane’s side.

Frattesi’s goal arrived three minutes after Sebastiano Esposito had missed a penalty, and France conceded a second spot kick, converted by the younger Esposito brother, to take the game beyond the visitors.

“We started well and we were good in possession, but in the second half we ran into difficulties, especially defensively,” Zidane told a press conference.

Asked if the team lacked courage, he replied: “No, quite the opposite. We stayed in the game, we did well in possession, especially in the first half, but in the second half we caved in a bit, especially after 2-1. It’s part of the process.”

France were twice denied by the woodwork and had 60 per cent possession and 18 attempts during an entertaining game as they slipped behind Italy into second place on head-to-head record in Group A1.

Zidane’s side host Turkey, who have failed to pick up a single point thus far, in their final game on Sunday, while Italy travel to Belgium, who are one point behind in third.

“The most important thing is creating chances,” Zidane added.

“Hitting the post had an impact, but I’m not disappointed. I would have been if we hadn’t created good possession. What we need to analyse is why we weren’t at the right level off the ball.”

– Mancini tips Esposito for record –

France were without star attackers Kylian Mbappe and Ousmane Dembele for the trip to Milan, but Zidane denied that their absence impacted the performance and revealed that Real Madrid striker Mbappe could return against Turkey.

“I think all the players were focused. As I said, we were a little less focused and less effective in the second half,” Zidane said.

“I hope (Mbappe) can play against Turkey. That is the plan, we decided not to risk him tonight because he had a little problem.”

Italy coach Roberto Mancini’s impressive start to his second spell continued as his side moved top and stretched their unbeaten run to four games.

Esposito’s double caught the attention as the Inter Milan striker took his international tally to nine goals in 14 games, and Mancini believes he could even eye the long-standing national record held by 1968 European champion Gigi Riva.

“Let’s hope he scores a lot more goals,” Mancini said.

“Gigi Riva has been up there on 35 for a lifetime. Let’s hope someone surpasses him. We need goals from Pio and the others too, but he can score a lot.”

Esposito could have had a hat-trick had his older brother not taken – and missed – Italy’s first penalty of the match during the second half, a moment Mancini revealed was not part of the plan.

“Pio is first choice and then Sebastiano. It was a family thing,” Mancini laughed.

str/mw

World.title: Klopp asks for time in Germany rebuild
World.content:
Berlin – Germany coach Jurgen Klopp on Thursday dismissed talk his squad lacked talent but asked for more time to improve the four-time world champions after poor results at major tournaments over the past decade.

Klopp took over from Julian Nagelsmann in the summer after Germany were knocked out by Paraguay at the last-32 stage of the World Cup.

It was Germany’s third straight early exit from the tournament, after group stage eliminations in 2018 and 2022.

Speaking in Belgrade ahead of Friday’s Nations League clash with Serbia, Klopp said he was confident in the talent at his disposal and said the players needed time together.

“It is very often said that German football is lacking in many areas — including the number of good players, great talents, world-class players, and so on,” said Klopp.

“But I have a super positive outlook on this team. To be honest, we have a very good mix.”

Klopp, 59, said he was not “naive or wide-eyed — we’re genuinely very good… we just need to make that visible, to translate it onto the pitch.”

The former Liverpool manager also asked for time when taking over at Anfield, saying he needed to turn everyone at the fallen English giants from “doubter to believer” to restore the club to their former glory.

“I have to allow myself the time,” Klopp said Thursday, but added: “if this suits the public, that’s not something I can control.

“We are on the right path — though we are, of course, still a long way from the end. The foundation, however, is genuinely good.”

Klopp praised Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz, who has been in better form in recent weeks.

“Flo (Wirtz) is in top condition. He can be an immense help to us,” Klopp said.

Wirtz has come under fire since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, but he has improved under new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola.

He has three assists in his past four Premier League games and scored his first league goal of the season in Sunday’s 3-1 win at Crystal Palace.

The former Bayer Leverkusen player is still just 23 but could play his 50th match for Germany on Monday in Berlin.

Wirtz felt the team was improving under Klopp and said he wanted to take on a greater leadership role in the young squad.

“I feel like we’ve gelled even better and solidified the things we’ve been working on in training. It comes down to bringing will, conviction, and passion onto the pitch,” Wirtz said Thursday.

World.title: US Congress steps up scrutiny of Trump, Nvidia after Huang exit
World.content:
Washington – Key US lawmakers on Thursday called for clarity on what the Trump administration knew about Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, after the AI chip giant announced his departure.

Huang, now Nvidia’s former CEO, had pushed for looser rules on sales of US chips to China — crucial in the AI race — and the controversy has reenergized advocates of a hard line on Beijing, days before Donald Trump travels to China.

“Despite Jensen Huang’s resignation, Congress must demand answers from Mr. Huang and others at Nvidia about how they may have put US national security at risk,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said on social media.

“The Trump administration must also answer for what it did once it learned about Mr. Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset,” he added.

Huang, a co-founder of the AI chip giant, on Sunday acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related.

US intelligence suspects her of working for Beijing, which has strongly denied the allegations.

– ‘Obvious threat’ –

According to The New York Times, Trump was informed of the suspicions last year, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed them to him in May.

Trump said on Monday he knew “the FBI is looking into” the affair, adding that he expected Huang to be “in good shape.” He said Huang had told him he did not know the woman was a spy.

Huang was ultimately brought down by the scandal on Thursday, when the company’s board announced his departure, effective immediately.

Lawmakers are also raising questions about Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s alleged reluctance to impose restrictions on exports of the chips to China.

Three Republican House committee chairmen had already said they wanted to hear from Huang behind closed doors on November 18.

Democrats, who will take control of both chambers of Congress in January after winning the midterm elections, have also said they intend to look more closely into the affair.

The top Democrats on the Senate Finance and House Ways and Means committees told Lutnick in a letter on Thursday that they were investigating the administration’s “scheme to approve and tax” Nvidia chip exports to Chinese firms linked to Beijing’s government and military.

They accuse Lutnick and Trump of ignoring the “obvious national security threat” posed by the ties between Huang and a suspected Chinese intelligence agent, even though they had reportedly been informed of them.

– Corruption –

Senate Republican leader John Thune told reporters on Thursday that a congressional investigation “would make sense” given the national security interests at stake.

Schumer, who will succeed Thune as the Senate’s most powerful lawmaker in January, demanded answers from the White House: “Were government officials told not to investigate because of Trump’s relationship with Mr. Huang? What did Trump know when he personally invited Mr. Huang aboard Air Force One?” for a state visit to China in May.

Beyond the national security questions, Democrats could also look for signs of corruption.

According to The Washington Post, Nvidia pledged $25 million toward the ballroom Trump is building at the White House, a few months after chip sales to China resumed. The company says the donation was unrelated to its business interests.

“The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump administration, Chinese spies and AI billionaires, the more I’m convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn’t corrupt,” Democratic Senator Chris Coons wrote on X last week.

“Congress will investigate and get answers.”

World.title: Pro-Palestinian group seeks ban on Israeli real-estate fair in Paris
World.content:
Paris – Pro-Palestinian activists have asked a French court to ban an Israeli real-estate fair in Paris which they say offers a bonus to prospective Jewish settlers in the occupied territories, sources told AFP on Thursday.

The Franco-Palestinian NIDAL association filed an emergency motion to a court against the 9th Icube real estate and investment salon, arguing that the fair violates human rights.

The event is to place on Sunday at the European Centre for Judaism in the French capital.

Other major cities have seen similar uproars over Israeli real estate fairs accused of marketing houses in the occupied territories. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned the 2026 edition of the Great Israeli Real Estate Event in Manhattan for that reason.

NIDAL asked the court to either order the head of Paris police force to ban the event outright or to ensure that the event does not sell property in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, whose occupation by Israel since 1967 is considered illegal under international law.

Before taking legal action, the group said they had sent a letter to the Paris police on November 5, which went unanswered.

In the filing, seen by AFP, the rights group argues that marketing Israeli settlements in the occupied territories contributes to the replacement of the Palestinian people through population transfer — a practice prohibited by international law and classified as a war crime under the French penal code.

In particular, the activists highlighted the presence of BH Nadlan, a company that markets apartments in both East Jerusalem and the West Bank on its website.

They also pointed to the fair’s official guide’s offer of a “significant” financial “bonus” for newcomers settling in “Judea and Samaria”, the Israeli term for the occupied West Bank.

World.title: AI industry weighs future without Nvidia’s Huang
World.content:
San Francisco – He had rock star status, and now the artificial intelligence industry is weighing who can fill the shoes of Jensen Huang after his forced exit from US chip king Nvidia left the “central bank of AI” without its longtime leader.

Huang’s abrupt fall comes at a sensitive time for the sector, just days before the closely watched IPO of AI firm Anthropic and amid mounting concerns about the financial soundness of the industry’s colossal investment spree.

Before his resignation on Thursday after details emerged about multiple extramarital affairs, including with a suspected Chinese spy, Huang had positioned himself as a major booster for the AI industry across both political and financial lines.

He had built close ties to Donald Trump, accompanying him on Air Force One earlier this year when the US president traveled to Beijing for a summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

And while other executives called for slowing down AI development over safety concerns, Huang pushed for plowing forward — perhaps not surprising from the head of a company that has poured billions into companies, data centers and chip deals from which it stands to profit.

Those efforts sparked questions about so-called circular dealmaking, highlighting the potentially fragile nature of Nvidia’s financing activities.

Among those deals was a more than $100 billion financing guarantee for a new data center in Ohio for ChatGPT-maker OpenAI.

Nvidia has also committed to buying $10 billion worth of shares in Anthropic’s IPO next week.

– Stable, or chaos? –

The chip designer’s growth appears solid for now, with TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo writing on X that the CEO transition would not affect Nvidia’s “product development and competitiveness” until 2028 at the earliest.

Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO on Thursday.

But expect “chaos,” warned Gary Marcus, a longtime tech industry critic, who wrote on Substack that “things will clearly never be the same, neither for Nvidia, nor the AI industry as a whole. Congressional investigations will continue. The market may crash.”

Huang persuaded Trump to allow sales of some of Nvidia’s high-end chips to China, despite the rivalry between the two countries and existing export controls.

Huang will now be absent when the US president meets Xi next week at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

In a note published Thursday, analyst Dan Ives called the whole saga a “black eye moment” for Huang.

However, the situation might “sharpen the sword in the battle and arms race” between the US and China, the note continued.

Huang’s resignation also presents an opportunity for the industry.

“Other US tech leaders are now going to have [to] step in,” Ives wrote, pointing to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Google CEO Sundar Pichai and Apple Chairman Tim Cook, among others.

– ‘Huge void’ –

Major Silicon Valley figures lamented Huang’s departure, crediting him with putting Nvidia at the center of the AI boom.

“A sad day for Nvidia, developers, America, and all humanity,” Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney wrote on X.

Sweeney said Huang had built one of the few companies to reach massive scale while continuing to innovate, while others “fell into the trap” of choosing profits over innovation.

Clement Delangue, CEO of AI platform Hugging Face, which is owned by Nvidia, called it “a really sad day,” saying: “This whole thing sucks, and I wish none of it had happened.”

Delangue vowed to “keep fighting for open-source AI, harder than ever.”

“Infidelity is obviously bad,” wrote Shaun Maguire, a partner at venture capital firm Sequoia Capital. “But his contributions to American innovation and AI leadership cannot be overstated.”

Maguire warned that Huang’s exit would leave “a huge void,” adding that “the American AI community needs to work double-time in an attempt to fill this void.”

Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, said in a video clip shared on X that it would be “an honor” to hire Huang.

World.title: Scaloni to stay on as Argentina coach until 2030 World Cup
World.content:
Buenos Aires – Lionel Scaloni on Thursday agreed to stay on as coach of Argentina’s national football team until after the 2030 World Cup, ending the doubts that had been swirling since this year’s World Cup final defeat.

Scaloni’s decision to renew his contract was announced by Argentine Football Association president Claudio Tapia at a press conference with the 48-year-old manager.

Scaloni, who took the Albiceleste to victory at the 2022 tournament in Qatar, told reporters he was as enthusiastic as “on day one”.

“A new project begins now,” he said a month after Lionel Messi, the team’s leading light for 20 years, bowed out of international football.

Tapia said that Scaloni would be the Argentina manager with the most World Cups under his belt by the time his contract ended.

Scaloni had cast doubt on his future with the team after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat by Spain in a bad-tempered July 19 World Cup final in New Jersey.

He has been coach for eight years, taking over in September 2018, after a traumatic World Cup in Russia, where Argentina were eliminated in the round of 16.

Scaloni took over one of the most prestigious jobs in football without any prior experience and built the team into one widely considered the best in Argentine history.

Besides the 2022 World Cup he coached Argentina to two Copa America titles, in 2021 and 2024.

He now faces the task of taking the team forward without his 39-year-old talisman Messi.

“What must remain is this team spirit, this feeling of unity among the players and the people,” he said after losing the final to Spain.

World.title: Trump calls for Apple’s Cook to replace Huang at Nvidia
World.content:
Washington – US President Donald Trump said Thursday that former Apple CEO Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia, after Huang quit over revelations of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

“Now that Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place — TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump said on his Truth Social network.

“A Legend replaces a Legend!”

Trump has no formal say in who should run chip giant Nvidia, which is at the center of the AI revolution, but his extraordinary intervention underscores his close ties to both Huang and Cook.

During his second presidency, Trump has treated Nvidia co-founder Huang as a close adviser, even bringing him on board Air Force One for a state visit to China in May.

After allegations emerged about Huang’s ties to Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, Trump this week defended the Nvidia boss and said he had no idea Alice Huang was allegedly spying for Beijing.

Trump added that Jensen Huang, who is not related to Alice Huang, was “suffering greatly” and described the Taiwanese-born tech boss as “an amazing guy.”

But Trump still faces questions over what he knew about the allegations — and when he knew.

The New York Times reported earlier this week that Trump was informed about the allegations by Secretary of State Marco Rubio aboard Air Force One in May — shortly before picking up Huang in Alaska for the flight to Beijing.

Cook — who stood down as Apple CEO in September but remains executive chair of its board of directors — is another of the tech titans who have swarmed around the White House since Trump’s return.

In August 2025, Cook appeared in the Oval Office with Trump to announce that Apple would increase its investments in the United States to $600 billion, as Trump threatened huge tariffs on tech products made abroad.

He also brought one of the flashy presents that Trump loves — a custom-engraved glass piece made by iPhone glassmaker Corning, set in a 24-karat gold base.

The gift helped smooth relations between Cook and Trump, who had repeatedly criticized Apple in the past for not manufacturing its iPhones in the United States.

Cook also accompanied Trump to China in May, and both he and Huang attended the lavish state banquet that the US president held at the White House for Xi in September.

World.title: Rs 81 lakh property of PoK terror handler seized in J&K's Rajouri
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir Police has attached immovable property worth Rs 81 lakh belonging to a Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK)-based terror handler in Rajouri district, officials told news agency ANI on Friday.

The attachment was carried out by Rajouri Police on Thursday under Sections 87 and 88 of the CrPC and Sections 2 and 3 of the EIMCO Act.

The property belongs to Mohd Arshad, a resident of Khablan Thanamandi, and comprises 2 Kanals and 14 Marlas of land spread across Khasra numbers 125, 128 and 160 in the village.

The action comes amid an intensified crackdown on terror networks in the region. As part of the drive this year, Jammu and Kashmir Police has attached properties worth crores of rupees belonging to 10 PoK-based terror handlers, aiming to dismantle the support network of terrorism and take action against those involved in anti-national activities.



In a separate operation, Baramulla Police and security forces arrested a man and recovered two hand grenades from the Baderkoot forest area of Tangmarg, police said on Thursday.

The accused was identified as Ghulam Jeelani Reshi, a resident of Baderkote in Tangmarg. The operation was conducted by Baramulla Police along with CICT Ftr BSF (112/06 Bn), 2RR and CRPF 176 Bn during an Area Domination Patrol (ADP) in the forest.

NEW DELHI: Seventy-five postgraduate medical candidates allotted seats across 72 institutes are facing uncertainty over their admissions after the institutions failed to complete mandatory reporting on the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) portal, prompting the regulator to reopen the Round 1 reporting window for one final day.In a notice issued on Thursday, MCC said the institutes had failed to complete admission reporting despite repeated emails and phone calls. It warned that any admission not submitted on the portal by the college authorities would be treated as "Null & Void". Candidates whose admissions remain unreported will be considered "Not Reported", and their seats will automatically become available for allotment in the next counselling round.Explaining the reasons behind the pendency, a senior health ministry official said the problem was a combination of errors in document uploads by candidates and delays in verification by institutes. Some candidates had uploaded unclear or illegible certificates, which were returned for correction, but the revised documents were not uploaded. Several institutes, meanwhile, failed to complete verification or resolve discrepancies in time.âSmaller DNB institutes, which often lack dedicated administrative staff, have faced particular difficulty with the online process. Document-upload errors by candidates and incomplete verification by institutes have left around 72 institutions affected out of a total of 1,600-1,700. We have given them a final one-day window to complete the process and expect the pending cases to be resolved by tomorrow, allowing candidates to be accommodated and Round 2 counselling to proceed,â official said.The official said that while medical colleges participating in MBBS counselling were familiar with online processes, several smaller DNB institutions lacked a structured administrative setup. In some cases, doctors involved in patient care were also handling document verification, while the work was assigned to clerical or data-entry staff.As a one-time measure, MCC will reopen the Round 1 reporting portal on November 13 from 9.30 am to 11 pm. Institutes that have not reported candidates have been directed to complete the admission process within the stipulated window. Candidates have also been asked to ensure that their online admission letters have been generated by the respective institutes.The list includes institutions such as Grant Medical College, Mumbai; ESIC Medical College and Hospital, Ahmedabad; Santosh Medical College, Ghaziabad; Mahatma Gandhi Medical College and Research Institute, Puducherry; Shroff Eye Centre, Delhi; Medanta Super Speciality Hospital, Indore; and Ranchi Institute of Neuro-Psychiatry and Allied Sciences.MCC has cautioned that any adverse consequences arising from non-compliance will be the sole responsibility of the institute or candidate.

World.title: Urine biomarker may offer new way to flag cancer risk in India, study suggests
World.content:
Representative AI image

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With an estimated 15.6 lakh new cancer cases and 8.7 lakh deaths in India in 2024, a new study points to a possible way of identifying people at higher risk of developing cancer even before symptoms appear: a urine biomarker.The research, published in Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention last week, found that the profile of certain molecules in urine could help predict the risk of developing multiple cancers over five years.The study followed healthy adults enrolled in the Lifelines population cohort in the Netherlands. Researchers analysed 24-hour urine samples from all 827 participants who developed cancer within five years and a random sample of 4,609 who did not. The results were scaled to estimate risk across a cohort of 1,24,436 adults.Researchers from Lund University, the University of Liverpool, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Elypta measured three chondroitin sulphate disaccharides in urine using mass spectrometry. They combined these measurements into a GAGome score and assessed its predictive value both independently and alongside 13 established risk factors.The five-year risk of developing cancer was 0.18% in the low-risk group, 2.3% in the intermediate-risk group, 7.6% in the high-risk group and 32% in the very-high-risk group. A one standard deviation increase in the score was associated with a 66% higher risk of cancer, even after accounting for established risk factors.The researchers estimated that screening people classified as high risk could identify 54% of cancers, including 54% of in-situ carcinomas, with a 17% false-positive rate.âThe association was independent of established risk factors and consistent across cancer stages, which makes this dynamic biological marker worth testing prospectively,â said John Field, professor of molecular oncology at the University of Liverpool and a co-author of the study.âUrinary GAG profiling offers a promising, non-invasive approach to identifying people at increased risk of multiple cancers. However, findings from the Dutch population cannot be directly extrapolated to India because of differences in genetic backgrounds, risk factors and cancer patterns. Large, multicentric studies in Indian populations are needed to establish its accuracy and cost-effectiveness. The test should be considered for wider screening only if it demonstrates improved early diagnosis and reduced cancer mortality,â said Dr Abhishek Shankar, associate professor of radiation oncology at AIIMS.The findings could pave the way for more personalised cancer risk assessment, but the urine biomarker is not a diagnostic test. Its accuracy and clinical usefulness will need to be established through further prospective studies, particularly in Indian populations, before it can be considered for wider screening.

NEW DELHI: From next Jan, smaller entrepreneurs, local firms and start-ups would be able to get licences under âRent a Cabâ scheme, as govt has proposed reducing the minimum fleet requirement for such operators to five vehicles from 50, with at least two cabs per place of location.The requirement for branches in five tourist cities is being removed, further lowering entry barriers for smaller entrepreneurs, local rental companies and start-ups. The draft Rent-a-Cab Scheme, 2026, also explicitly extends its coverage to vehicles rented with or without drivers, which will widen consumer choice. This means a person who hires a cab from a licenced operator for personal use can either drive it themselves or avail the service of a driver provided by the operator.The proposed scheme, which will replace the 1989 framework, introduces sweeping changes to licencing, safety, insurance and operational requirements.Operators will be able to obtain a single electronic licence, valid across the state or Union territory, for a uniform fee of Rs 25,000, replacing separate main and branch licences. Approved operating locations can include airports, railway stations and bus terminals.The ministry has proposed a 60-day timeline for grant and renewal of licences, which will remain valid for five years. Applications for adding or removing vehicles or operating locations will be deemed approved if authorities do not complete the process within 30 days. Electronic Vahan registers and automatic retrieval of vehicle data are also expected to reduce paperwork.The draft introduces a nine-year age limit for vehicles and mandates valid registration, fitness and pollution certificates, payment of motor vehicle taxes and comprehensive insurance covering occupants as per the vehicleâs passenger capacity. Vehicles must also be free of specified pending challans and unpaid toll dues and should not figure in the NCRBâs police crime database.For chauffeur-driven rentals, operators must provide drivers with valid licences and police-verified antecedents. The cabs must also have location-tracking devices, first-aid kits and optional child restraint systems. Operators must maintain websites, provide round-the-clock grievance support and arrange emergency repairs and towing when needed. Website-based complaints must be resolved within 24 hours, while inquiries into complaints against drivers must be completed within seven days.

World.title: Rs 10 lakh fine slapped on Ola for ‘tip to ride’ nudge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Central consumer protection authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of Rs 10 lakh on ANI Technologies, which operates ride-hailing platform

, for misleading consumers into paying an additional fare to improve their chances of getting a faster ride.

It has also directed the platform to immediately discontinue display of all prompts, messages, interface designs, pre-set amounts, or any other dark pattern elements that âsolicit, nudge, coerce or psychologically pressure consumers into paying any amount, whether described as a tip, add-on, additional fare or by any other name, over and above the upfront fare displayed at the time of booking, prior to the completion of the journeyâ.



The action follows a similar order and Rs 10 lakh penalty in Sep against ride-hailing platform Rapido for a similar violation. CCPA had also ordered Rapido to discontinue this practice. TOI has learnt that CCPA is also investigating similar complaints against another popular ride-hailing platform.

The penalty so far seems to have had little impact as such platforms are continuing the practice.

The authority took up a complaint it received in May 2025 alleging that Olaâs app was prompting customers to pay tips in advance out of fear that their bookings could be delayed or drivers might not accept their rides.





The app displayed the message, âadding a tip might help increase the chances of getting a ride fasterâ, along with pre-set tip amounts.

Ola had defended this, saying that it only offered customers an option to voluntarily reward drivers and the entire tip went to them. The company also argued that ride allocation and driver acceptance were determined by standardised algorithms that did not take tipping behaviour into account.

It maintained that customers had equal access to rides irrespective of whether they chose to pay an additional amount.

The company had also told the authority that it had modified the user interface, presenting the payment as an optional add-on. However, the CCPA observed that Ola had not provided technical evidence or backend documentation to substantiate its claim that tipping did not influence ride allocation.

The regulator said suggesting that an additional payment could improve the chances of securing a quicker ride could create a misleading impression among consumers and undermine the voluntary nature of tipping. It also said that consumers should not be made to feel that they need to pay over and above the disclosed fare to receive a basic service.

World.title: Indians top again: 9.3L get OECD citizenships in 5 years
World.content:
Indians continue to top the list of people acquiring citizenship in advanced economies, with around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquiring the nationality of an OECD member country between 2020 and 2024, according to the 'International Migration Outlook - 2026' report released on Thursday by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), reports Lubna Kably.

The figure marks a sharp increase of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh Indians who acquired citizenship of OECD member countries during 2015-2019. India remains the largest country of former nationality among those acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries, ahead of Syria and Mexico.

OECD countries took nearly 87L new citizens during 2020-2024

India remains ahead of Syria and Mexico. whose nationals accounted for around 5.9 lakh citizenships in OECD countries each during the five-year period 2020â2024.



Interestingly, while China was the sixth largest source country whose nationals acquired OECD member country citizenship, the numbers fell by nearly 12% to 3.4 lakh in 2020-24 as compared to the previous five-year period. OECD comprises 38 member countries â notably US, UK, European nations, Australia, Canada, Japan and South Korea.

According to additional data shared with TOI, during 2020-2024, OECD member countries embraced nearly 87 lakh new citizens â Indians constitute around 10% of its new citizens.





In the previous five-year period, nearly 65 lakh individuals acquired citizenship of an OECD member country â once again the composition of Indians was 10%.

OECD also shared year-on-year India-specific data with TOI, showing that 2.3 lakh Indians acquired citizenship of OECD member countries in 2024, mainly in Canada (87,320), US (48,820) and Australia (28,969). In 2023, the overall India-figure was marginally lower at nearly 2.2 lakh, with the same three countries accounting for most of the citizenship acquisitions.

The latest figures underline the growing permanence of Indian migration to advanced economies. While immigration flows measure the number of people moving to another country, citizenship acquisitions offer an indication of how many immigrants have progressed to acquiring the nationality of their destination country.

Indians also continued to move to OECD member countries for work and study, although the pace of migration slowed.

India remained the largest origin country of new migrants to OECD member countries in 2024. However, the number of Indian-origin migrants moving to OECD member countries fell by 19% in 2024, from 6.1 lakh in 2023 to 4.9 lakh in 2024.

âMigration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16% of employment across the OECD,â Mathias Cormann, OECD secretary-general said. âWith ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

That means helping migrants move into jobs where they can contribute most, and giving immigrant entrepreneurs better access to finance, networks and business support,â he added.

One in five STEM graduates across OECD member countries is foreign-born, and immigrants are over-represented among researchers and founders of innovative firms. Yet immigrants are also more likely to work in lower-productivity sectors, with their skills often underutilised, states OECD. The report finds that immigrantâs contribution to productivity depends on how effectively countries make use of their skills â many countries have expanded programmes to attract highly skilled workers.

The gap between Indian and Chinese students studying in OECD member countries narrowed, with 8.3 lakh Indian students and 8.5 lakh Chinese students studying in these countries.

World.title: Rajasthan SSR draft counts 11  lakh more voters than SIR list
World.content:
Rajasthan's draft voter roll shows 5.26 crore electors, leaving discrepancies across three official rolls.

Changes in Raj rolls can be sought till Jan

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

JAIPUR: Rajasthan's latest draft electoral roll, published Thursday under the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, has produced a fresh numbers puzzle. It records about 5.26 crore voters - about 11 lakh more than the 5.15 crore in the final Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll published in Feb.But the number is still far below another official figure in circulation: State Election Commission's final electoral roll, which stood at 5.45 crore voters in early Oct.That leaves Rajasthan with three voter counts in less than a year - 5.15 crore in the final SIR roll, 5.45 crore in the SEC roll, and now 5.26 crore in the ECI-linked SSR draft. The latest figure sits between the two, but does not settle the central question: why official rolls for the same state show such wide variation. According to Chief Electoral Officer Naveen Mahajan, the SSR draft has 2,75,24,780 male voters, 2,51,42,052 female voters and 584 transgender voters. The qualifying date for the revision is Jan 1, 2027. EC has opened claims and objections from Nov 12 to Dec 11. The final roll will be published on Jan 4, 2027.The difference between SIR and SSR is critical to understanding the numbers. SIR is a deeper verification exercise in which booth-level officers conduct house-to-house enumeration.Existing voters are given pre-filled forms and are required to submit them for their names to be considered in the revised roll.SSR begins with the last published final roll. Existing voters are generally carried forward and not required to prove eligibility afresh merely to retain their names. The exercise is meant to update the roll through additions, deletions and corrections.This difference in method explains why a draft SSR roll may not mirror a final SIR roll. But the wider problem is the coexistence of sharply different official numbers. The SSR draft is around 11 lakh higher than the final SIR roll, yet around 18 lakh lower than the SECâs early-Oct roll.The draft rolls have been shared with recognised political parties and uploaded on the CEO website. Voters can seek inclusion, deletion or correction through the prescribed forms before the final roll is frozen in January.Mahajan urged eligible citizens to verify their names in the draft roll and apply for inclusion if their names are missing. Those completing 18 years by Jan 1, 2027, can apply for enrolment. Young citizens turning 18 by Oct 1, 2027, can also submit advance applications.

World.title: Microsoft 365 outage drags on as company observes ‘limited recovery’
World.content:
Microsoft Outlook suffered a major outage across the world Thursday (November 12, 2026), with tens of thousands of users struggling to access their email as the company said it was working "aggressively" to reduce the impact.

The disruption, which Microsoft attributed to "elevated load" on its infrastructure, dragged on for much of the U.S. workday and also affected other company products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.

The disruption went global within a span of an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.

A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.

Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports "in the Americas," but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected "Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."

Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.

"We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company wrote on X.

"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.

"We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."

In the United States, around 130,000 users reported issues with Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time (1800 GMT), according to Downdetector.

Outage reports have since declined, with about 37,000 users reporting experiencing issues with Outlook as of 6 pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT).

Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.

As the outage dragged on for hours, Microsoft posted a series of updates on X, detailing continued but unsuccessful efforts to restore full service.

In one update shortly after 6 pm Eastern Time, Microsoft said it was "observing limited recovery" as it sought to route user traffic away from affected servers.

"As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect," the company added.

World.title: Four PRTS corridors proposed in Hyderabad; first phase to be completed within a year
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy directed officials to complete the tendering process for the proposed Personal Rapid Transit System (PRTS) in Hyderabad by December and ensure that the first phase of the project is completed within a year.

At a review meeting on the proposed PRTS on Thursday, the Chief Minister said the proposed network was aimed at improving connectivity between key government, commercial and public destinations in the city.

Proposed PRTS routes in Hyderabad

One corridor should connect LB Stadium with the Ranigunj bus station via the Ambedkar statue, Indira Park and Lower Tank Bund, he suggested. Another corridor should connect the Assembly Metro station with Ravindra Bharathi, the Secretariat and IMAX, extending further to Begumpet.

Mr. Revanth Reddy also proposed setting up a multi-level parking facility along Necklace Road, with a dedicated depot for PRTS services as part of the facility. In the western part of the city, he directed officials to immediately take up a PRTS corridor connecting KPHB Metro station with Durgam Cheruvu, Raheja Mindspace and Biodiversity Metro stations. A multi-level parking facility with a PRTS depot should also be established near IKEA at Gachibowli to facilitate operations on the proposed corridor.

World.title: Kolkata-Sairang train derailment: Preliminary probe points to faulty braking system
World.content:
A preliminary probe into the derailment of the Kolkata-Sairang Express at Digaru Railway Station in Assam on November 11 has pointed to a malfunctioning main braking system on the train.

A six-member probe team, in its report, found that the system primarily responsible for applying brakes in the coaches, technically known as the BP angle cock, was in an isolated condition in the locomotive.

"This may be the reason for this accident, as the brakes may not have been applied when the FP/BP angle cock of the loco was in an isolated condition," a joint note prepared by the probe team on the day of the accident said.

Assam train derailment updates

It further stated that the train crew applied the brakes, "but the brakes may not have been applied as the angle cock was previously in the closed position".

The probe report does not identify who rendered the braking system dysfunctional or whether the train crew overlooked safety procedures to check its functionality before operating the train.

However, in their statements, the train's crew members — the loco pilot, assistant loco pilot and guard — said that the braking system was functioning properly when they took charge of the train at Guwahati around 5.30 am on November 11.

According to the report, the train was stopped at Panbari (PNB) station at 6.16 am after the wheels of one of the coaches were found to have overheated due to jammed brake pads.

The crew attended to the problem, following which the train remained halted at the station for about 30 minutes.

When the train left PNB at 6.46 am and was approaching Digaru station, the station master concerned signalled it to enter the loop line and stop there to allow another train to pass first.

According to the report, the brakes failed to work when the crew applied them to stop the train. It overshot the red signal, hit a dead end, and came to a halt after derailing.

Some safety experts said the crew might have been using the alternative braking system available on the train, known as the regenerative braking system, to control its speed during the journey. They might have applied the main braking system while attempting to stop the train near the loop line, only to find that it was dysfunctional.

"Who isolated the main braking system? Did railway staff do it and forget to restore it later? Looking at the sequence of events, the possibility of involvement of some outsider is highly unlikely. The incident raises several questions and warrants a thorough probe," a safety expert said.

Advisories issued by some railway divisions after the incident suggest that railway staff might have closed the angle cock while attending to the jammed braking pad at PNB station and forgot to reopen it before the train resumed its journey.

World.content:
In a wide-ranging interview, German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck spoke to The Hindu about evolving European security architecture, the potential for growth in the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA), bilateral clean energy and defence initiatives and opportunities for skilled Indian workers in Germany.
