World.title: World leaders set out clashing priorities as COP31 turns to negotiations
World.content:
LIGHTS ON. A drone light show displays the COP31 logo during the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey, on November 11, 2026.

Developing countries reiterate requests that they have made during many years of UN talks for rich countries to provide more finance to help them shift to cleaner energy, adapt to a warming world, and repair climate-driven destruction

ANTALYA, Turkey – World leaders have set out competing positions and made clashing demands in two days of intense speech-making at the COP31 climate change talks in Turkey, leaving negotiators with a tough task to draft a meaningful deal that all can agree.

Small island states, among the most vulnerable in the world as global warming makes sea levels rise, pleaded for urgent cuts to greenhouse gas emissions.

European leaders, meanwhile, lined up behind a proposal to expand global electrification, developing countries asked for more finance from rich ones, and fossil fuel producers said oil, gas, and coal should continue to be used.

“We reaffirm our sovereign right to strengthen our energy and oil industry as a driver of our national development,” Venezuela’s acting President Delcy Rodriguez told the conference, after UN leaders had made the case for bringing to an end the age of fossil fuel.

Apart from trying to accommodate incompatible national positions aired on Wednesday, November 11 and Thursday, November 12, conference host Turkey and negotiations lead Australia also have the challenge of trying to make progress when wars and inflation have pushed climate concerns down the political agenda.

“It’s my job to steer consensus, not to bang tables and demand any particular action, but to steer consensus to the strongest, most ambitious possible outcome within the constraints of that consensus-driven process,” Chris Bowen, Australia’s COP31 president of negotiations, told Reuters.

Asked what a good deal might look like, he said: “I have many more hours of consultations with partners to do.”

Climate activists say short-term political concerns should not get in the way of addressing an issue that will get more pressing if ignored.

A UN report last month found the world was already on course to break through the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) warming limit that countries had agreed to pursue under the 2015 Paris Agreement to prevent the worst effects of climate change.

“The situation could not be less under control. The planet is not dying. It is being killed,” Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg said on the sidelines of the UN conference.

“It is being killed by the very same people often thought to come to our rescue. No one is coming to our rescue.”

Britain’s Burnham backs renewables

Earlier on Thursday, the leaders of small island states including the Bahamas, Tuvalu, the Solomon Islands and Saint Lucia called for swift action.

“Major emitters must move beyond the usual promises. They must reduce emissions that the climate crisis demands,” said Saint Lucia’s Prime Minister Philip J. Pierre.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham backed a proposal by Turkey to increase electricity’s share of world energy consumption to 35% by 2035, from a little over a fifth now, to help advance that goal. Turkey has not specified whether the extra energy used would be renewable.

Burnham told the conference that energy supply disruptions from the US-Israeli war with Iran and Russia’s war with Ukraine showed clean energy was the wise choice.

“It is now plain for everyone to see that if we depend on energy we do not control, then we leave ourselves exposed to prices we cannot control,” he said. “The shift to clean energy is the only route to energy security.”

Developing countries reiterated requests that they have made during many years of UN talks for rich countries to provide more finance to help them shift to cleaner energy, adapt to a warming world, and repair climate-driven destruction.

Fernanda de Carvalho, the head of climate policy for the World Wildlife Fund environmental group, said he found the leaders’ speeches underwhelming, especially as COP31 is the first UN conference since scientists have publicly said the world is set to breach the 1.5C threshold.

“It is worrying that the climate issue is not as high on the global political agenda as it needs to be,” he said. – Rappler.com

World.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down in big blow to AI boom
World.content:
The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang's push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down, leaving the AI industry without its biggest champion and clouding the future of the chipmaker he built into an AI powerhouse.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday, November 12. It named former Synopsys CEO and board member Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chairman.

Play Video

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and is its fourth-largest investor with a stake of about 3.61%, will exit the board as well.

Nvidia shares fell more than 10% in premarket trading, and weighed on the broader market.

Pressure had been mounting on Huang in recent days after reports said the 63-year-old, who is married, had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.

Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday, November 11, to consider his ouster, a person familiar with the matter said, after reports earlier in the day that Huang also had an extramarital affair with a senior company executive who reported to him.

Huang’s exit plunges the $4 trillion company into uncertainty and threatens to disrupt an AI ecosystem that he helped bankroll by pouring Nvidia’s swelling cash pile back into cloud providers, suppliers and the industry’s biggest labs.

“The risk is not that Nvidia suddenly loses its technology roadmap…that roadmap is largely visible for the next several years. The risk is execution. Jensen has been the chief conductor of an extraordinarily complex system,” said Michael Feldman, portfolio manager at ClearBridge Investments.

“In a world with real bottlenecks, that coordination is a competitive advantage in itself.”

Investor sentiment toward AI stocks has already been shaky as soaring cash burn and rising debt at traditionally cash-rich tech giants fuel doubts over whether the AI boom will pay off.

The departure could also have far-reaching consequences for US chip export policy, given Huang’s push to preserve access to the Chinese market and his close ties with US President Donald Trump.

Trump said on Sunday, November 8, that Huang had “done an amazing job for our country” and that the Nvidia chief had told him he had no idea the Chinese woman he had an affair with was a spy.

Huang’s rock-star status

For years, Nvidia was best known to gamers chasing top-tier graphics. But its chips’ ability to perform many calculations at once has made them the oil of the AI boom and a strategic prize in the US-China race to dominate the technology. It also made Nvidia the world’s most valuable company.

That turned Huang into a rock-star CEO, mobbed by fans in Taiwan and South Korea who ask him to sign books, posters and sometimes even their bodies. Such is his pull that stocks moved at his mere mention of company names at events.

But scrutiny of his conduct has intensified in recent days after reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud company Megaspeed, who US authorities have concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

The two, who have been photographed together in Taiwan, Singapore and California, are not related.

Washington has also investigated Megaspeed, a coveted official Nvidia cloud partner with priority access to its chips, over suspicions it helped China obtain advanced AI chips restricted under US export controls, according to media reports. Beijing has denied Alice Huang is a spy.

Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched a probe, led by independent directors with outside legal counsel, into whether Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. It also expressed confidence in him at the time.

The controversy escalated on Wednesday when the New York Times reported Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported to him. – Rappler.com

World.title: Trump visit stirs Zambales fishers’ fears over US military presence
World.content:
Fisherfolk from Zambales join a consultation opposing the proposed US ammunition factory in Subic Bay and the planned visit of US President Donald Trump ahead of the ASEAN Summit (Photo courtesy of Pamalakaya)

Fisherfolk in Zambales province have reiterated their opposition to the proposed construction of a United States (US) ammunition factory in Subic Bay, warning that the project could pave the way for the return of a US military presence in the area.

Fisherfolk group Pamalakaya said in a statement on Friday that local fisherfolk associations joined in calling for US President Donald Trump to stay away during a consultation this week, ahead of his visit to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit that begins on Monday (November 16).

The group said Trump’s visit would reinforce what they described as unequal military and economic agreements that do not serve the interests and welfare of marginalized communities.

Article continues after this 

READ: Zambales fishers oppose plan for US ammo factory in Subic

“The Filipino fisherfolk are among the many sectors that will not give a warm welcome to US President Trump. We do not need his investments and unequal agreements that will expose our land and natural resources to foreign plunderers,” said Roselyn Regalado, president of the Cabangaan 3 Fishermen’s Unity Association.

“We strongly reject the proposed ammo factory in Subic Bay. This is tantamount to the restoration of the US base that we once ejected,” she added.

Pamalakaya said that while fisherfolk continue to face threats from China in the West Philippine Sea (WPS), US military intervention was also unacceptable, warning that it could further heighten tensions rather than ease them.

US forces stepped up their presence in the WPS through joint maritime patrols and cooperative activities with Philippine forces.

Article continues after this 

Many fishermen from Zambales continue to report harassment by Chinese vessels near Bajo de Masinloc, or Scarborough Shoal, where tensions have persisted despite the 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated China’s sweeping maritime claims.

The ruling affirmed the Philippines’ sovereign rights over its exclusive economic zone and found no legal basis for China’s claim to historic rights within the so-called nine-dash line.

Article continues after this 

READ: US gun maker BADI weighs Subic, Cavite for PH plant

However, Chinese Coast Guard vessels have continued to operate around the shoal, where Filipino fishermen have reported being driven away from traditional fishing grounds and encountering restrictions on their access to the area.

The group urged Filipinos to oppose the proposed US military installation in Subic Bay, which is intended for the manufacture of so-called forward-staged ammunition for the Indo-Pacific region.

Meanwhile, fisherfolk groups in Batangas also staged protests against US-backed economic and military initiatives.

In Balayan Bay and Nasugbu Bay, members of Pamalakaya-Timog Katagalugan and the Haligi ng Batanguenong Anakdagat (HABAGAT) set afloat a raft bearing their opposition to the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) and the Pax Silica initiative.

World.title: Marina suspends safety permit of vessel grounded in Surigao City
World.content:
GROUNDED VESSEL The passenger vessel MV Georgia 1 sits in shallow waters off the Port of Surigao in Surigao City after running aground early Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026. (Photo courtesy of MARINA)

BUTUAN CITY — The Maritime Industry Authority (Marina) has immediately suspended the Passenger Ship Safety Certificate (PSSC) of MV Georgia 1 after the vessel ran aground at the Port of Surigao in Surigao City early Thursday.

In a statement, Marina said the suspension was done in keeping with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon’s directive to ensure safe and reliable sea transport services.

Operated by San Ricardo Shipping Lines Corp., MV Georgia 1 departed from San Ricardo, Southern Leyte, and arrived at the Port of Surigao around 4 a.m. on Thursday.

Article continues after this 

READ: Tanker runs aground in Surigao del Norte waters; gas odor detected

According to Marina’s initial report, the vessel encountered sudden gusts of wind and strong sea currents during low tide while maneuvering to dock, pushing it toward shallow waters where it ran aground.

Marina Officer-in-Charge Administrator Loumer Bernabe stressed that passenger safety must never be compromised to maintain shipping operations.

“No vessel should be allowed to continue operating until its seaworthiness is assured,” Bernabe said in Filipino.

Marina said an underwater inspection is underway to assess the condition of the ship’s hull, while the shipping company has been ordered to submit a notarized Marine Protest.

The vessel’s PSSC will remain suspended until Marina completes its inspection and evaluation, confirming that the ship is safe to sail again./coa

World.title: NCRPO warns protesters anew: No rallies outside freedom parks
World.content:
Artists from Tambisan sa Sining and Surian ng Sining work on an effigy titled “Puppet and the Puppet Master” during a workshop ahead of protests coinciding with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s fifth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on July 27. (File photo from NIÑO JESUS ORBETA / Inquirer)

MANILA, Philippines — The National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) warned that police would arrest or take legal action against persons who will hold demonstrations outside the designated freedom parks.

This warning is in effect during the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) Summit that will happen from Nov. 15 to 17.

Several groups previously announced that they would stage rallies before, during and after the regional high-stakes gathering, where foreign delegates and leaders, including United States Donald Trump, will attend.

Article continues after this 

NCRPO Officer-in-Charge Brig. Gen. Christopher Abrahano on Friday said that he directed police commanders to strictly enforce security restrictions around the main venue in Pasay City.

Also under heavy security are hotels and other major summit routes.

Abrahano further reminded protesters to confine their assemblies within the freedom parks in Metro Manila.

READ: PNP to take action vs disruptive Asean Summit rallyists

“Respecting the people’s right to peaceful assembly does not mean allowing demonstrations in areas where they are prohibited under lawful security arrangements,” the Metro Manila police chief stressed in a statement.

Article continues after this 

“We will not compromise the security of the summit, our foreign delegates, and the general public,” he added.

The Philippine National Police (PNP) earlier issued a warning to individuals who may cause public disruptions or harm to an individual, especially to a foreign visitor.

Article continues after this 

Abrahano cited that under Batas Pambansa Blg. 880, or the Public Assembly Act of 1985, particularly Section 4, assemblies held in public spaces requires a permit from the local government.

The exemption is in duly established freedom parks and other specified locations.

He further asserted that the police would not hesitate to take action against violators.

“Our instructions are clear: Maintain peace and order, protect the security of the summit, and respect the constitutional rights of our people,” he emphasized. “We will enforce the law firmly but professionally. Peaceful assembly is a right, but it must be exercised within the bounds of the law,” he noted.

A ‘Trump-out’ protest is being held at several areas in Quezon City and Manila City on Friday, ahead of the expected visit of the US president in the country.

According to the PNP, more than 19,000 police officers and 3,075 personnel from other agencies were deployed to enforce security measures as the country hosts the 49th Asean summit on Nov. 15 to 17.

World.title: Oriental Mindoro inflation surges to 9.3% in October
World.content:
Headline inflation in Oriental Mindoro accelerated to 9.3 percent in October from 7.7 percent in September, according to official government data released on November 10, 2026. NQUIRER FILE PHOTO

CALAPAN CITY — Headline inflation in Oriental Mindoro accelerated to 9.3 percent in October from 7.7 percent in September, according to official government data released on November 10.

The sharp increase brought the province’s average inflation rate from January to October to 6.1 percent, up from 1.8 percent in October last year.

Data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) showed the provincial rate surpassed both the national inflation rate of 7.8 percent and the Mimaropa regional average of 6.7 percent for the same month.

Article continues after this 

READ: Inflation jumps to three-year high of 7.8% in October

Charlyn Romero-Cantos, chief statistical specialist of the PSA Provincial Statistical Office in Oriental Mindoro, said the primary driver of the upward price momentum was the faster annual increase in housing, water, electricity, gas, and other fuels, which spiked to 20.7 percent in October from 14.8 percent in September.

Transport costs also rose substantially, to 18.1 percent from 13.3 percent in the previous month.

The PSA identified the top five contributors to the province’s overall inflation index as rentals, which registered at 19.7 percent; rice at 23.7 percent; gasoline at 51 percent; shell or nut charcoal at 62.8 percent; and wood and bamboo charcoal at 54.4 percent.

Price hikes were likewise reported across other commodity groups, including health (5.6 percent), recreation, sport, and culture (6.8 percent), restaurants and accommodation services (8.4 percent), and personal care and miscellaneous goods (2.3 percent).

Article continues after this 

The economic burden was heavier for vulnerable sectors, as inflation for the bottom 30 percent of income households rose to 10.6 percent in October from 10.1 percent in September.

The higher inflation rate among low-income households was largely attributed to steep increases in transport costs, which climbed to 19.6 percent from 14.1 percent, and housing and utilities, which rose to 21.7 percent from 20.7 percent. /coa

World.title: Eating out, commuting get pricier in Baguio, Cordillera in October
World.content:
Dining out and commuting by public transportation were a bit pricey in October, as shown by inflation rates of 9.3 percent in Baguio City and 9.2 percent in the Cordillera region.

BAGUIO CITY — Dining out and commuting by public transportation were a bit pricey in October, as shown by inflation rates of 9.3 percent in Baguio City and 9.2 percent in the Cordillera region.

The October inflation was the highest rate yet this year for the mountain resort city and the highland provinces of Ifugao, Abra, Apayao, Benguet, Mountain Province, and Kalinga, and its component Tabuk City, said Aldrin Federico Bahit Jr., chief statistician of the Philippine Statistics Authority for the Cordillera, during a briefing on Thursday.

With the 1.9 percent inflation rate at the start of the year, Cordillera commodity prices became so expensive that inflation initially peaked at 7.6 percent in April, he said. But Cordillera inflation followed a sustained upward trajectory, climbing to 8.3 percent in September and 9.2 percent last month.

Article continues after this 

READ: Inflation jumps to three-year high of 7.8% in October

Inflation in the summer capital followed a similar trend, from 4 percent in January to 7.8 percent in September before high prices pushed it to 9.3 percent last month.

A weakened peso in October, when the exchange rate traded at P63-64 per US dollar, and global uncertainties over the protracted war in Iran have directly impacted the Cordillera, Bahit said.

Philippine transactions are dollar-based, so when the peso depreciates, commodities purchased abroad, like gasoline, become expensive, as does the domestic supply chain when truckers deliver Benguet vegetables to Manila and contend with high fuel costs. “The compounding effect of high-priced gas and a depreciating peso on Cordillera households is high,” Bahit said.

Food like rice remained a major contributor to upland inflation, with the inflation rate at 20.2 percent in October, up from “an already double-digit rate” of 18.2 percent in September, he said.

Article continues after this 

Restaurants and cafes with full service helped accelerate October inflation, with an 11.4 percent rate last month, which was up from the 10.2 percent rate recorded in September, Bahit said. Utility expenses, rent and LPG prices also helped jack up Cordillera inflation.

READ: Fuel prices drive highest Philippine inflation in years

Article continues after this 

But last month’s decision to raise passenger fees for jeepneys (a provisional hike from P13 to P15) and taxicabs (a flagdown rate of P65 from the original P50) in Baguio and public utility vehicles like tricycles in Abra or Mountain Province reflected a “second round of risk” confronting families, Bahit said.

Gasoline sold in the Cordillera posted an inflation rate of 48.4 percent in October from 41 percent in September.

The Strong El Niño would worsen inflation because of its effect on food supplies like rice, Bahit pointed out. The prolonged dry spell came at a time when regions like the Cordillera are affected by the Middle East war and the closure of the trade route through the Strait of Hormuz, he said.

The outlook has not dampened travel to the highlands. Drawing an average of 250,000 to 300,000 visitors every December, which is the start of Baguio’s peak tourist season, the city “remains a favorite destination during Christmas despite any crisis,” said Aloysius Mapalo, Baguio tourism operations officer. World.title: Prosec: Duterte’s camp in panic, still no answer to ill-gotten wealth allegations
World.content:
Manila Rep. Joel Chua (right) and Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong (Photos from House of Representatives, Inquirer files)

MANILA, Philippines — Despite Vice President Sara Duterte’s lawyers’ presentation of six witnesses to the impeachment trial in four days, the prosecution panel believes that the allegations raised under Article II have not been disputed.

The group believes this situation is causing panic in the ranks of the defense team. Article II pertains to the alleged unexplained wealth and reported violations in the Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth.

Prosecution spokesperson and Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said in a press briefing on Thursday that the defense panel’s decision to withdraw the presentation of several witnesses may be a sign of a change in strategy by the defense team.

Article continues after this 

He observes that there are no strong point countering the case against Duterte that has been made.

During the 43rd day of Duterte’s trial, the defense manifested that they will no longer be calling many witnesses, including Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) senior vice president and lawyer Paul Roderick Ysmael.

“It only manifests how the defense is now panicking. They’re trying to re-strategize again their initial, probably initial attempt to attack the case of the prosecution,” Adiong said in a press briefing.

“It has already been proven, based on the testimonies of their previous witnesses, that they were not able to accomplish the purpose of their presentation in the first place,” he noted.

“Because first, there is the question of competency […]. Many of them are not sure, do not know the answer, when confronted with hard questions,” the lawmaker noticed.

Article continues after this 

Adiong was referring to witnesses who have earned the ire of some senator-judges for allegedly being evasive and lying when confronted by the prosecution during cross examination.

Of the first three witnesses that Duterte’s lawyers presented from Monday to Tuesday, two were called out — Davao City Assessor Engr. Jaime Adalin and Davao City Accountant Vingelin Bajan.

Article continues after this 

Adalin and Bajan both failed to remember things when the prosecution tried to question their credibility.

Adalin was presented to prove that the property owned by Duterte’s husband, lawyer Manases Carpio, was declared in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN) as a residential lot in Davao’s Barangay 74-A.

According to Adalin, the 379-square-meter parcel of land in Davao City’s Matina Crossing under Carpio’s name was the same property listed by Duterte.

READ: Davao land assessor: Carpio’s Matina property listed in Duterte’s SALN

Adalin was confronted with a recent trip to China, as the prosecution was trying to establish that he is not a credible witness.

But when asked about the trip which happened in 2025, the city assessor said he could not remember details of it.

Bajan, on the other hand, also used the same answers that Adalin gave — that she does not know or does not recall signing documents.

The witness gave these responses when she was confronted with an Articles of Partnership of accounting firm Ampil, Elises, Ciudadano & Co. CPAs bearing her name.

According to counsel for prosecution Mae Divinagracia, the accounting firm was responsible for auditing companies linked to Duterte, like Gencorp Industries Inc.

READ: Davao accountant was partner at firm that audited VP-linked companies

Bajan was presented by the defense to prove that the money received by Duterte from Davao City in 2023 was for a late payment based on adjusted salaries.

Adiong also pointed out that the testimony of Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay, the corporate counsel for Gencorp and Metro City Chow Foods Corp., seemed to even favor the prosecution.

Punay admitted that Duterte received P2.14 million from Gencorp between 2022 and 2025, describing it as a “return of capital” on a “loose investment” in a Jollibee branch in Davao City.

However, when confronted by the prosecution, the witness could not produce written records establishing the amount or terms of Duterte’s original investment or explain the basis for the payments.

This lack of papers prompted senator-judges to question whether the money represented repayment of capital or actual profit.

Punay also admitted, upon questioning from Presiding Officer Francis Escudero, that she had questions about the company’s payments to Duterte.

READ: Witness admits questioning GenCorp payments to VP Duterte

Adiong said it is unclear how the Duterte camp will dispute the prosecution’s allegations with the answer of these witnesses, coupled with the withdrawal of bank officials’ presentation.

“Many of the managers of the banks (where Duterte and Carpio) have active corporate and individual accounts […] have already testified,” the lawmaker noticed.

“We have already presented them and they actually confirmed that there have been remaining balances in all of these accounts that actually were not part of the declaration of the vice president in her SALN,” he said.

“So that would be an indisputable fact because the bank managers themselves have testified on those bank accounts that bore certain amounts,” he added.

Aside from Adiong, public prosecutor and Manila Rep. Joel Chua also accused Duterte’s lawyers of setting up a defense that seems to be more of a drama.

Chua sees that the defense team is sticking to rhetoric, instead of addressing pressing issues.

The legislator said the two defense witnesses who testified before the Senate Impeachment Court on Thursday were geared for the social media content of Duterte’s team.

Chua said the witnesses were not presented to dispute the report of financial forensic expert Atty. Alexander Cabrera.

READ: Chua: Duterte camp’s ‘K-drama’ defense only plays on public sympathy

Cabrera testified last October 9 as a witness for the prosecution, saying that the vice president has not declared P817 million worth of assets in her SALN from 2022 to 2025.

If it were up to him, Chua said he would have tackled the supposedly more glaring issues raised by the prosecution.

These matters include the testimony from Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura, who disclosed that Duterte and Carpio had P4.4 billion worth of flagged transactions.

World.title: BFAR warns vs eating shellfish from 4 Eastern Visayas bays due to red tide
World.content:
(File Photo by Joey A. Gabieta)

TACLOBAN CITY — The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) warned the public against gathering, selling and consuming shellfish from four coastal areas in Eastern Visayas.

The alert comes after laboratory tests detected paralytic shellfish toxins associated with red tide.

In its advisory dated Nov. 12, BFAR-8 identified Carigara Bay, Irong-Irong Bay, Matarinao Bay and Cambatutay Bay as areas where shellfish samples tested positive for red tide toxins.

Article continues after this 

Carigara Bay spans across the coasts of Babatngon, San Miguel, Capoocan, Barugo and Carigara towns in Leyte and Irong-Irong Bay in Catbalogan City, Samar.

Matarinao Bay includes the coasts of General MacArthur, Quinapondan, Hernani and Salcedo towns in Eastern Samar.

Cambatutay Bay covers the coasts of Tarangnan town, Samar.

The examinations of shellfish samples were conducted by the BFAR-8 Regional Fisheries Laboratory.

BFAR said it had issued a local red tide warning for Cambatutay Bay while awaiting confirmatory test results from the BFAR National Fisheries Laboratory Division using the Receptor Binding Assay.

Article continues after this 

The public has been advised to avoid gathering, selling and eating all types of shellfish, including Acetes species or alamang, from the affected waters.

However, BFAR clarified that fish, squid, shrimp and crabs from these sites remain safe to eat, provided they are fresh and their internal organs, particularly the intestines and gills, are removed before thorough washing.

Article continues after this 

Red tide is caused by the rapid multiplication of certain microscopic algae that can produce toxins harmful to humans and marine organisms.

Shellfish can accumulate these toxins as they feed by filtering seawater.

Saxitoxin causes paralytic shellfish poisoning, which can lead to numbness, tingling, difficulty breathing, and, in severe cases, death.

Cooking or boiling contaminated shellfish does not destroy the toxin.
